children.title: Regularized Empirical Risk Minimization Architecture
children.top_down_role: Common formulation components and parameterizations that precede individual regularizer families.

children.title: Data-Fit Families
children.top_down_role: Loss-side families that determine smoothness, robustness, and response-model geometry.

children.title: Quadratic Data Fit
children.top_down_role: Least-squares learning and inverse-problem fidelity models.

assumptions_latex: The design matrix is \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), the response is \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and the parameter is \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
The regularizer \(R:\mathbb{R}^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex, and \(\lambda\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting objective is a convex regularized least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear least-squares fidelity with convex regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quadratic data-fit function is \(L(\beta)=\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2\). A regularized learning or inverse-problem estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda R(\beta)\right\}.\] The loss is convex and differentiable, with gradient \(\nabla L(\beta)=n^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}(X\beta-y)\) and Hessian \(\nabla^2L(\beta)=n^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}X\). It is strictly convex exactly when \(X\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic data fit minimizes squared residuals, optionally combined with a convex penalty; its curvature is determined by the design Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Data Fit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, derivatives, strict-convexity condition, and content kind are mathematically appropriate, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Generalized Linear Model Losses
children.top_down_role: Regularized likelihood families for categorical, count, and related responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Linear Model Losses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical generalized linear models with fixed dispersion and convex regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R\) be the natural-parameter domain of \(b\), and let \(\mathcal B=\{\beta\in\mathbb R^p:x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta\in\mathcal D\text{ for all }i\}\). After dropping terms independent of \(\beta\) and suppressing any fixed positive dispersion factor, the empirical negative log-likelihood is \[L(\beta)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(b(x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta)-y_i x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta\bigr),\qquad \beta\in\mathcal B.\] Regularized fitting minimizes \(L(\beta)+\lambda R(\beta)\) over \(\mathcal B\). Bernoulli logistic regression has \(b(\eta)=\log(1+e^\eta)\), and Poisson regression has \(b(\eta)=e^\eta\). Because \(b\) is convex and each predictor is affine in \(\beta\), both \(L\) and the regularized objective are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a canonical generalized linear model with fixed dispersion, the negative log-likelihood is a convex sum of log-partition terms minus response–predictor products; adding a convex regularizer preserves convexity.
assumptions_latex: Conditionally on \(x_i\), the response has a canonical exponential-family model with natural parameter \(\eta_i=x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta\), convex log-partition function \(b\), and a fixed positive dispersion factor.
The function \(R:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex, and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The negative log-likelihood and its sum with \(\lambda R\) are convex on \(\mathcal B\).

notation.meaning: Canonical natural parameter for observation i.
Feasible coefficient set induced by the natural-parameter domain.
Convex regularizer and its nonnegative weight.

children.title: Margin-Quantile Loss Contrast
children.top_down_role: Nonsmooth classification and conditional-quantile loss families.

children.title: Margin Losses
children.top_down_role: Nonsmooth data-fit choices for margin-based classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Margin Losses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex binary-classification losses expressed through a signed margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observation \(i\), define the signed margin \(m_i=y_i f_\beta(x_i)\). A convex margin loss has the form \(\ell_i(\beta)=\phi(m_i)\), and its regularized empirical-risk problem is \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\quad \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi\bigl(y_i f_\beta(x_i)\bigr)+\lambda R(\beta).\] Standard examples are the hinge penalty \(\phi(m)=\max\{0,1-m\}\) and logistic penalty \(\phi(m)=\log(1+e^{-m})\). Since \(\phi\) is nonincreasing, increasing a positive signed margin cannot increase the loss. If \(f_\beta(x)\) is affine in \(\beta\), the displayed objective is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex margin loss applies a nonincreasing convex penalty to a binary classifier's signed score; hinge and logistic loss are standard examples, and affine scores with convex regularization give a convex objective.
assumptions_latex: For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), the score \(f_\beta(x)\in\mathbb R\) is affine in \(\beta\).
The function \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) is convex and nonincreasing.
The function \(R:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex, and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized empirical margin-risk objective is convex in \(\beta\).

notation.meaning: Convex regularizer and its nonnegative weight.

children.title: Quantile Losses
children.top_down_role: Asymmetric data-fit choices for conditional-quantile estimation.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantile Losses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex check loss for a fixed conditional quantile level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau\in(0,1)\), the check loss is \[\rho_\tau(u)=u\bigl(\tau-\mathbf 1_{\{u<0\}}\bigr)=\max\{\tau u,(\tau-1)u\}.\] Regularized quantile regression solves \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\rho_\tau\bigl(y_i-q_\beta(x_i)\bigr)+\lambda R(\beta)\right\}.\] Positive residuals receive slope \(\tau\), and negative residuals receive slope \(\tau-1\). For a scalar random variable \(Y\), every minimizer \(q\) of \(\mathbb E[\rho_\tau(Y-q)]\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(Y<q)\le\tau\le\mathbb P(Y\le q)\), and hence is a \(\tau\)-quantile under this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantile regression uses the asymmetric convex check loss. With an affine predictor and convex regularizer it is a convex program, and its scalar population minimizers satisfy the defining quantile inequalities.
assumptions_latex: A level \(\tau\in(0,1)\) is fixed, and \(x_i\in\mathcal X\), \(y_i\in\mathbb R\), and \(\beta\in\mathbb R^p\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), the predictor \(q_\beta(x)\in\mathbb R\) is affine in \(\beta\).
The function \(R:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex, and \(\lambda\ge0\).
For the population statement, \(\mathbb E[\rho_\tau(Y-q)]\) is finite for at least one \(q\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The empirical objective is convex in \(\beta\), and scalar population minimizers obey the \(\tau\)-quantile inequalities.

children.title: Classification–Quantile Contrast
children.top_down_role: Differences in targets, residual geometry, use cases, and regularized interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Classification–Quantile Contrast
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural contrast between binary margin risk and conditional quantile risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Margin classification uses risks of the form \(\mathbb E[\phi(Y_{\mathrm c}f(X))]\), where \(Y_{\mathrm c}\in\{-1,1\}\) and the loss acts on the signed margin \(Y_{\mathrm c}f(X)\). Quantile regression uses risks of the form \(\mathbb E[\rho_\tau(Y_{\mathrm q}-q(X))]\), where \(Y_{\mathrm q}\in\mathbb R\) and the loss acts on an additive residual. A conditional minimizer of the check-loss risk satisfies the conditional \(\tau\)-quantile inequalities. Although both empirical objectives can be convex and piecewise linear, their arguments and targets are different: a nonincreasing margin loss favors larger correctly signed scores, whereas check loss balances underprediction and overprediction according to \(\tau\) and \(1-\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Margin losses act on signed binary-classification scores, while quantile losses act on additive real-valued residuals and identify conditional quantiles; their similar convex forms do not make their targets interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The classification response satisfies \(Y_{\mathrm c}\in\{-1,1\}\), and the quantile response satisfies \(Y_{\mathrm q}\in\mathbb R\).
The function \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) is convex and nonincreasing, and \(\rho_\tau\) is the check loss for \(\tau\in(0,1)\).
The relevant risks are finite, and conditional check-loss minimizers exist for the quantile statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two risks may both be convex, but signed margins and additive residuals encode different prediction targets and are not interchangeable.

children.title: Robust Loss Families
children.top_down_role: Data-fit choices for outliers, heavy tails, and contaminated observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Loss Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex residual losses whose bounded subgradients limit the first-order contribution of extreme residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_i=y_i-f_\beta(x_i)\). A regularized convex robust data-fit objective is \[F(\beta)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\rho(r_i)+\lambda R(\beta).\] The absolute loss is \(\rho(r)=|r|\). For \(\delta>0\), the Huber loss is \[\rho_\delta(r)=\begin{cases}\frac12r^2,&|r|\le\delta,\\ \delta|r|-\frac12\delta^2,&|r|>\delta.\end{cases}\] Its derivative satisfies \(\rho_\delta'(r)\in[-\delta,\delta]\). More generally, if every subgradient of \(\rho\) has magnitude at most \(C\), no residual can contribute a scalar loss subgradient larger than \(C\), even when its magnitude is arbitrarily large. Affine prediction and convex regularization make \(F\) convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex robust losses such as absolute and Huber loss have bounded slopes, limiting the scalar first-order contribution of extreme residuals; affine prediction and convex regularization preserve convexity.
assumptions_latex: For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(f_\beta(x)\in\mathbb R\) is affine in \(\beta\).
The function \(\rho:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) is proper and convex, and there is \(C<\infty\) such that \(|s|\le C\) for every \(s\in\partial\rho(r)\) and \(r\in\mathbb R\).
The function \(R:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex, and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective \(F\) is convex, and each residual's scalar loss subgradient is uniformly bounded.

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on scalar loss subgradients.

children.title: Regularization Geometry-Role Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Structural purposes and geometric classes of convex regularization.

children.title: Shrinkage Stabilization Roles
children.top_down_role: Regularization roles centered on conditioning and coefficient shrinkage.

children.title: Coefficient Shrinkage
children.top_down_role: Magnitude contraction across coefficient blocks and parameter directions.

assumptions_latex: A vector \(z\in\mathbb{R}^p\), proximal scale \(t>0\), and penalty weight \(\lambda>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quadratic regularization contracts every coefficient toward zero by the common factor \((1+2t\lambda)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient contraction induced by squared Euclidean regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proximal update for squared Euclidean regularization is \[\operatorname{prox}_{tR}(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{\frac12\lVert\beta-z\rVert_2^2+t\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2\right\}=\frac{1}{1+2t\lambda}z.\] Consequently, every coordinate magnitude weakly decreases, the coefficient direction is preserved for \(z\ne0\), and \(\lVert\operatorname{prox}_{tR}(z)\rVert_2=(1+2t\lambda)^{-1}\lVert z\rVert_2\). This is shrinkage rather than exact selection: a nonzero coordinate of \(z\) remains nonzero after the update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared Euclidean regularization uniformly contracts coefficients toward zero but does not set nonzero coordinates exactly to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Shrinkage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal formula and its shrinkage-without-selection consequences are correct and fit a property container, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Numerical Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Conditioning improvements associated with regularized estimation.

assumptions_latex: The quadratic data-fit Hessian is \(H=X^{\mathsf T}X/n\), with eigenvalues \(0\le\mu_{\min}\le\mu_{\max}\).
A ridge term \(\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2/2\) is added with \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized Hessian is positive definite and has a smaller spectral condition number whenever the original condition number is finite and exceeds one.

notation.meaning: Smallest and largest eigenvalues of H.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning effect of ridge regularization in least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding the ridge term changes the Hessian from \(H\) to \(H_\lambda=H+\lambda I\). Hence \(\lambda_{\min}(H_\lambda)=\mu_{\min}+\lambda>0\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(H_\lambda)=\mu_{\max}+\lambda\). Its spectral condition number is \[\kappa_2(H_\lambda)=\frac{\mu_{\max}+\lambda}{\mu_{\min}+\lambda}.\] If \(0<\mu_{\min}<\mu_{\max}\), then \(\kappa_2(H_\lambda)<\mu_{\max}/\mu_{\min}\); if \(\mu_{\min}=0\), regularization replaces singularity by the finite condition number \((\mu_{\max}+\lambda)/\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge regularization shifts every Hessian eigenvalue upward, removes singularity, and reduces the spectral condition number of a non-isotropic least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Stabilization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The eigenvalue shift and condition-number comparisons are correct, with singular and positive-definite cases properly separated, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Bias–Variance Effects
children.top_down_role: Statistical consequences of stronger or weaker contraction.

assumptions_latex: The Gaussian sequence model is \(Z_j=\theta_j+\varepsilon_j\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\), with independent \(\varepsilon_j\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\).
The shrinkage estimator is \(\widehat\theta_j=aZ_j\) for a fixed \(a\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decreasing \(a\) lowers variance but increases squared bias, with the exact mean-squared-error decomposition displayed in the statement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bias–variance decomposition for scalar linear shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each coordinate, \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat\theta_j]=a\theta_j\), so its bias is \((a-1)\theta_j\), while \(\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\theta_j)=a^2\sigma^2\). Therefore \[\mathbb{E}\lVert\widehat\theta-\theta\rVert_2^2=(1-a)^2\lVert\theta\rVert_2^2+a^2p\sigma^2.\] Relative to the unshrunk estimator \(a=1\), any \(a<1\) reduces the variance term from \(p\sigma^2\) to \(a^2p\sigma^2\) but introduces squared bias \((1-a)^2\lVert\theta\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear shrinkage reduces estimator variance while introducing bias; in the Gaussian sequence model the two contributions admit an exact risk decomposition.
knowledge_statements.title: Bias–Variance Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gaussian-sequence bias–variance decomposition is exact and the representation content kind fits, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Sparsity Selection Roles
children.top_down_role: Coordinate, group, and transformed-coordinate selection roles.

children.title: Coordinate Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Selection organized around individual parameter coordinates.

assumptions_latex: A vector \(z\in\mathbb{R}^p\) and threshold \(\lambda>0\) are fixed.
Coordinate sparsity is promoted by the penalty \(R(\beta)=\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal solution is coordinatewise soft thresholding and has an exact zero wherever \(|z_j|\le\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate selection generated by the lasso proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proximal problem \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\quad \frac12\lVert\beta-z\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\] has the unique solution \(\beta_j=S_\lambda(z_j)=\operatorname{sign}(z_j)\max\{|z_j|-\lambda,0\}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\). Thus \(\beta_j=0\) exactly when \(|z_j|\le\lambda\), while surviving coordinates are reduced in magnitude by \(\lambda\). The nonsmooth geometry of the \(\ell_1\) norm therefore permits coordinatewise exact zeros, unlike squared Euclidean shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lasso proximal map soft-thresholds each coordinate, producing exact zeros below the threshold and shrinking larger coordinates toward zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Sparsity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The soft-thresholding formula, uniqueness, and exact-zero condition are correct and fit the coordinate-sparsity leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Group Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Selection organized around predefined parameter blocks.

assumptions_latex: The indices \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\) are partitioned into disjoint groups \(\mathcal{G}\).
Positive group weights \(w_g\) and a penalty level \(\lambda>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal map removes or retains each entire group according to its Euclidean norm.

notation.meaning: Partition of coefficient indices into groups.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonoverlapping group-lasso geometry and block soft thresholding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For input \(z\in\mathbb{R}^p\), the proximal map of the group penalty separates across groups and satisfies \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{R}(z)\bigr)_g=\left(1-\frac{\lambda w_g}{\lVert z_g\rVert_2}\right)_+z_g,\] with the value defined as \(0\) when \(z_g=0\). Consequently, the whole block indexed by \(g\) is zero exactly when \(\lVert z_g\rVert_2\le\lambda w_g\). When the block survives, all its coordinates are scaled by the same nonnegative factor, preserving its within-group direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group lasso applies block soft thresholding, setting an entire predefined coefficient group to zero when its Euclidean norm is below threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Group Sparsity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For disjoint groups, the block soft-thresholding formula and zero-block criterion are correct and fit a property container, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Transformed-Coordinate Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection expressed after applying a structural transform.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformed-Coordinate Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Analysis regularization selecting zeros after a fixed linear transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Transformed-coordinate selection uses the convex problem \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\quad L(\beta)+\lambda\lVert D\beta\rVert_1.\] For any minimizer \(\widehat\beta\), its selected cosupport is \[\Lambda(\widehat\beta)=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:(D\widehat\beta)_j=0\}.\] Thus the penalty promotes zeros among analyzed coefficients, differences, or other fixed linear features rather than necessarily among the coordinates of \(\beta\). For \(D=I\), the formulation reduces to coordinatewise \(\ell_1\) regularization. For a first-difference operator, it promotes piecewise-constant coefficient sequences by encouraging adjacent differences to be zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analysis regularization penalizes the l1 norm of a fixed linear transform, so any attained solution is selected through zero transformed features such as differences rather than necessarily through zero original coefficients.
assumptions_latex: The map \(D:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(L:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex, and \(\lambda>0\).
The displayed optimization problem has at least one minimizer \(\widehat\beta\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalty promotes sparsity in \(D\widehat\beta\), and the selected transformed coordinates are recorded by \(\Lambda(\widehat\beta)\).

notation.meaning: A minimizer of the analysis-regularized problem.

children.title: Selection Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of selected structures under weak separation or perturbation.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A duplicated-feature lasso instance exhibiting nonunique selected supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=(1,1)\in\mathbb R^{1\times 2}\), \(y=1\), and \(0<\lambda<1\). Consider
\[\min_{\beta\in\mathbb R^2}\ \frac12(1-\beta_1-\beta_2)^2+\lambda(|\beta_1|+|\beta_2|).\]
Its complete solution set is
\[\{\beta\in\mathbb R_+^2:\ \beta_1+\beta_2=1-\lambda\}.\]
Thus \((1-\lambda,0)\), \((0,1-\lambda)\), and solutions with both coordinates positive attain the same optimum but have different supports. Consequently, the selected coordinate set is not determined by the fitted value or objective value when duplicated features destroy strict convexity in the coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With two identical features, lasso has equally optimal coefficient vectors selecting the first feature, the second feature, or both; hence support selection is unstable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta}\{\tfrac12(1-\beta_1-\beta_2)^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_1\}=\{\beta\ge 0:\beta_1+\beta_2=1-\lambda\}\), so optimal supports are nonunique.

notation.meaning: Indices of the nonzero coordinates of beta.

review_flags: Exact supporting source for the duplicated-feature lasso counterexample is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct and its content kind fits the failure-oriented leaf, but the exact duplicated-feature lasso solution set has no cited source.

children.title: Structured Smoothness Coupling
children.top_down_role: Regularizers encoding similarity, variation, graph, or ordering structure.

children.title: Local Smoothness
children.top_down_role: Regularization of variation between nearby parameter locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic regularization of parameter differences across prescribed local neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,p\}\), let \(E_{\mathrm{loc}}\subseteq\{\{i,j\}:i\ne j\}\) encode local neighborhoods, and let \(w_{ij}\ge 0\). For \(\theta\in\mathbb R^p\), the local-smoothness penalty is
\[R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_{\mathrm{loc}}}w_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j)^2.\]
It is a convex quadratic regularizer, vanishes precisely when \(\theta_i=\theta_j\) on every positive-weight local edge, and favors gradual local changes without directly requiring coordinate sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local smoothness penalizes squared differences between parameters attached to neighboring locations, encouraging nearby coordinates to take similar values.
assumptions_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is a finite undirected neighborhood relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is convex and \(R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\theta)=0\) exactly when \(\theta_i=\theta_j\) on all edges with \(w_{ij}>0\).

notation.meaning: Set of prescribed local neighbor pairs.

review_flags: Supplied smoothness locators concern smooth functions rather than neighborhood-difference regularization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and stated convexity and nullspace properties are precise, but no source supports neighborhood-difference regularization in this local sense.

children.title: Graph Coupling
children.top_down_role: Parameter relationships encoded through graph connectivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-matrix representation of convex coupling over a weighted graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an oriented graph with incidence matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times |V|}\), and let \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_e)\) with \(w_e\ge0\). For \(\theta\in\mathbb R^{|V|}\), graph coupling may be represented by
\[R_{G,q}(\theta)=\|W^{1/q}B\theta\|_q^q=\sum_{e=(i,j)\in E}w_e|\theta_i-\theta_j|^q,\qquad q\ge1.\]
The value is independent of the chosen edge orientations. It is convex; for positive weights, its nullspace consists of vectors constant on each connected component of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph coupling applies a convex penalty to parameter differences along graph edges and is expressible through the graph incidence matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite graph with an arbitrary edge orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{G,q}(\theta)=\sum_{e=(i,j)}w_e|\theta_i-\theta_j|^q\) is convex and orientation-independent.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports incidence-matrix graph regularization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incidence-matrix representation is mathematically sound and appropriately classified, but it lacks a source for graph regularization and its nullspace characterization.

children.title: Ordered Variation
children.top_down_role: Variation control over sequences, grids, or ordered domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Variation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-variation regularization for parameters indexed by a linear order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an ordered parameter vector \(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_p)\in\mathbb R^p\) and weights \(w_i\ge0\), define the ordered-variation penalty by
\[R_{\mathrm{ord}}(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}w_i|\theta_{i+1}-\theta_i|.\]
This convex seminorm penalizes changes between consecutive coordinates. If every \(w_i>0\), then \(R_{\mathrm{ord}}(\theta)=0\) exactly for constant vectors. An \(\ell_1\) penalty on successive differences promotes a sparse set of change points and hence piecewise-constant fitted sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered variation sums absolute successive differences, promoting sequences with few change points and piecewise-constant segments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{ord}}\) is convex, and positive weights give \(R_{\mathrm{ord}}(\theta)=0\iff\theta_1=\cdots=\theta_p\).

notation.meaning: Weight on the difference between consecutive coordinates.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly covers ordered total-variation regularization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted ordered total-variation definition is correct and fits the leaf, but the change-point and piecewise-constant claims require a specific source.

children.title: Similarity Penalties
children.top_down_role: Regularization favoring agreement among related parameter components.

knowledge_statements.title: Similarity Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise convex penalties encoding known similarity between parameter components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\{\{i,j\}:i\ne j\}\) be a set of pairs declared similar, let \(w_{ij}\ge0\), and let \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) be convex, even, and satisfy \(\phi(0)=0\). The associated similarity penalty is
\[R_S(\theta)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in S}w_{ij}\phi(\theta_i-\theta_j),\qquad \theta\in\mathbb R^p.\]
It is convex and favors agreement on heavily weighted pairs. Choosing \(\phi(t)=|t|\) promotes exact fusion, whereas \(\phi(t)=t^2/2\) produces continuous quadratic shrinkage toward similarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Similarity penalties charge discrepancies between designated parameter pairs; absolute differences promote fusion, while squared differences produce smooth shrinkage.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite set of unordered coordinate pairs and \(w_{ij}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_S\) is a convex function of \(\theta\) that is minimized by agreement across positive-weight similarity pairs.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this general pairwise-similarity penalty template.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general similarity-penalty template is coherent and correctly classified as a definition, but no inspectable source supports the template or the fusion-versus-quadratic distinction.

children.title: Decomposable-Regularizer Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Structural decompositions connecting penalty geometry with external statistical guarantee frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposable-Regularizer Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspace decomposability condition used to connect regularizer geometry with statistical error analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal M\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be linear subspaces, and let \(R:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R_+\) be a norm or convex gauge. The regularizer is decomposable with respect to \((\mathcal M,\overline{\mathcal M}^{\perp})\) when
\[R(u+v)=R(u)+R(v)\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal M\text{ and }v\in\overline{\mathcal M}^{\perp}.\]
Here \(\mathcal M\) represents the model subspace and \(\overline{\mathcal M}^{\perp}\) the perturbation directions separated additively by the penalty. This equality, not merely the triangle inequality, is the decomposable-regularizer interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularizer is decomposable when it adds exactly across a model subspace and the orthogonal complement of an enclosing subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) are linear subspaces.
\(R\) is a norm or convex gauge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\text{ is decomposable with respect to }(\mathcal M,\overline{\mathcal M}^{\perp})\iff R(u+v)=R(u)+R(v)\) for all admissible \(u,v\).
review_flags: The supplied inventory contains no locator for decomposable regularizers or their statistical interface.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decomposability condition matches the node's structural-interface role, but the extension from norms to general convex gauges and the statistical-interface interpretation need authoritative support.

children.title: Regularized Formulation Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Canonical parameterizations of regularized empirical risk and sparse recovery.

children.title: Penalized ERM
children.top_down_role: Regularization-weight parameterizations of empirical risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized ERM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex empirical risk augmented by a weighted convex regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given observations \(z_1,\ldots,z_n\), a convex parameter domain \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), losses \(\ell(\cdot;z_i):\Theta\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), a proper convex regularizer \(R:\Theta\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), penalized empirical risk minimization returns any
\[\widehat\theta_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\left\{\widehat L_n(\theta)+\lambda R(\theta)\right\},\qquad \widehat L_n(\theta)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(\theta;z_i).\]
When each loss and \(R\) are convex, the displayed problem is convex; existence additionally requires attainment, for example through lower semicontinuity and level-boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalized ERM minimizes average sample loss plus a nonnegative weight times a convex structural regularizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\theta_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\{\widehat L_n(\theta)+\lambda R(\theta)\}\), a convex optimization problem.

notation.meaning: Empirical risk, the average observed loss.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.1 General Formulation of the Problem p. 3

review_flags: The locator supports the general convex formulation; ERM-specific terminology requires source confirmation.

children.title: Regularizer-Budget ERM
children.top_down_role: Constraint-form parameterizations using a structural-complexity budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularizer-Budget ERM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical-risk minimization constrained by a structural-complexity budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be convex, let \(\widehat L_n:\Theta\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper convex empirical risk, let \(R:\Theta\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper convex regularizer, and let \(\tau\in\mathbb R\). Regularizer-budget ERM returns any
\[\widehat\theta_\tau\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\widehat L_n(\theta)\quad\text{subject to}\quad R(\theta)\le\tau.\]
The problem is convex whenever its feasible set is nonempty. The budget \(\tau\) directly bounds admissible structural complexity rather than pricing it in the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularizer-budget ERM minimizes empirical risk among parameters whose regularizer value does not exceed a prescribed structural budget.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is convex and \(\widehat L_n,R\) are proper convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\theta_\tau\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\widehat L_n(\theta):\theta\in\Theta,\ R(\theta)\le\tau\}\), a convex constrained problem.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.1 General Formulation of the Problem p. 3

children.title: Residual-Budget Recovery
children.top_down_role: Structural minimization under a data-fidelity budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Budget Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural minimization subject to a convex data-fidelity constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, let \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(R:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper convex structural regularizer, and let \(D(\cdot,y):\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper convex discrepancy. For a fidelity budget \(\varepsilon\), residual-budget recovery returns any
\[\widehat\theta_\varepsilon\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\mathbb R^p}R(\theta)\quad\text{subject to}\quad D(A\theta,y)\le\varepsilon.\]
This is convex when the feasible set is nonempty; with \(D(u,y)=\|u-y\|\), the constraint directly bounds the residual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-budget recovery minimizes structural complexity while requiring the model-data discrepancy to remain below a prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is linear and \(R\) is proper convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\theta_\varepsilon\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{R(\theta):D(A\theta,y)\le\varepsilon\}\), a convex recovery problem.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.1 General Formulation of the Problem p. 3

children.title: Multi-Penalty Formulations
children.top_down_role: Models with separately controlled shrinkage, sparsity, or structural components.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Penalty Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex ERM with independently weighted structural regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be convex, let \(\widehat L_n:\Theta\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper convex empirical risk, and let \(R_k:\Theta\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex regularizers for \(k=1,\ldots,K\). A multi-penalty formulation is
\[\widehat\theta_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\left\{\widehat L_n(\theta)+\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_kR_k(\theta)\right\},\qquad \lambda_k\ge0.\]
Each coefficient independently prices a designated geometry, such as shrinkage, sparsity, or coupling. The formulation remains convex, though its decomposition into penalty terms need not be identifiable when the regularizers are redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-penalty ERM adds several convex regularizers with separate nonnegative weights, allowing distinct structural effects to be controlled independently.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is convex and \(\widehat L_n,R_1,\ldots,R_K\) are proper convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L_n+\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_kR_k\) is convex, so the displayed multi-penalty program is convex.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative weight assigned to the kth regularizer.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.1 General Formulation of the Problem p. 3

children.title: Regularization Parameter-Value Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Routes connecting alternative formulations and the boundaries of those correspondences.

children.title: Lagrangian Parameter Routes
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-based navigation between penalties and active budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Parameter Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT-based correspondence between an active regularizer budget and a penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the convex budget problem \(\min_{\theta\in\Theta} f(\theta)\) subject to \(R(\theta)\le\tau\), where \(f\) and \(R\) are proper closed convex functions and \(\Theta\) is convex. If Slater's condition holds and \(\theta_\tau\) is optimal, then there exists \(\lambda_\tau\ge0\) such that
\[\theta_\tau\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\{f(\theta)+\lambda_\tau R(\theta)\},\qquad \lambda_\tau(R(\theta_\tau)-\tau)=0.\]
Conversely, any penalized minimizer \(\theta_\lambda\) solves the budget problem with \(\tau=R(\theta_\lambda)\). The multiplier route may be set-valued when minimizers or multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under convexity and Slater feasibility, a budget solution has a supporting penalty multiplier; a penalized solution solves the budget problem at its attained regularizer value.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(R\) are proper closed convex functions on a convex set \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda_\tau\ge0\) satisfying penalized optimality and \(\lambda_\tau(R(\theta_\tau)-\tau)=0\); conversely set \(\tau=R(\theta_\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: Optimal multiplier and corresponding penalty weight.
Relative interior of the feasible domain.

source_refs.locator: 4.2.4. Augmented Lagrangian Duality p. 140

review_flags: The supplied duality locator is adjacent in subject but must be checked for the exact KKT correspondence stated.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.4. Augmented Lagrangian Duality p. 140

children.title: Pareto Tradeoff Routes
children.top_down_role: Tradeoff-curve navigation between structural size and data fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Tradeoff Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Efficient frontier relating empirical loss to attained structural complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible parameter set \(\Theta\), convex loss \(f\), and convex regularizer \(R\), define the upper attainable set
\[\mathcal U=\{(r,\ell)\in\mathbb R^2:\exists\theta\in\Theta,\ R(\theta)\le r,\ f(\theta)\le\ell\}.\]
Its lower-left boundary is the Pareto tradeoff frontier. Every minimizer of \(f(\theta)+\lambda R(\theta)\) with \(\lambda>0\) yields a weakly Pareto-efficient point \((R(\theta),f(\theta))\). Conversely, every properly supported frontier point minimizes such a weighted sum for some \(\lambda>0\). Varying a budget or supporting weight therefore traces supported portions of the same loss-complexity tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Pareto frontier records nondominated loss-complexity pairs; positive weighted penalties generate its supported points, while budgets navigate it by structural size.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(R\) are proper convex functions with attained relevant minima.
The converse is restricted to properly supported frontier points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\operatorname*{argmin}(f+\lambda R)\), \(\lambda>0\), implies \((R(\theta),f(\theta))\) is weakly Pareto efficient; properly supported points admit such a \(\lambda\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the weighted-sum characterization of the Pareto frontier.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto upper-image construction and supported-point route fit the leaf, but the weighted-sum characterization and its converse have no cited source.

children.title: Parameter Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Multiple parameter values or multipliers associated with the same solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete convex example where many positive penalty parameters yield the same optimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\), \(F(x)=0\), and \(R(x)=|x|\). For every \(\lambda>0\), the penalized problem is \[\min_{x\in X} F(x)+\lambda R(x)=\min_{x\in[-1,1]}\lambda|x|,\] whose unique minimizer is \(x=0\). Hence \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}(F(x)+\lambda R(x))=\{0\}\) for every \(\lambda\in(0,\infty)\). Thus the optimizer set does not, in general, identify a unique regularization parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for convex objectives, every positive regularization parameter can produce the same optimizer, so parameter-to-solution correspondence need not be injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}(F(x)+\lambda R(x))=\{0\}\) for all \(\lambda>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conclusion follows by direct minimization of the displayed one-dimensional convex objective

children.title: Degenerate Correspondence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Constraint regimes where correspondence becomes degenerate or a formulation loses feasibility.

children.title: Inactive-Constraint Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter ranges where a budget ceases to determine the solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Constraint Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inactive regularization budgets force a zero KKT multiplier and collapse positive-parameter correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in C}F(x)\) subject to \(R(x)\leq\tau\), where \(F\) and \(R\) are proper convex functions and KKT conditions hold. If an optimal point \(x^\star\) satisfies \(R(x^\star)<\tau\), complementary slackness gives \(\lambda^\star(R(x^\star)-\tau)=0\), hence \(\lambda^\star=0\). The Lagrangian objective then reduces to \(F\); consequently this constrained solution is associated canonically only with the unregularized endpoint, and no positive multiplier is supplied by KKT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the budget constraint is slack at an optimum, complementary slackness sets its multiplier to zero, so the usual positive-regularization correspondence degenerates.
assumptions_latex: \(F,R\) are proper convex functions on a convex set \(C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^\star=0\).

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier of the budget constraint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct application of KKT complementary slackness
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Infeasible-Budget Regimes
children.top_down_role: Budget ranges for which the constrained formulation has no admissible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Budget Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgets below the least attainable regularizer value make the constrained formulation infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be the decision set and define \(r_{\min}=\inf\{R(x):x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}F\}\). If \(\tau<r_{\min}\), then no point in \(C\cap\operatorname{dom}F\) satisfies \(R(x)\leq\tau\). Therefore the budget-constrained problem \[\min\{F(x):x\in C,\ R(x)\leq\tau\}\] has empty feasible set and no optimizer. Accordingly, no penalization parameter can correspond to a constrained optimizer at that budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A budget below the minimum attainable regularizer value leaves no feasible point, so optimizer-based correspondence with a penalized problem is impossible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}F:R(x)\leq\tau\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: infimum of the regularizer over loss-finite decisions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: infeasibility follows immediately from the definition of an infimum lower bound

children.title: Correspondence Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Loss of a usable mapping between penalized and constrained controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Correspondence Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonconvex attainable tradeoff set can contain unsupported constrained optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b,c\}\), with \((R(a),F(a))=(0,2)\), \((R(b),F(b))=(1,3/2)\), and \((R(c),F(c))=(2,0)\). At budget \(\tau=1\), the constrained problem uniquely selects \(b\). For \(b\) to minimize \(F+\lambda R\), comparison with \(a\) requires \(\lambda\leq1/2\), while comparison with \(c\) requires \(\lambda\geq3/2\). These conditions are incompatible, so no \(\lambda\geq0\) reproduces the constrained optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained optimum on a nonconvex tradeoff frontier may be unsupported: no nonnegative weighted-sum parameter recovers it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{R(x)\leq1}F(x)=\{b\}\), but \(b\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}(F(x)+\lambda R(x))\) for every \(\lambda\geq0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the finite counterexample is verified by the displayed pairwise comparisons

children.title: Regularization Convention Interface
children.top_down_role: Formulation conventions that materially alter the interpretation of regularization controls.

children.title: Model Scaling Convention System
children.top_down_role: Normalization choices governing comparable regularization across models and datasets.

children.title: Feature Scaling
children.top_down_role: Predictor normalization choices affecting coefficient comparability and penalty strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Feature Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal feature rescaling transports coefficients and converts an unweighted penalty into a weighted penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) and let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)\) with every \(d_j\neq0\). Define scaled features \(X'=XD\) and coefficients \(\beta'=D^{-1}\beta\). Then \(X'\beta'=X\beta\), so every loss depending only on fitted linear predictors is unchanged. Under this reparameterization, the original penalty becomes \(R(\beta)=R(D\beta')\); in particular, \(\|\beta\|_1=\sum_{j=1}^p|d_j||\beta'_j|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling feature columns requires inverse coefficient scaling to preserve predictions and generally transports an unweighted coefficient penalty into a weighted one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X'\beta'=X\beta\) and \(R(\beta)=R(D\beta')\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact algebraic change of variables in a linear predictor
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Response Scaling
children.top_down_role: Outcome normalization choices affecting fitted scales and tuning interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Response Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Response rescaling transports squared-loss coefficients and the regularization parameter according to penalty homogeneity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq1\), \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\lambda\geq0\). Define \(Q_{y,\lambda}(\beta,b)=\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta-b\mathbf{1}\rVert_2^2+\lambda R(\beta)\), where \(R(t\beta)=|t|^qR(\beta)\) for every \(t\neq0\). For \(c\neq0\), set \(y'=cy\), \(\beta'=c\beta\), \(b'=cb\), and \(\lambda'=|c|^{2-q}\lambda\). Then \[Q_{y',\lambda'}(\beta',b')=c^2Q_{y,\lambda}(\beta,b).\] Consequently, \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta',b'}Q_{y',\lambda'}(\beta',b')=\bigl\{(c\beta,cb):(\beta,b)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta,b}Q_{y,\lambda}(\beta,b)\bigr\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For squared loss and a homogeneous penalty, multiplying the response by a nonzero scalar multiplies the fitted coefficients and intercept by that scalar and transports the regularization parameter by the factor given by the penalty's homogeneity degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda'=|c|^{2-q}\lambda\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta',b'}Q_{cy,\lambda'}=\{(c\beta,cb):(\beta,b)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta,b}Q_{y,\lambda}\}\).

notation.meaning: regularized squared-loss objective for response y and parameter lambda

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact scaling identity for squared loss and a homogeneous regularizer
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Loss Normalization
children.top_down_role: Objective averaging or aggregation conventions affecting regularization calibration.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sum-loss and mean-loss conventions are equivalent after transporting the regularization coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observations \(i=1,\ldots,n\), define \(J_{\mathrm{sum}}(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_i(\theta)+\lambda_{\mathrm{sum}}R(\theta)\) and \(J_{\mathrm{mean}}(\theta)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_i(\theta)+\lambda_{\mathrm{mean}}R(\theta)\). If \(\lambda_{\mathrm{mean}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{sum}}/n\), then \(J_{\mathrm{mean}}=J_{\mathrm{sum}}/n\). Since multiplication by a positive constant preserves minimizers, the two conventions have identical optimizer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing empirical loss from a sum to a mean preserves minimizers when the regularization coefficient is divided by the sample size.
assumptions_latex: Both objectives have the same feasible domain
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\mathrm{mean}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{sum}}/n\) implies \(\operatorname*{argmin}J_{\mathrm{mean}}=\operatorname*{argmin}J_{\mathrm{sum}}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive rescaling of an objective preserves its argmin set
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Regularization-Scale Transport
children.top_down_role: Translation of tuning controls across alternative normalization conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization-Scale Transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive rescaling of loss and penalty induces an exact transport rule for the regularization parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F'=c_FF\) and \(R'=c_RR\), where \(c_F>0\) and \(c_R>0\). For any \(\lambda\geq0\), choose \(\lambda'=c_F\lambda/c_R\). Then \[F'(x)+\lambda'R'(x)=c_F\bigl(F(x)+\lambda R(x)\bigr).\] Therefore the transformed and original objectives have exactly the same minimizer set over every common feasible domain. Conversely, equality up to the factor \(c_F\) requires this parameter transport whenever \(R\) is not identically zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If loss and penalty scales change by positive factors, multiplying the regularization parameter by the loss factor divided by the penalty factor preserves minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The original and transformed problems share a feasible domain
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda'=c_F\lambda/c_R\) implies \(\operatorname*{argmin}(F'+\lambda'R')=\operatorname*{argmin}(F+\lambda R)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact positive scaling identity for regularized objectives
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Unpenalized Component Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Components commonly separated from the penalized parameter block.

children.title: Intercept Handling
children.top_down_role: Centering and penalty conventions for model intercepts.

knowledge_statements.title: Intercept Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An intercept is an optimized constant predictor component commonly excluded from the regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For responses \(y_i\), features \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^p\), coefficient vector \(\beta\), and scalar intercept \(b\), unpenalized intercept handling means solving \[\min_{\beta,b}\ \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell\bigl(y_i,x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta+b\bigr)+\lambda R(\beta).\] The intercept \(b\) is optimized jointly with \(\beta\) but is absent from \(R\). Equivalently, the penalty is invariant along the intercept coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unpenalized intercept is a fitted constant added to every linear predictor while the regularizer acts only on the remaining coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\) is optimized, while the penalty term is \(\lambda R(\beta)\) and contains no \(b\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard regularized empirical-risk formulation with an unpenalized intercept
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Fixed Offsets
children.top_down_role: Known additive components retained outside the optimized penalized block.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Offsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed offset is a known predictor component that is neither estimated nor penalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given known offsets \(o_1,\ldots,o_n\), a regularized model with fixed offsets solves \[\min_{\beta}\ \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell\bigl(y_i,o_i+x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta\bigr)+\lambda R(\beta).\] Each \(o_i\) is data, not a decision variable, and is therefore neither optimized nor included in the penalty. The fitted linear predictor is \(\eta_i=o_i+x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed offset is a known additive predictor term retained in the loss but excluded from both optimization and regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_i=o_i+x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta\), with \(o_i\) fixed and absent from \(R(\beta)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard offset formulation in regression-type empirical risk
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Nuisance Components
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary estimated terms separated from primary regularized parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Nuisance Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nuisance components are jointly estimated variables excluded from the penalty on the target coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be a finite-dimensional vector space, let \(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to W\) and \(B:\mathbb{R}^q\to W\) be linear maps, let \(L:W\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(R:\mathbb{R}^p\to[0,+\infty]\), and let \(\lambda\geq0\). An unpenalized nuisance-component formulation is \[\inf_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p,\,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^q}\bigl\{L(A\beta+B\gamma)+\lambda R(\beta)\bigr\}.\] Both \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\) affect the loss, but only \(\beta\) enters the regularizer. Its profiled form is \[\inf_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{\inf_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^q}L(A\beta+B\gamma)+\lambda R(\beta)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nuisance coefficients affect the loss and are optimized jointly with the target coefficients, but they are excluded from the target regularizer; profiling minimizes the loss over the nuisance block for each target coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\beta,\gamma}\{L(A\beta+B\gamma)+\lambda R(\beta)\}=\inf_{\beta}\{\inf_{\gamma}L(A\beta+B\gamma)+\lambda R(\beta)\}\).

notation.meaning: linear design maps for target and nuisance components

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block-variable formulation and elementary partial minimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Partial Penalization
children.top_down_role: Mixed parameter blocks with distinct penalty eligibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Penalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial penalization regularizes only a designated linear image or parameter block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be a finite-dimensional parameter space, \(P:\Theta\to V\) a linear map, and \(R:V\to[0,\infty]\) a penalty. A partially penalized problem has the form \[\min_{\theta\in\Theta}L(\theta)+\lambda R(P\theta).\] Directions in \(\ker P\) are unpenalized because \(P(\theta+u)=P\theta\) for every \(u\in\ker P\). For a block decomposition \(\theta=(\beta,\gamma)\) with \(P\theta=\beta\), this becomes \(L(\beta,\gamma)+\lambda R(\beta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial penalization applies the regularizer only to a selected parameter image; directions in the penalty operator's kernel remain unpenalized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in\ker P\) implies \(R(P(\theta+u))=R(P\theta)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Factor Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted coordinate and group penalties in finite-dimensional regularized empirical risk minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb{R}^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper convex loss. Coordinate penalty factors \(w_j\ge 0\) define \(P_1(\beta)=\sum_{j=1}^p w_j|\beta_j|\). For a collection of groups \(\mathcal G\subseteq 2^{\{1,\ldots,p\}}\), factors \(v_g\ge 0\) define \(P_{\mathcal G}(\beta)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}v_g\|\beta_g\|_2\). A penalty-factor system is the specification of these factors together with the convention that a zero factor leaves its coordinate or group unpenalized. The associated estimator minimizes \(L(\beta)+\lambda P(\beta)\) for \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty factors assign different regularization scales to coordinates or groups; a zero factor designates an unpenalized component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\{L(\beta)+\lambda P(\beta)\}\).

children.title: Isotropic Ridge

knowledge_statements.title: Isotropic Ridge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform quadratic regularization for a finite-dimensional convex loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous convex loss and let \(\lambda>0\). The isotropic ridge estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{L(\beta)+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2\right\}.\] The penalty treats every Euclidean direction with the same curvature. Because the quadratic term is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex, the objective has at most one minimizer; it has exactly one whenever the minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Isotropic ridge adds the same quadratic shrinkage in every coefficient direction, yielding a unique minimizer whenever one exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L+(\lambda/2)\|\cdot\|_2^2\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex and therefore has at most one minimizer.

children.title: Generalized Tikhonov Regularization

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Tikhonov Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic regularization shaped by a linear transform or positive-semidefinite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(T:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, and let \(\lambda>0\). Generalized Tikhonov regularization defines \[\widehat\beta_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{L(\beta)+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|T\beta\|_2^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, its penalty is \((\lambda/2)\beta^\top Q\beta\) with \(Q=T^\top T\succeq0\). Directions in \(\ker T\) are unpenalized, and uniqueness requires sufficient curvature from \(L\) on those directions or \(Q\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized Tikhonov regularization applies quadratic shrinkage after a linear transform, allowing anisotropic or partially unpenalized directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|T\beta\|_2^2=\beta^\top T^\top T\beta\), with \(\ker(T)\) unpenalized.
review_flags: The supplied source hints do not support generalized Tikhonov regularization; an exact source locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches generalized Tikhonov regularization, but the transform representation and uniqueness qualification have no cited, inspectable support.

children.title: Ridge Constraint Form

knowledge_statements.title: Ridge Constraint Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalized ridge represented by a quadratic norm budget under convexity and attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex. If \(\widehat\beta_\lambda\) minimizes \(L(\beta)+(\lambda/2)\|\beta\|_2^2\) for \(\lambda>0\), then it also solves \[\min_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}L(\beta)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|\beta\|_2^2\le t,\qquad t=\|\widehat\beta_\lambda\|_2^2.\] Conversely, if the constrained problem with \(t>0\) attains a solution and satisfies Slater's condition, then some optimal multiplier \(\mu\ge0\) makes every constrained optimum minimize \(L(\beta)+\mu\|\beta\|_2^2\); positive multipliers correspond to active budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ridge solution determines an equivalent norm budget; under Slater’s condition, a constrained solution is supported by a quadratic penalty multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The relevant optimization problems attain their minima.
For the converse, \(t>0\) and Slater's condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t=\|\widehat\beta_\lambda\|_2^2\) gives the penalized-to-constrained representation, while an optimal multiplier gives the converse.

children.title: Spectral-Filtering Interface
children.top_down_role: Singular-direction interpretation of quadratic regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Filtering Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value representation of ridge-regularized linear least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\) have compact singular value decomposition \(X=U\Sigma V^\top\), with positive singular values \(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r\), and let \(\lambda>0\). The unique minimizer of \(\frac12\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+(\lambda/2)\|\beta\|_2^2\) is \[\widehat\beta_\lambda=V\,\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{\sigma_i}{\sigma_i^2+\lambda}\right)_{i=1}^r U^\top y.\] Hence the fitted response is \(X\widehat\beta_\lambda=U\,\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i^2/(\sigma_i^2+\lambda))_{i=1}^rU^\top y\), so small-singular-value directions receive stronger attenuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge acts spectrally: each data singular direction is multiplied by a shrinkage factor determined by its singular value and the penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient and fitted-value filters are respectively \(\sigma_i/(\sigma_i^2+\lambda)\) and \(\sigma_i^2/(\sigma_i^2+\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: compact singular value decomposition of X

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Elastic Net
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-parameter penalized elastic net for a proper convex loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous convex loss. For \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\), the penalized elastic-net solution set is \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{L(\beta)+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1+\frac{\lambda_2}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2\right\}.\] The \(\ell_1\) term permits sparse solutions, while the quadratic term supplies uniform curvature. If \(\lambda_2>0\) and a minimizer exists, it is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalized elastic net combines an absolute-value penalty with quadratic shrinkage; a positive quadratic coefficient ensures uniqueness when a solution exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lambda_2>0\), the elastic-net objective is \(\lambda_2\)-strongly convex and has at most one minimizer.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the elastic-net formulation; an exact authoritative statistical-learning source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly targets the penalized elastic-net formulation, but the formulation and uniqueness claim lack cited support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalized Elastic-Net Least-Squares Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalized elastic-net formulation, endpoint penalties, and uniqueness when the quadratic component is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(N\ge 1\), \(x_i\in\mathbb R^p\), \(y_i\in\mathbb R\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), the elastic-net estimator solves
\[
\min_{(\beta_0,\beta)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac12\sum_{i=1}^N(y_i-\beta_0-x_i^T\beta)^2+\lambda\left[\frac12(1-\alpha)\|\beta\|_2^2+\alpha\|\beta\|_1\right]\right\}.
\]
For an individual coefficient, the unweighted penalty is \(\frac12(1-\alpha)\beta_j^2+\alpha|\beta_j|\). At \(\alpha=1\) this is the lasso penalty, and at \(\alpha=0\) it is the ridge penalty. If \(\alpha<1\), then the objective is strictly convex and has a unique minimizer, even when predictor columns are correlated or duplicated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic net minimizes least-squares loss plus a mixture of squared Euclidean and l1 penalties on the coefficients. Alpha equal to one gives lasso, while alpha equal to zero gives ridge. With positive regularization weight and alpha below one, the positive quadratic component makes the objective strictly convex, so the solution is unique even with correlated or duplicated predictors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\widehat\beta_0,\widehat\beta)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(\beta_0,\beta)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac12\sum_{i=1}^N(y_i-\beta_0-x_i^T\beta)^2+\lambda\left[\frac12(1-\alpha)\|\beta\|_2^2+\alpha\|\beta\|_1\right]\right\},\qquad \alpha<1\implies\text{the minimizer is unique}.

knowledge_statements.title: Budget-Constrained Elastic Net
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elastic net expressed through a single mixed-penalty budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, choose \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), and define \(P_\alpha(\beta)=\alpha\|\beta\|_1+(1-\alpha)\|\beta\|_2^2/2\). For a budget \(t\ge0\), the budget-constrained elastic net is \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\ L(\beta)\quad\text{subject to}\quad P_\alpha(\beta)\le t.\] At \(\alpha=1\) the budget is purely \(\ell_1\); at \(\alpha=0\) it is purely quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constrained elastic net minimizes loss within a budget combining absolute and squared Euclidean coefficient size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is \(\{\beta:P_\alpha(\beta)\le t\}\), a closed convex mixed-penalty sublevel set.

children.title: Dual-Control Elastic Net

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Control Elastic Net
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elastic net with separate sparsity and quadratic budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. For budgets \(t_1,t_2\ge0\), the dual-control elastic-net problem is \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\ L(\beta)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|\beta\|_1\le t_1,\qquad\frac12\|\beta\|_2^2\le t_2.\] Its two constraints control sparsity-inducing size and quadratic size independently. Under Slater's condition and attainment, optimal multipliers \(\mu_1,\mu_2\ge0\) yield the supported penalized objective \(L(\beta)+\mu_1\|\beta\|_1+(\mu_2/2)\|\beta\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-control elastic net imposes separate L1 and quadratic budgets, whose multipliers recover a supported two-penalty formulation.
assumptions_latex: Multiplier correspondence requires attainment and Slater's condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimal constraint multipliers act as the two elastic-net penalty coefficients.

children.title: Elastic-Net Parameter Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Parameter Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence among two-coefficient, scale-mixture, and constrained elastic-net parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\), not both zero, define \(\lambda=\lambda_1+\lambda_2\) and \(\alpha=\lambda_1/(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)\). Then \[\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1+\frac{\lambda_2}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2=\lambda\left(\alpha\|\beta\|_1+\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2\right).\] Thus \(\lambda_1=\lambda\alpha\) and \(\lambda_2=\lambda(1-\alpha)\). Any penalized minimizer determines the constrained budget \(t=P_\alpha(\widehat\beta)\); conversely, under convexity, attainment, and Slater's condition, a constrained optimum has a supporting multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\), though the parameter correspondence need not be one-to-one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two elastic-net penalty coefficients equal an overall scale times a mixing fraction; constrained and penalized parameters correspond through budgets and multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Constrained-to-penalized correspondence assumes convexity, attainment, and Slater's condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda=\lambda_1+\lambda_2\), \(\alpha=\lambda_1/\lambda\), and \((\lambda_1,\lambda_2)=(\lambda\alpha,\lambda(1-\alpha))\).

children.title: Elastic-Net Augmented-Data Representation

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Augmented-Data Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact augmented least-squares representation under the unscaled two-penalty convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\). Define \(X_a=\begin{bmatrix}X\\ \sqrt{\lambda_2}I_p\end{bmatrix}\) and \(y_a=\begin{bmatrix}y\\0_p\end{bmatrix}\). Then, for every \(\beta\in\mathbb R^p\), \[\frac12\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1+\frac{\lambda_2}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2=\frac12\|y_a-X_a\beta\|_2^2+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1.\] Consequently, the elastic-net and augmented-data Lasso problems have identical objectives and identical minimizer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending a scaled identity matrix and zero responses converts elastic-net least squares exactly into a Lasso problem on augmented data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}\) of the elastic-net objective equals \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta}\{\|y_a-X_a\beta\|_2^2/2+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1\}\).
review_flags: The supplied source hints do not cover the augmented-data elastic-net identity.

children.title: Elastic-Net Grouping Behavior
children.top_down_role: Mixed-penalty behavior for correlated predictors.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Grouping Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-difference bound for active predictors having the same coefficient sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat\beta\) minimize \(\frac12\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1+(\lambda_2/2)\|\beta\|_2^2\), where \(\lambda_2>0\), and write \(r=y-X\widehat\beta\). If \(\widehat\beta_j\widehat\beta_k>0\), the optimality conditions imply \[|\widehat\beta_j-\widehat\beta_k|\le\frac{\|x_j-x_k\|_2\,\|r\|_2}{\lambda_2}.\] In particular, identical predictor columns with same-sign nonzero fitted coefficients receive identical coefficients. Thus increasing predictor similarity tightens the possible separation between their active coefficients, conditional on the residual size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For same-sign active coefficients, elastic net bounds their difference by predictor dissimilarity divided by the quadratic penalty strength.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widehat\beta_j-\widehat\beta_k|\le \|x_j-x_k\|_2\|r\|_2/\lambda_2\).

notation.meaning: fitted residual y minus X beta-hat

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Limiting Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint and intermediate regimes of the normalized elastic-net mixing parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), define \(F_{\lambda,\alpha}(\beta)=L(\beta)+\lambda\{\alpha\|\beta\|_1+(1-\alpha)\|\beta\|_2^2/2\}\). At \(\alpha=1\), \(F_{\lambda,1}\) is the Lasso-type objective \(L+\lambda\|\cdot\|_1\). At \(\alpha=0\), \(F_{\lambda,0}\) is the ridge objective \(L+(\lambda/2)\|\cdot\|_2^2\). For \(0<\alpha<1\), both penalties are present; if \(\lambda>0\), the objective is \(\lambda(1-\alpha)\)-strongly convex whenever \(L\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixing endpoints recover Lasso and ridge, while interior values combine sparsity-inducing and strongly convex quadratic regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha=1\) gives Lasso, \(\alpha=0\) gives ridge, and \(0<\alpha<1\) gives a mixed penalty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness induced by a positive quadratic coefficient in mixed regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,R:\mathbb{R}^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{dom}R\ne\varnothing\). For \(\lambda_1\ge0\) and \(\lambda_2>0\), define \(F(\beta)=f(\beta)+\lambda_1R(\beta)+(\lambda_2/2)\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2\). Then \(F\) is proper and \(\lambda_2\)-strongly convex. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning of smooth quadratic-loss objectives after ridge regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\lambda_2>0\). For \(q(\beta)=(2n)^{-1}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+(\lambda_2/2)\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2\), the Hessian is \(H=X^{\mathsf T}X/n+\lambda_2I_p\). If \(m\le\lambda_{\min}(X^{\mathsf T}X/n)\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(X^{\mathsf T}X/n)\le L\), where \(0\le m\le L\), then the eigenvalues of \(H\) lie in \([m+\lambda_2,L+\lambda_2]\), and \(\kappa_2(H)\le(L+\lambda_2)/(m+\lambda_2)\). Equality holds when \(m\) and \(L\) are the smallest and largest eigenvalues of \(X^{\mathsf T}X/n\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge regularization shifts every curvature eigenvalue upward, producing a positive smallest eigenvalue and a finite spectral condition number bounded by the shifted spectral bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic regularization restores positive curvature when the design matrix is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(X)<p\), let \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(n\ge1\). The least-squares Hessian \(X^{\mathsf T}X/n\) is singular, so unregularized least squares need not have a unique coefficient vector. For every \(\lambda_2>0\), define \(q_{\lambda_2}(\beta)=(2n)^{-1}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+(\lambda_2/2)\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2\). Its Hessian \(H_{\lambda_2}=X^{\mathsf T}X/n+\lambda_2I_p\) satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}H_{\lambda_2}v\ge\lambda_2\lVert v\rVert_2^2\) for every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and hence \(q_{\lambda_2}\) has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with a rank-deficient design, positive ridge regularization makes the least-squares Hessian positive definite and the coefficient estimate unique.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection–Shrinkage Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate behavior of elastic-net regularization under an orthonormal design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(X^{\mathsf T}X/n=I_p\) and define \(z=X^{\mathsf T}y/n\). For \(\lambda_1\ge0\) and \(\lambda_2\ge0\), the minimizer of \((2n)^{-1}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda_1\lVert\beta\rVert_1+(\lambda_2/2)\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2\) has coordinates \(\widehat\beta_j=S_{\lambda_1}(z_j)/(1+\lambda_2)\), where \(S_t(u)=\operatorname{sign}(u)(|u|-t)_+\). Hence \(\lambda_1\) determines exact zeros, while \(\lambda_2\) continuously contracts every selected coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With orthonormal predictors, the lasso term sets the selection threshold and the quadratic term further shrinks every surviving coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta_j=0\iff |z_j|\le\lambda_1\), while nonzero coordinates are divided by \(1+\lambda_2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate predictors exhibit stable coefficients without identification of a unique sparse support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[x,x]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times2}\) with \(x\ne0\), let \(G=X^{\mathsf T}X/n\), and, for a score \(s\in\mathbb{R}^2\), define \(Q_s(\beta)=\tfrac12\beta^{\mathsf T}G\beta-s^{\mathsf T}\beta+\lambda_1\lVert\beta\rVert_1+(\lambda_2/2)\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2\), where \(\lambda_1\ge0\) and \(\lambda_2>0\). The minimizer \(\widehat\beta(s)\) is unique and satisfies \(\lVert\widehat\beta(s)-\widehat\beta(s')\rVert_2\le\lambda_2^{-1}\lVert s-s'\rVert_2\) for all \(s,s'\in\mathbb{R}^2\). When \(s_1=s_2\), symmetry gives \(\widehat\beta_1(s)=\widehat\beta_2(s)\). If this common value is nonzero, both duplicate variables are selected even though the same fitted direction admits a representation using either variable alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With duplicate predictors, a positive quadratic penalty makes the coefficient solution Lipschitz-stable in the linear score, yet symmetry can select both duplicates and cannot identify a unique one-variable support.
knowledge_statements.title: Stability without Support Identification

children.title: Least-Squares Lasso
