knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Lasso
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-dimensional lasso with squared-error loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), a least-squares lasso estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\right\}.\] The fitted vector \(X\widehat\beta\) is unique, although \(\widehat\beta\) itself may be nonunique when \(X\) is rank deficient. An unpenalized intercept, if present, is represented separately and excluded from \(\lVert\beta\rVert_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-squares lasso minimizes normalized squared error plus an ℓ1 penalty on the regression coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\) belongs to the displayed convex argmin set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical normalized least-squares lasso definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation is a correct finite-dimensional least-squares lasso definition, and the accompanying fitted-value uniqueness qualification is correct. The definition content kind fits the exact leaf. No cited source or inspectable locator is supplied, and the local inventory does not concern lasso regression.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lasso as the Convex Boundary of ℓq-Penalized Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes least-squares lasso through comparison with the q=0 best-subset and q=2 ridge members, including orthonormal-design formulas and the Laplace-prior interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\ge 0\) and \(\lambda>0\), consider \[\min_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac{1}{2N}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p|\beta_j|^q\right\},\] with the \(q=0\) term interpreted as \(\|\beta\|_0\). The cases \(q=0,1,2\) give best-subset selection, lasso, and ridge regression, respectively. For \(0\le q<1\), the penalty and its corresponding constraint region are nonconvex; \(q=1\) is the smallest \(q\) yielding a convex penalty and constraint region. If \(X^TX/N=I\) and \(\widetilde\beta=X^Ty/N\), then the \(q=0,1,2\) solutions act coordinatewise as hard thresholding at \(\sqrt{2\lambda}\), soft thresholding at \(\lambda\), and proportional shrinkage by \((1+2\lambda)^{-1}\), respectively. When the scaled squared-error term is the negative log-likelihood up to constants, an independent Laplace prior \(p(\beta)\propto\exp(-\lambda\|\beta\|_1)\) makes the lasso solution a MAP estimator. This continuous prior does not produce exactly sparse posterior draws, and posterior means are generally not sparse; exact zeros in posterior sampling require prior point mass at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within ℓq-penalized least squares, q=0 gives best-subset selection, q=1 gives lasso, and q=2 gives ridge regression. Penalties below one are nonconvex, making lasso the closest convex member to subset selection. Under a normalized orthonormal design, these three estimators become hard thresholding, soft thresholding, and proportional shrinkage. Lasso is also a MAP estimator under independent Laplace priors, but a continuous Laplace prior does not yield exactly sparse posterior draws; that requires a prior atom at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q=0\Rightarrow\text{best subset and hard thresholding},\quad q=1\Rightarrow\text{lasso, soft thresholding, convex boundary, and Laplace-prior MAP},\quad q=2\Rightarrow\text{ridge and proportional shrinkage};\quad 0\le q<1\Rightarrow\text{nonconvex penalty and constraint region}.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Linear Lasso
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lasso template for canonical generalized linear models with convex negative log-likelihood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let observations be \((x_i,y_i)\) with \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and let \(b:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be a convex log-partition function. For \(\lambda\ge0\), a generalized linear lasso estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(b(x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta)-y_i x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta\bigr)+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\right\}.\] Constants independent of \(\beta\) may be omitted. A separately represented intercept may remain unpenalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized linear lasso combines a convex canonical negative log-likelihood with an ℓ1 coefficient penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^p\) and each \(y_i\) lies in the response domain.
\(b\) is proper and convex on all attained linear predictors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed objective is convex, and \(\widehat\beta\) is any attained minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Weighted Lasso
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted lasso with deterministic, strictly positive coordinate weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:\mathbb{R}^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper convex loss, let \(w_j>0\) be fixed weights, and let \(\lambda\ge0\). A fixed weighted-lasso estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{L(\beta)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p w_j|\beta_j|\right\}.\] Equivalently, with \(D=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_p)\), the penalty is \(\lVert D\beta\rVert_1\). Strict positivity ensures that this penalty is a norm and penalizes every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed weighted lasso assigns a predetermined positive ℓ1 penalty weight to each coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\) minimizes \(L(\beta)+\lambda\lVert D\beta\rVert_1\).

notation.meaning: fixed penalty weight for coordinate j

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Lasso
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage weighted lasso using inverse powers of a pilot estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p\) be a pilot estimate, choose \(\gamma>0\), and define \(w_j=|\widetilde\beta_j|^{-\gamma}\), with \(w_j=+\infty\) when \(\widetilde\beta_j=0\). For a proper convex loss \(L\) and \(\lambda\ge0\), an adaptive-lasso estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{L(\beta)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p w_j|\beta_j|\right\}.\] The extended-value convention \((+\infty)|\beta_j|\) constrains \(\beta_j=0\); regularized weights may instead be specified explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive lasso uses inverse pilot-coefficient magnitudes as ℓ1 weights, penalizing initially small coordinates more heavily.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde\beta\) is a fixed pilot estimate and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\) solves the displayed weighted convex program under the stated extended-value convention.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: adaptive lasso is a weighted lasso with inverse-power pilot weights

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive lasso formulation from a pilot estimate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares adaptive lasso with coordinate weights derived from a pilot coefficient estimate.

\]

children.title: Weight Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Pathologies caused by zero, infinite, unstable, or poorly calibrated weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weight Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero or infinite weights change a weighted lasso from norm regularization to partial penalization or hard constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P_w(\beta)=\sum_{j=1}^p w_j|\beta_j|\), finite weights satisfying \(w_j>0\) make \(P_w\) a norm. If \(w_k=0\), then \(P_w(te_k)=0\) for every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), so the penalty gives no coercive control or shrinkage in coordinate \(k\). If \(w_k=+\infty\) under the extended-value convention, the effective domain requires \(\beta_k=0\). Thus allowing degenerate weights can respectively create unpenalized directions or impose irreversible coordinate deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero weight leaves a coordinate unpenalized, whereas an infinite weight fixes it at zero; neither case is an ordinary weighted norm.
assumptions_latex: \(P_w\) uses the extended-value convention for infinite weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_k=0\) creates a null direction of \(P_w\), while \(w_k=+\infty\) restricts \(\operatorname{dom}P_w\) to \(\{\beta:\beta_k=0\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct consequences of zero and extended-real infinite weights

children.title: Square-Root Lasso
children.top_down_role: Sparse regression using a scale-equivariant residual criterion.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\{\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2/\sqrt n+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square-root lasso template using the residual Euclidean norm rather than squared loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), a square-root lasso estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{\frac{\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2}{\sqrt n}+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\right\}.\] This formulation uses the residual root-mean-square norm and does not introduce a separate noise-scale variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Square-root lasso minimizes the residual root-mean-square norm plus an l1 penalty without introducing a separate noise-scale variable.

children.title: Scaled Lasso
children.top_down_role: Sparse regression with joint coefficient and noise-scale estimation.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Lasso
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint convex estimation of regression coefficients and a positive noise scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), a scaled-lasso pair is any solution of \[ (\widehat\beta,\widehat\sigma)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p,\,\sigma>0}\left\{\frac{\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2}{2n\sigma}+\frac{\sigma}{2}+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\right\}. \] The objective is jointly convex on \(\sigma>0\). For any fixed \(\beta\) with nonzero residual, minimizing over \(\sigma\) gives \(\sigma=\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2/\sqrt n\), reducing the profiled objective to the square-root-lasso form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled lasso jointly estimates coefficients and noise scale; profiling out the scale produces the square-root-lasso objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\sigma=\lVert y-X\widehat\beta\rVert_2/\sqrt n\) whenever the optimal residual is nonzero.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: perspective formulation of squared loss and its scale profile
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perspective objective is jointly convex on the positive-scale domain, and profiling a fixed coefficient vector with nonzero residual gives the stated residual scale and square-root-lasso objective. The definition kind fits the leaf. No relevant cited source or inspectable locator supports the scaled-lasso formulation.

children.title: Noise-Scale Calibration
children.top_down_role: Tuning interpretation under unknown or estimated noise scale.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda\) may be calibrated from the distribution of \(\lVert X^\top\varepsilon\rVert_\infty/(\sqrt n\lVert\varepsilon\rVert_2)\), without knowing \(\sigma\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scale-free score calibration for square-root-type Lasso losses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pivotal calibration for the square-root-loss convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\{\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2/\sqrt n+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\}\). At the true coefficient, the normalized loss gradient is \(-X^\top\varepsilon/(\sqrt n\lVert\varepsilon\rVert_2)\), which is independent of the multiplicative noise scale \(\sigma\). Hence a noise-scale-free choice is any \(\lambda\) satisfying \(\mathbb P\{\lVert X^\top\varepsilon\rVert_\infty/(\sqrt n\lVert\varepsilon\rVert_2)\leq\lambda\}\geq1-\alpha\) for a prescribed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Square-root-loss Lasso can calibrate its penalty from a normalized noise score whose distribution does not depend on the unknown noise standard deviation.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Scale Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scale cancellation and normalized gradient are correct for the stated square-root-loss convention, but the calibration probability requires an inspectable specialized source and clarification of whether it is conditional on a fixed design or taken under a joint design-noise law.

children.title: Domain-Constrained Lasso
children.top_down_role: Lasso formulations combined with sign, box, simplex, or related domain restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained Lasso is a convex optimization problem, and any minimizer belongs to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares Lasso with an additional closed convex coefficient domain.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.3 Constrained Minimization p. 50

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The domain-constrained Lasso formulation is \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in C}\left\{\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\right\}.\] Equivalently, it minimizes the same objective plus the indicator \(\delta_C(\beta)\). Choices such as \(C=\mathbb R_+^p\), a coordinate box, or the simplex \(\{\beta\geq0:\mathbf1^\top\beta=1\}\) impose sign, bound, or compositional restrictions while preserving convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain-constrained Lasso adds a closed convex coefficient restriction, such as nonnegativity, box bounds, or simplex membership, to the usual penalized least-squares objective.

children.title: Sorted L1 Penalties
children.top_down_role: Coordinate penalties indexed by ranked coefficient magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_\lambda\) is convex; it is a norm exactly when \(\lambda_1>0\).

notation.meaning: coordinates of absolute coefficient values sorted nonincreasingly

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: ordered nonnegative weights define the standard sorted L1 functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sorted L1 penalty with nonincreasing nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), let \(|b|_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq|b|_{(p)}\) be the decreasing rearrangement of \((|b_1|,\ldots,|b_p|)\). The sorted L1 functional associated with \(\lambda\) is \[J_\lambda(b)=\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j|b|_{(j)}.\] Under the stated ordering of the weights, \(J_\lambda\) is convex, permutation invariant, and sign invariant. It is a norm if and only if \(\lambda_1>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sorted L1 penalty weights coefficient magnitudes according to rank rather than coordinate identity; decreasing nonnegative weights make it convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Sorted L1 Penalties

children.title: SLOPE Formulations
children.top_down_role: Sorted-penalty formulations associated with sparse estimation and selection control.

knowledge_statements.title: SLOPE Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical least-squares SLOPE formulation and its parameter-dependent constrained counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(J_\lambda(\beta)=\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j|\beta|_{(j)}\). A SLOPE estimator is any \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+J_\lambda(\beta)\right\}.\] If \(\widehat\beta\) solves this problem and \(t=J_\lambda(\widehat\beta)\), then \(\widehat\beta\) also solves \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\ \frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad J_\lambda(\beta)\leq t.\] Conversely, a constrained solution corresponds to a penalized solution when the constraint admits an appropriate nonnegative optimal multiplier; the multiplier is the penalty coefficient for the chosen loss normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SLOPE minimizes normalized least-squares loss plus a sorted L1 penalty. A penalized solution also solves the constrained problem at its attained penalty value, while the converse requires an appropriate constraint multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\) minimizes a convex sorted-L1-regularized least-squares objective and, with \(t=J_\lambda(\widehat\beta)\), the corresponding constrained objective.

notation.meaning: constraint level for the sorted L1 functional

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical penalized least-squares SLOPE formulation

children.title: Rank-Weight Calibration
children.top_down_role: Choices of ordered weight sequences and their structural consequences.

assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is the standard normal distribution function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \(\lambda_j=c\Phi^{-1}(1-qj/(2p))\) is nonincreasing and nonnegative whenever \(qj/(2p)\leq1/2\).

notation.meaning: positive scaling constant matching the loss convention

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Gaussian quantile rank weights are a standard SLOPE calibration template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian quantile calibration; scaling depends on the objective normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Gaussian rank-weight calibration takes \[\lambda_j=c\,\Phi^{-1}\!\left(1-\frac{qj}{2p}\right),\qquad j=1,\ldots,p,\] where \(c>0\) matches the noise and loss normalization. Because \(j\mapsto1-qj/(2p)\) is nonincreasing and \(\Phi^{-1}\) is increasing, the resulting weights are nonincreasing. The factor \(c\) must be altered when the least-squares loss, column norms, or noise scale use a different convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard SLOPE calibration uses decreasing Gaussian upper quantiles, with an overall scale chosen to match the loss, design, and noise normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Weight Calibration

notation.meaning: cone of ordered nonnegative weight sequences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible weights for convex rank-ordered coordinate penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordered weight system of length \(p\) is a vector \(\lambda\in\Lambda_p\), where \[\Lambda_p=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p:\lambda_1\geq\lambda_2\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_p\geq0\}.\] For the associated functional \(J_\lambda(b)=\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j|b|_{(j)}\), equal adjacent weights make the penalty insensitive to rank exchanges within the corresponding block, while strict decreases distinguish adjacent ranks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered weight systems are nonnegative, nonincreasing sequences; equal weights merge rank effects, while strict decreases distinguish neighboring ranks.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Weight Systems

children.title: Permutation-Tie Geometry
children.top_down_role: Solution structure associated with coefficient ordering and equal magnitudes.

children.title: Coefficient-Magnitude Ties
children.top_down_role: Geometric regimes containing equal absolute coefficient values.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Magnitude Ties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient geometry of a maximal nonzero coefficient-magnitude tie block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a maximal set of indices satisfying \(|b_i|=a>0\), and let \(R\) be the complete set of ranks occupied by these tied magnitudes. Writing \(s_i=\operatorname{sign}(b_i)\) for \(i\in B\), the restriction of the sorted-L1 subdifferential to \(B\) is \[\left\{g_B:g_i=s_i u_i,\ (u_i)_{i\in B}\in\operatorname{conv}\left\{(\lambda_{\pi(i)})_{i\in B}:\pi:B\to R\text{ is a bijection}\right\}\right\}.\] Thus the block subgradient permits every assignment of the occupied rank weights to the tied coordinates and every convex mixture of those assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a maximal block of equal nonzero coefficient magnitudes, the sorted-L1 subgradient convexly mixes all assignments of the block's complete set of rank weights, with coordinate signs restored afterward.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is a maximal magnitude-tie block with \(|b_i|=a>0\) for all \(i\in B\).
\(R\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is the complete rank set occupied by \((|b_i|)_{i\in B}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block subgradients are the signed convex hull of all bijective assignments of \((\lambda_j)_{j\in R}\) to the coordinates in \(B\).

notation.meaning: maximal indices sharing one nonzero coefficient magnitude
complete rank set occupied by the tie block
sign of the tied coefficient at coordinate i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: subdifferential of a maximum of finitely many weighted linear forms

children.title: Permutation Symmetry
children.top_down_role: Invariance under coordinate reorderings compatible with ranked penalties.

assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) is a permutation matrix.
\(D\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) is diagonal with entries in \(\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_\lambda(PDb)=J_\lambda(b)\) for every \(b\in\mathbb R^p\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sorting absolute coordinates is invariant under signed permutations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed-permutation invariance of sorted coordinate penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), the vectors \(b\) and \(PDb\) have the same multiset of coordinate magnitudes. Consequently their decreasing rearrangements coincide and \[J_\lambda(PDb)=\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j|(PDb)|_{(j)}=\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j|b|_{(j)}=J_\lambda(b).\] Hence every sublevel set \(\{b:J_\lambda(b)\leq t\}\) is invariant under the signed-permutation group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorted L1 penalties and their sublevel sets are unchanged by coordinate permutations or sign changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Permutation Symmetry

children.title: Tie-Induced Faces
children.top_down_role: Faces and strata arising from shared coefficient ranks.

knowledge_statements.title: Tie-Induced Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral cell intersections produced by nonzero coefficient-magnitude ties under strictly decreasing sorted weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\cdots>\lambda_p>0\). On each region with a fixed coordinate-sign pattern and strict ordering of the coordinate magnitudes, \(J_\lambda\) agrees with one linear form. If two adjacent nonzero magnitudes tie, the point lies in the intersection of the closures of the two neighboring ordering regions, and the corresponding distinct linear forms agree there. At a boundary point satisfying \(J_\lambda(b)=c\) with \(c>0\), this tie lies on the intersection of the corresponding facets of the polytope \(\{u\in\mathbb R^p:J_\lambda(u)\leq c\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With strictly decreasing positive rank weights, sorted L1 penalties are linear on strict signed-ordering regions. A nonzero adjacent magnitude tie lies where neighboring regions and their corresponding sublevel-set facets meet.

children.title: Coefficient Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact singleton criterion using the common fit and KKT face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the lasso, all minimizers have a common fitted value \(\widehat f\) and residual \(\widehat r=y-\widehat f\). Put \(E=\{j:|X_j^{\mathsf T}\widehat r|=\lambda\}\) and \(z_E=X_E^{\mathsf T}\widehat r/\lambda\). The complete coefficient solution set is \[\mathcal S=\{\beta:\beta_{E^c}=0,\ X_E\beta_E=\widehat f,\ z_j\beta_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\in E\}.\] Consequently, the lasso coefficients are unique exactly when \(\mathcal S\) is a singleton. In particular, full column rank of \(X_E\) is sufficient for coefficient uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficients are unique exactly when the KKT-compatible coefficients producing the common fit form a singleton; full rank of the equicorrelation design suffices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\text{ is unique}\iff |\mathcal S|=1\); in particular, \(\operatorname{rank}(X_E)=|E|\Rightarrow |\mathcal S|=1\).

children.title: Fitted-Value Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.title: Fitted-Value Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of lasso predictions despite possible coefficient nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat\beta^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat\beta^{(2)}\) minimize \(\tfrac12\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\) with \(\lambda>0\). Then their fitted values coincide: \[X\widehat\beta^{(1)}=X\widehat\beta^{(2)}.\] Hence the optimal residual and every correlation \(X_j^{\mathsf T}(y-X\widehat\beta)\) are also unique. The conclusion follows from strict convexity of squared loss as a function of the fitted value, although the objective need not be strictly convex as a function of \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any two lasso minimizers produce the same prediction, residual, and residual correlations, even when their coefficient vectors differ.
assumptions_latex: Both coefficient vectors are global minimizers of the same squared-loss lasso problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\widehat\beta^{(1)}=X\widehat\beta^{(2)}\).

knowledge_statements.title: General-Position Designs

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Designs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate predictors create coefficient nonuniqueness while preserving prediction uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[x\ x]\) with \(x\ne0\), and suppose \(x^{\mathsf T}y>\lambda>0\). Define \(s^*=(x^{\mathsf T}y-\lambda)/\lVert x\rVert_2^2\). For every \(t\in[0,s^*]\), the vector \(\beta(t)=(t,s^*-t)\) minimizes \(\tfrac12\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\). These minimizers are distinct but all satisfy \(X\beta(t)=xs^*\). Thus duplicated columns can destroy coefficient uniqueness without destroying fitted-value uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With two identical predictors, a positive optimal coefficient can be split continuously between them, yielding distinct coefficients but one common prediction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(t,s^*-t):0\le t\le s^*\}\) is a nontrivial set of minimizers with common fit \(xs^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Angle Regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical LARS construction for a least-squares coefficient path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input centered \(y\) and standardized columns of \(X\). Initialize \(\beta=0\), residual \(r=y\), and active set \(A=\varnothing\). Add a variable attaining \(\max_j|X_j^{\mathsf T}r|\), recording its correlation sign. Move \(X\beta\) in the equiangular direction generated by the signed active columns, choosing the largest step before an inactive absolute correlation ties the active correlations. Add the tying variable and repeat. Stop when all variables are active, the residual is zero, or a prescribed path endpoint is reached; output the successive knots and linear segments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LARS repeatedly joins the most correlated variable and moves in an equiangular active direction until the next correlation tie.
assumptions_latex: The response and predictors are centered, and nonzero predictors are standardized.
Ties are resolved by a specified deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the knot sequence and piecewise-linear least-angle coefficient path.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Least-angle regression path procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative characterization of the standardized least-angle regression path construction and its dimensional stopping boundary; it does not establish generic equivalence with every lasso path variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the presented least-angle regression procedure, set \(\beta=0\) and activate a predictor having maximal absolute correlation with the residual. Move its coefficient toward its least-squares value until an inactive predictor attains the same absolute residual correlation; thereafter move the active coefficients jointly so that their absolute residual correlations remain tied and decrease, adding predictors at successive knots. When all predictors enter, the procedure ends at the full least-squares fit. With centered data accounting for an intercept, if \(p>N-1\), it instead reaches a zero-residual solution after \(N-1\) steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-angle regression starts from zero coefficients and activates a predictor with maximal absolute residual correlation. Its coefficient moves toward the least-squares value until another predictor catches up; active coefficients then move jointly while their absolute residual correlations remain tied and decrease. Predictors join at successive knots. The process ends at the full least-squares fit when all predictors enter, while centered data with an intercept and p greater than N−1 reach zero residual after N−1 steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Entry Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT boundary condition for an inactive variable entering a lasso path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a lasso path segment with active set \(A\), let \(r(\lambda)=y-X_A\beta_A(\lambda)\), where \(\beta_A(\lambda)\) is affine. An inactive index \(j\notin A\) is eligible to enter at the next penalty \(\lambda_*\) exactly when \[|X_j^{\mathsf T}r(\lambda_*)|=\lambda_*\] and \(|X_j^{\mathsf T}r(\lambda)|<\lambda\) immediately before the event along the decreasing-\(\lambda\) path. Its entering sign is \(\operatorname{sign}(X_j^{\mathsf T}r(\lambda_*))\). The next entry is the first admissible boundary hit among inactive indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inactive variable enters when its residual correlation first reaches the dual boundary as the penalty decreases; the correlation determines its sign.
assumptions_latex: The squared-loss lasso path is followed with decreasing \(\lambda>0\).
The current active coefficients and residual are affine on the open segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j\) enters only at a first boundary hit \(|X_j^{\mathsf T}r(\lambda_*)|=\lambda_*\).

children.title: Variable-Exit Events

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Exit Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-crossing condition for removing an active lasso variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a lasso path segment with fixed active set \(A\) and signs, write \(\beta_A(\lambda)=a-\lambda d\). An index \(i\in A\) has an exit event at an admissible penalty \(\lambda_*\) when \[a_i-\lambda_*d_i=0\] and this is the first zero reached by an active coefficient as \(\lambda\) decreases along the segment. At the knot, remove \(i\) from the active set before continuing so that coefficient signs remain compatible with the lasso KKT subgradient. If \(d_i\ne0\), its candidate exit value is \(\lambda_*=a_i/d_i\), subject to lying in the current interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active variable exits when its affine coefficient first reaches zero; removing it prevents continuation with a KKT-incompatible sign.
assumptions_latex: The squared-loss lasso path is followed with decreasing \(\lambda>0\).
The active coefficients have the affine form \(\beta_A(\lambda)=a-\lambda d\) on the current segment.

children.title: Sign-Change Events
children.top_down_role: Path locations associated with coefficient sign transitions.

assumptions_latex: On an open interval adjacent to \(\lambda_0>0\), the selected solution branch is continuous and each active coefficient is affine in \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_0\) is a sign-change event for coordinate \(j\) when \(\widehat\beta_j(\lambda_0)=0\) and there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\widehat\beta_j(\lambda_0-	au)\widehat\beta_j(\lambda_0+\tau)<0\) for every sufficiently small \(\tau\in(0,\varepsilon)\). Such an event is necessarily a path knot: the signed active-set description cannot remain constant across \(\lambda_0\). Under a convention that removes a coordinate immediately upon reaching zero, the same zero crossing is represented as an exit followed, possibly at the same knot, by re-entry with the opposite sign.

notation.meaning: A selected lasso solution branch at penalty level \(\lambda\).

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports lasso path sign-change calculus.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a continuous selected branch; nonunique lasso solutions require an explicit branch convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the lasso path, a sign-change event is a zero crossing of an active coefficient along a continuous selected solution branch. Precisely, \(\lambda_0\) is such an event for coordinate \(j\) if \(\widehat\beta_j(\lambda_0)=0\) and the one-sided nonzero values have opposite signs. Because an active sign is part of the local KKT regime, the signed active set changes at \(\lambda_0\), making \(\lambda_0\) a knot. If the path algorithm deletes coefficients at zero, the crossing is encoded by exit and opposite-sign re-entry rather than by retaining the coordinate through zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sign-change event occurs when a selected lasso coefficient crosses zero; it is a knot and may be encoded as exit followed by opposite-sign re-entry.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Change Events

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but no citation supports the claims that every sign crossing is a knot or that deletion conventions encode it as exit and re-entry.

children.title: Simultaneous Events
children.top_down_role: Path locations containing multiple coincident support changes.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and a lasso solution branch \(\widehat\beta(\lambda)\) is selected.
Candidate entry and exit times are computed from the same current affine KKT segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An event at \(\lambda_0\) is simultaneous when the set \(E(\lambda_0)\cup L(\lambda_0)\) contains at least two distinct coordinates, where \(E(\lambda_0)\) contains inactive coordinates satisfying \(\lvert X_j^{\mathsf T}(y-X\widehat\beta(\lambda_0))/n\rvert=\lambda_0\), and \(L(\lambda_0)\) contains active coordinates satisfying \(\widehat\beta_j(\lambda_0)=0\). Every tied condition must be imposed in determining the next KKT regime; processing tied coordinates in an arbitrary sequential order may select a branch not determined by the event data alone.

notation.meaning: Coordinates eligible to enter at the event.
Active coordinates reaching zero at the event.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports simultaneous lasso path events.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers tied entry and exit conditions on a selected lasso path branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a current affine segment of the lasso path, let \(E(\lambda_0)\) be the inactive coordinates whose KKT correlations reach magnitude \(\lambda_0\), and let \(L(\lambda_0)\) be the active coordinates whose coefficients reach zero. The knot \(\lambda_0\) is a simultaneous event exactly when \(\lvert E(\lambda_0)\cup L(\lambda_0)\rvert\ge 2\). The post-event active set and signs must satisfy all tied KKT equalities and inequalities together. Consequently, a one-coordinate-at-a-time tie-breaking rule is an additional branch-selection convention and is not intrinsic to the simultaneous event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous event is a knot where at least two entry or exit conditions tie; all tied KKT conditions must be resolved together.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Events

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope fit, but the simultaneous-event and branch-selection assertions require a specific lasso path source.

children.title: Path Knots
children.top_down_role: Breakpoint organization across piecewise path segments.

assumptions_latex: A solution selection \(\widehat\beta(\lambda)\in S(\lambda)\) is fixed when coefficient-level path features are discussed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A value \(\lambda_0>0\) is a path knot if no neighborhood \(I\) of \(\lambda_0\) admits one constant signed active set for which \(\widehat\beta(\lambda)\) is affine in \(\lambda\) on all of \(I\). Equivalently for a nondegenerate classical lasso path, \(\lambda_0\) is an endpoint of a maximal affine segment and is caused by an entry, exit, sign change, or tie among such events. Between consecutive knots, the active set and active signs are constant.

notation.meaning: The lasso solution set at penalty \(\lambda\).
A positive penalty value marking a candidate knot.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the lasso path-knot characterization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines knots for the classical squared-loss lasso after fixing a coefficient-path selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the squared-loss lasso, a path knot is a penalty value \(\lambda_0>0\) at which the selected coefficient path cannot be represented on a full neighborhood of \(\lambda_0\) by one affine formula with a constant signed active set. Under nondegeneracy, knots are precisely the endpoints of maximal affine path segments and arise when a KKT event changes the active set or its signs. Thus, on every open interval between consecutive knots, \(\widehat\beta(\lambda)\) is affine in \(\lambda\), while its derivative or signed active-set description changes at a knot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path knot is a penalty value separating maximal affine lasso segments, typically where an entry, exit, sign change, or tied event occurs.

children.title: Nonlinear Path Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regularization paths lacking classical piecewise-linear structure.

assumptions_latex: \(L:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and twice continuously differentiable on the relevant active-coordinate region.
\(\widehat\beta(\lambda)\) locally minimizes \(L(\beta)+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\) with fixed active set \(A\) and sign vector \(s_A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The active coefficients satisfy \(
abla_A L(\widehat eta(\lambda))+\lambda s_A=0\) and hence \( rac{d}{d\lambda}\widehat eta_A(\lambda)=-[
abla^2_{AA}L(\widehat eta(\lambda))]^{-1}s_A\). Therefore the segment is generally nonlinear whenever the active Hessian varies with \(\widehat eta(\lambda)\). It is affine on the regime if the vector \([
abla^2_{AA}L(\widehat eta(lambda))]^{-1}s_A\) is constant there, as occurs for quadratic loss with a fixed active set.

notation.meaning: Active coordinate set on the local regime.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports regularization-path differentiation for nonquadratic loss.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes smooth nonquadratic loss with locally fixed support and signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within a regime having fixed active set \(A\) and signs \(s_A\), the KKT equation for \(L(\beta)+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\) is \(\nabla_A L(\widehat\beta(\lambda))+lambda s_A=0\). If the active Hessian is nonsingular, implicit differentiation gives \(\widehat\beta_A'(\lambda)=-[\nabla^2_{AA}L(\widehat\beta(\lambda))]^{-1}s_A\). Hence a varying active Hessian generally produces a curved, rather than piecewise-affine, regularization path. Quadratic loss is the special case in which the active Hessian is constant and each fixed-sign regime is affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With smooth nonquadratic loss, the active-path derivative depends on the changing Hessian, so fixed-support path segments are generally curved rather than affine.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Path Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but several occurrences of lambda lack a backslash, and variation of the Hessian alone does not necessarily imply variation of its inverse applied to the fixed sign vector. A source is needed for the precise path-differentiation claim.

children.title: Set-Valued Paths
children.top_down_role: Parameter ranges admitting multiple coefficient solutions.

assumptions_latex: For every \(\lambda>0\), the minimum of \(F(\beta)+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularization path is the multifunction \(S:(0,\infty)\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^p\) defined by \(S(\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\{F(\beta)+lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\}\). It is set-valued at \(\lambda_0\) exactly when there exist distinct \(\beta^1,beta^2\u0000in S(\lambda_0)\). Convexity implies that \(S(\lambda_0)\) is convex, so the entire segment \(t\beta^1+(1-t)beta^2\), \(t\in[0,1]\), also consists of minimizers. Any coefficient path is therefore a selection \(\widehat\beta(lambda)in S(\lambda)\), not the multifunction itself.

notation.meaning: The minimizer multifunction indexed by the penalty.
A single-valued selection from the solution set.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports set-valued regularization paths.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treats nonuniqueness through the argmin multifunction rather than an unspecified coefficient selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex loss \(F\), the regularization path is naturally the argmin multifunction \(S(lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\{F(\beta)+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\}\). The path is set-valued at \(\lambda_0\) when \(S(\lambda_0)\) contains two or more distinct coefficient vectors. Because the objective is convex, every attained solution set \(S(\lambda)\) is convex. A plotted or algorithmically traced coefficient path \(\widehat\beta(lambda)\) is a selection satisfying \(\widehat\beta(\lambda)in S(\lambda)\); properties of that selection need not be intrinsic to the full solution multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued regularization path maps each penalty to its entire convex minimizer set; any displayed coefficient curve is only a selection from it.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Paths

children.title: Branch Selection
children.top_down_role: Choices among admissible solution branches along a nonunique path.

assumptions_latex: The minimizer set \(S(\lambda)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) is nonempty and closed for every penalty under consideration.
A reference point \(b(\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^p\) and a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(W\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Define \(\widehat\beta(lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in S(lambda)}\frac12\lVert\beta-b(lambda)\rVert_W^2\), where \(\lVert u\rVert_W^2=u^{\mathsf T}Wu\). Since \(S(lambda)\) is closed and convex and the tie-break objective is strongly convex, this minimizer exists whenever the displayed problem is coercive and is unique. Thus the rule defines a single-valued branch. Choosing \(b(lambda)\) as the preceding branch value gives a continuation rule; choosing \(b(lambda)=0\) gives a minimum-W-norm rule. Different rules may produce different coefficient branches while preserving optimality.

notation.meaning: The full minimizer set at penalty \(\lambda\).
Reference point used to select a branch.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this explicit branch-selection construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a deterministic strongly convex tie-break over each convex solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty closed convex solution set \(S(lambda)\), select a coefficient branch by solving \(\widehat\beta(lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in S(lambda)}\frac12\lVert\beta-b(lambda)\rVert_W^2\), with \(W\) positive definite. The tie-break objective is strongly convex, so its minimizer over \(S(lambda)\) is unique whenever it is attained. For path continuation, initialize at a penalty with a known solution and, at each subsequent penalty, set \(b(lambda)\) equal to the previously selected coefficient vector. Output the resulting selection \(\widehat\beta(lambda)in S(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique branch can be selected by minimizing a strongly convex distance over each solution set, using either zero or the preceding solution as reference.
knowledge_statements.title: Branch Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is suitable for this leaf, but lambda notation is malformed and the preceding-solution continuation rule lacks a discretization or ordering specification. The construction has no cited source.

children.title: Path Discontinuities
children.top_down_role: Abrupt changes arising from parameterization, selection conventions, or degeneracy.

assumptions_latex: \(S:(0,\infty)\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^p\) is the nonempty solution multifunction of a regularized convex problem.
A single-valued selection \(\widehat\beta(lambda)in S(\lambda)\) has been chosen.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected path is discontinuous at \(\lambda_0\) if there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and a sequence \(\lambda_k\to\u0000lambda_0\) such that \(\lVert\widehat\beta(lambda_k)-widehat\beta(lambda_0)\rVert_2\ge\u0000varepsilon\) for all \(k\). Such a jump may be caused solely by branch selection when \(S(lambda_0)\) or nearby solution sets are non-singleton; it does not by itself establish discontinuity of the multifunction. For squared-loss lasso, all minimizers have the same fitted value \(X\beta\), so a coefficient-selection jump can occur without a jump in fitted values.

notation.meaning: Penalty value at which continuity is tested.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports discontinuities of selected regularization paths.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates discontinuity of a coefficient selection from behavior of the full solution set and fitted-value path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A selected regularization path \(\widehat\beta(lambda)in S(\lambda)\) has a discontinuity at \(\lambda_0\) when some sequence \(\lambda_k\to\u0000lambda_0\) keeps \(\widehat\beta(lambda_k)\) a positive distance from \(\widehat\beta(lambda_0)\). Nonuniqueness is the principal boundary: changing between admissible branches can create a coefficient jump even when the solution multifunction has well-behaved limiting sets. In the squared-loss lasso, strict convexity in the fitted value implies that all minimizers share \(X\beta\); consequently, discontinuity of an arbitrary coefficient selection need not imply discontinuity of predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient branch jumps when nearby selected solutions stay a positive distance apart; under nonuniqueness this may reflect tie-breaking rather than prediction discontinuity.
knowledge_statements.title: Path Discontinuities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the record contains malformed notation and null characters. The distinction between selection discontinuity, multifunction continuity, and fitted-value continuity also needs a precise source and continuity notion.

children.title: Prediction Guarantees

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(\Delta=\widehat\beta-beta^\star\), the lasso basic inequality implies \(\Delta\) belongs to the stated cone and \[\frac1n\lVert X\Delta\rVert_2^2\le\u00009\,\frac{lambda^2s}{phi_0^2}.\] Thus the in-sample mean squared prediction error is controlled at order \(\lambda^2s/phi_0^2\) on the noise event.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=X\beta^\star+varepsilon\), with true support \(S\) of size \(s\), and let \(\widehat\beta\) be the lasso estimator. Suppose \(\lVert X^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon/n\rVert_infty\le\u0000lambda/2\) and the compatibility inequality \(\lVert\delta_S\rVert_1\le\u0000sqrt{s}\lVert X\delta\rVert_2/(sqrt n\phi_0)\) holds whenever \(\lVert\delta_{S^c}\rVert_1\le 3\lVert\delta_S\rVert_1\). Then \(\Delta=widehat\beta-beta^\star\) lies in this cone and satisfies \(\lVert X\Delta\rVert_2^2/n\le 9\lambda^2s/phi_0^2\).

children.title: Oracle Guarantee Interfaces

assumptions_latex: \(y=f^star+varepsilon\) with fixed design \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), and \(\widehat\beta\) is a regularized estimator.
A comparator \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\) has support \(T=operatorname{supp}(b)\), and a restricted-curvature constant \(\phi(T)>0\) is available.
The score-noise event required by the estimator holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An oracle guarantee interface is an inequality of the form \[\frac1n\lVert X\widehat\beta-f^star\rVert_2^2\le C_1\frac1n\lVert Xb-f^star\rVert_2^2+C_2\frac{lambda^2|T|}{phi(T)^2}\quad\text{for every admissible }b.\] Taking the infimum over admissible comparators separates approximation error from a sparsity-and-curvature estimation price. The constants \(C_1,C_2\), comparator class, noise event, and definition of \(\phi(T)\) are mandatory parts of any instantiated oracle inequality.

notation.meaning: Comparator coefficient vector and its support.

review_flags: This is a guarantee template; a matching source is needed for any instantiated constants and curvature definition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the approximation-plus-estimation structure required of a fixed-design oracle inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed-design prediction, an oracle guarantee compares the estimator with every admissible sparse vector \(b\). Its canonical interface is \(\lVert X\widehat\beta-f^star\rVert_2^2/n\le C_1\lVert Xb-f^star\rVert_2^2/n+C_2\lambda^2|operatorname{supp}(b)|/phi(operatorname{supp}(b))^2\). The first term is comparator approximation error; the second is the estimation price determined by penalty, sparsity, and restricted curvature. An instantiated guarantee must specify the comparator class, score-noise event, curvature definition, and constants before taking the infimum over \(b\).

children.title: Support-Recovery Interfaces

assumptions_latex: \(\beta^star\in\mathbb{R}^p\) has support \(S\), and \(\widehat\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p\) is an estimator.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact support recovery means \(\widehat S_0=S\); exact signed-support recovery means \(\operatorname{sign}(widehat\beta_j)=operatorname{sign}(beta_j^\star)\) for every \(j\), using \(\operatorname{sign}(0)=0\). Approximate recovery at threshold \(\tau\) may be reported by the false-positive count \(\lvert\widehat S_tau\setminus S\rvert\), false-negative count \(\lvert S\setminus\widehat S_tau\rvert\), or symmetric-difference loss \(\lvert\widehat S_tau\triangle S\rvert\). A theorem claiming recovery must specify which predicate or loss is controlled, the threshold, and whether its conclusion is deterministic or probabilistic.

notation.meaning: induced maximum-row-sum norm, or vector maximum norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes uniform and sign-specific fixed-design Lasso versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The uniform irrepresentability condition for support \(S\) holds with margin \(\eta\) if \[\|\Sigma_{S^cS}\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}\|_\infty\leq1-\eta.\] For recovery of a fixed signed coefficient vector with \(z_S=\operatorname{sign}(\beta_S^\star)\), the weaker sign-specific condition is \[\|\Sigma_{S^cS}\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}z_S\|_\infty\leq1-\eta.\] These predicates bound the regression of inactive variables on active variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inactive variables must not be too representable by active variables, either uniformly over active signs or only for the target sign pattern.
knowledge_statements.title: Irrepresentability Conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform and sign-specific formulas are plausible fixed-design irrepresentability conditions, and the condition kind fits the terminal container. However, no authoritative model-selection source or specific locator is supplied to establish the norm convention, margins, and relationship between the two variants.

children.title: Mutual Incoherence Conditions
children.top_down_role: Pairwise correlation controls used in sparse recovery interfaces.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu:=\max_{j\neq k}|x_j^\top x_k|/n<1/(2s-1)\).

notation.meaning: mutual coherence of the normalized design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized fixed-design coherence condition at sparsity level \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The design satisfies mutual incoherence at sparsity level \(s\) when its normalized columns obey \[\mu:=\max_{j\neq k}\frac{|x_j^\top x_k|}{n}<\frac{1}{2s-1}.\] More generally, a coherence bound records \(\mu\leq\bar\mu\); the displayed threshold is the standard uniform separation regime used to control every support of cardinality at most \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After column normalization, every distinct pair has small correlation; the threshold below one over twice the sparsity minus one gives uniform separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Mutual Incoherence Conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized mutual-coherence quantity is well defined and the condition kind fits the terminal container. The threshold 1/(2s-1) is a particular sufficient sparse-recovery or separation regime rather than the definition of mutual coherence itself, so its stated role requires an authoritative sparse-recovery citation with a precise locator.

children.title: Condition Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Relative strength, compatibility, and use cases of separation conditions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\Sigma_{S^cS}\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}\|_\infty\leq s\mu/[1-(s-1)\mu]\); hence \(\mu<1/(2s-1)\) implies uniform irrepresentability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient implication from pairwise coherence to uniform irrepresentability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every support \(S\) of size \(s\), diagonal dominance gives \(\|\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}\|_\infty\leq[1-(s-1)\mu]^{-1}\), while \(\|\Sigma_{S^cS}\|_\infty\leq s\mu\). Consequently, \[\|\Sigma_{S^cS}\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}\|_\infty\leq\frac{s\mu}{1-(s-1)\mu}.\] Thus \(\mu<1/(2s-1)\) implies a positive uniform irrepresentability margin. The converse need not hold because irrepresentability is support-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently small pairwise coherence guarantees uniform irrepresentability, but support-specific irrepresentability can hold even when global coherence is too large.
knowledge_statements.title: Condition Comparisons

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed implication from pairwise coherence to uniform irrepresentability is mathematically plausible under the stated unit-diagonal and coherence assumptions. It is a comparison theorem or sufficient-condition result rather than merely an intrinsic property, although the selected property kind is not irreconcilable with the comparison container. No source or locator supports the inverse-norm bound, implication, or nonconverse claim.

children.title: Support-Identification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Design regimes where separation conditions cease to support reliable identification.

assumptions_latex: \(a\neq0\), and the observation law depends on \(\beta\) only through \(X\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{(a,0)}=P_{(0,a)}\), so no estimator can identify both supports \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2\}\) with probability exceeding \(1/2\) uniformly over these two parameters.

notation.meaning: data distribution under coefficient vector beta

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonidentifiability boundary caused by duplicate design columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta^{(1)}=(a,0,\ldots,0)\) and \(\beta^{(2)}=(0,a,0,\ldots,0)\). Since \(x_1=x_2\), one has \(X\beta^{(1)}=X\beta^{(2)}\), hence \(P_{\beta^{(1)}}=P_{\beta^{(2)}}\). For every support estimator \(\widehat S\), \[\min\!\left\{P_{\beta^{(1)}}(\widehat S=\{1\}),P_{\beta^{(2)}}(\widehat S=\{2\})\right\}\leq\frac12.\] Exact uniform support identification is therefore impossible without a design-separation assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate columns make two different singleton supports observationally indistinguishable, so no method can recover both supports uniformly with success probability above one half.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Identification Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the indistinguishability argument is plausible when the full observation distribution depends on beta only through X beta. A specific statistical model class and an authoritative information-theoretic locator are still needed to support the equality of laws and the uniform one-half bound.

children.title: Group Lasso Template
children.top_down_role: Block-sparse formulations over predefined coordinate groups.

children.title: Disjoint Group Lasso
children.top_down_role: Block selection over a coordinate partition.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\{L(\beta)+\lambda\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\|\beta_{G_g}\|_2\}\).

notation.meaning: coordinate block indexed by group g

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex group Lasso for a disjoint coordinate partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The disjoint group Lasso estimator is any solution of \[\widehat\beta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{L(\beta)+\lambda\Omega_w(\beta)\right\},\qquad \Omega_w(\beta):=\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\|\beta_{G_g}\|_2.\] Because the groups form a partition, \(\Omega_w\) is a norm. Its blockwise Euclidean terms encourage entire blocks \(\widehat\beta_{G_g}\) to equal zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint group Lasso minimizes a convex loss plus a weighted sum of Euclidean norms over a coordinate partition, promoting selection of whole blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjoint Group Lasso

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the disjoint-group-Lasso container, and the objective is internally consistent for a coordinate partition with positive weights. No authoritative group-Lasso source or specific definition/page locator is supplied for the formulation and block-selection interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Grouped-lasso multinomial logistic formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multinomial-logistic specialization of disjoint group lasso, with each predictor's coefficients across classes forming one group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K>2\), define \(\beta_j=(\beta_{1j},\ldots,\beta_{Kj})\in\mathbb R^K\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\). The grouped-lasso multinomial estimator minimizes
\[
-\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\log \Pr(Y=y_i\mid X=x_i;\{\beta_j\}_{j=1}^p)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p\|\beta_j\|_2.
\]
The unsquared group norms form an \(\ell_1/\ell_2\) penalty and induce joint inclusion or exclusion of each predictor block. A selected block is generically dense, although individual coordinates need not always be nonzero. Because the likelihood is invariant under a common classwise shift, when \(\lambda>0\) the penalty-selected representative satisfies \(\sum_{k=1}^K\beta_{kj}=0\) for every \(j\). The objective is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group each predictor's coefficients across all classes and penalize the sum of the groups' ordinary Euclidean norms. This convex formulation selects predictors blockwise. Selected blocks are generally dense, but individual coefficients can exceptionally be zero. With positive regularization, the penalty also selects the zero-sum representative of each softmax shift-equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\beta\in\arg\min_{\{\beta_j\}}\left[-\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\log\Pr(Y=y_i\mid X=x_i)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p\|\beta_j\|_2\right],\qquad \sum_{k=1}^K\widehat\beta_{kj}=0\quad(j=1,\ldots,p).

source_evidence.locator: Generalized Linear Models / 3.3. Multiclass Logistic Regression / Definition 3.3-extra-4

source_refs.locator: Generalized Linear Models / 3.3. Multiclass Logistic Regression / Definition 3.3-extra-4

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint group-lasso regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted least-squares group lasso over predefined nonoverlapping coefficient blocks, including its singleton-block boundary and weighting caveat.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For samples \(\{(y_i,z_{i1},\ldots,z_{iJ})\}_{i=1}^N\), the disjoint group-lasso estimator solves
\[
\min_{\theta_0\in\mathbb R,\,\theta_j\in\mathbb R^{p_j}}\left\{\frac12\sum_{i=1}^N\left(y_i-\theta_0-\sum_{j=1}^J z_{ij}^{T}\theta_j\right)^2+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^J\|\theta_j\|_2\right\},\qquad \lambda\ge 0.
\]
The block \(\ell_2\) penalty can set an entire fitted block to zero. For generic problems an active block has no zero coordinates, although special structure can produce within-block zeros. If every \(p_j=1\), the formulation reduces to ordinary lasso. Equal block weights can favor larger groups; group-size or design-scale weights define weighted variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The disjoint group lasso minimizes squared regression error plus Euclidean norms of predefined coefficient blocks. It promotes whole-block selection; active blocks are generically dense, although special structure can yield within-block zeros. Singleton blocks recover lasso, and equal weighting can favor larger groups.
assumptions_latex: \text{the coefficient groups are predefined and nonoverlapping}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\widehat\theta_0,\widehat\theta_1,\ldots,\widehat\theta_J)\in\arg\min\left\{\frac12\sum_{i=1}^N\left(y_i-\theta_0-\sum_{j=1}^Jz_{ij}^{T}\theta_j\right)^2+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^J\|\theta_j\|_2\right\},\qquad p_j=1\ \forall j\implies\sum_j\|\theta_j\|_2=\sum_j|\theta_j|.

source_evidence.locator: Generalizations of the Lasso Penalty / 4.3. The Group Lasso / Definition 4.3-extra-1
