children.title: Lag Ordering
children.top_down_role: Ordered inclusion preferences across lag-indexed predictors.

assumptions_latex: For each predictor \(j\), lags are indexed by \(\ell=1,\ldots,L_j\).
Each coefficient is represented as \(\beta_{j\ell}=\beta^+_{j\ell}-\beta^-_{j\ell}\) with nonnegative parts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta^+_{j1}\ge\cdots\ge\beta^+_{jL_j}\ge0\) and \(\beta^-_{j1}\ge\cdots\ge\beta^-_{jL_j}\ge0\) for every \(j\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient of predictor j at lag ell.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex signed-split formulation of ordered lag coefficients
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex signed-split lag ordering; it does not impose nonconvex ordering of absolute coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A signed-split lag-ordering constraint requires, for every predictor \(j\),
\[\beta^+_{j1}\ge\beta^+_{j2}\ge\cdots\ge\beta^+_{jL_j}\ge0,\qquad \beta^-_{j1}\ge\beta^-_{j2}\ge\cdots\ge\beta^-_{jL_j}\ge0,\]
with \(\beta_{j\ell}=\beta^+_{j\ell}-\beta^-_{j\ell}\). These inequalities define a convex polyhedral feasible set in the split variables. A later positive-part or negative-part contribution can be nonzero only if all earlier contributions of the same sign component are positive. Because cancellation between the two parts is possible, this condition is distinct from the generally nonconvex requirement \(|\beta_{j1}|\ge\cdots\ge|\beta_{jL_j}|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lag ordering uses monotone nonnegative positive and negative coefficient parts, producing a convex preference for earlier lags.
knowledge_statements.title: Lag Ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signed-split order cone is mathematically coherent and correctly distinguished from absolute-coefficient ordering, but a source is needed to establish that this is the intended lag-ordering variant.

children.title: Hierarchical Inclusion
children.top_down_role: Selection preferences governed by parent–descendant relationships.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a directed acyclic graph whose edge \((p,c)\) means that \(p\) is a parent of \(c\).
Each node \(v\in V\) has an activity variable \(u_v\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_c\le u_p\) for every \((p,c)\in E\), so \(u_c>0\Rightarrow u_p>0\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative activity assigned to node v.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: order-cone encoding of hierarchical inclusion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity-variable formulation on a directed acyclic parent-child graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Hierarchical inclusion is imposed by the order-cone constraints
\[u_c\le u_p\quad\text{for every }(p,c)\in E,\qquad u_v\ge0\quad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
Hence an active child, meaning \(u_c>0\), forces every ancestor on a directed path to \(c\) to be active. If coefficients satisfy \(|\beta_v|\le u_v\), the variables \(u_v\) provide a convex hierarchical envelope for coefficient magnitudes. Exact support hierarchy for \(\beta\) additionally requires a formulation preventing positive envelopes at zero coefficients; the order inequalities alone guarantee hierarchy of the activity variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative child activities are bounded by parent activities, so selecting a child forces activity along every ancestral path.
knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Inclusion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The activity-variable order cone and its limitation regarding coefficient support are stated accurately, but no inspectable source supports this hierarchical-inclusion formulation.

children.title: Structural Oversmoothing
children.top_down_role: Loss of genuine local variation, discontinuities, or heterogeneous structure.

assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\widehat\beta_\lambda\) minimizes squared loss plus \(\lambda\|D\beta\|_1\).
\(\beta_0=P_{\ker D}y\), the Euclidean projection of \(y\) onto \(\ker D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda\ge\lambda_0\Rightarrow\widehat\beta_\lambda=\beta_0\), where \(\lambda_0=\min\{\|z\|_\infty:D^Tz=y-\beta_0\}\).

notation.meaning: Projection onto the penalty null space.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct convex optimality threshold for collapse to an operator null space
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact large-penalty collapse threshold for squared-loss operator regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\widehat\beta_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\frac12\|y-\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|D\beta\|_1\right\}.\]
Because \(y-\beta_0\in(\ker D)^\perp=\operatorname{range}(D^T)\), define
\[\lambda_0=\min\{\|z\|_\infty:D^Tz=y-\beta_0\}.\]
For every \(\lambda\ge\lambda_0\), the unique minimizer is \(\widehat\beta_\lambda=\beta_0\). Thus sufficiently strong regularization removes every component detected by \(D\), retaining only the structural null-space component. Genuine variation outside \(\ker D\), including localized changes or discontinuities, is then completely oversmoothed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Beyond an explicit penalty threshold, the estimate collapses to the operator's null space and loses all detected local variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Oversmoothing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The squared-loss collapse threshold is mathematically consistent and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but this nontrivial threshold claim requires an authoritative source.

children.title: Equality-Constrained Basis Pursuit
children.top_down_role: Exact sparse representation over underdetermined or overcomplete systems.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and the affine system \(Ax=b\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\arg\min\{\|x\|_1:Ax=b\}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless equality-constrained basis pursuit over real finite-dimensional vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Equality-constrained basis pursuit is the convex optimization problem
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \|x\|_1\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad Ax=b.\]
Its solution set is \(\operatorname*{argmin}\{\|x\|_1:Ax=b\}\), which is nonempty whenever the affine constraint is feasible. The formulation seeks a minimum-\(\ell_1\)-norm exact representation of \(b\) in the columns of \(A\). It is a convex surrogate for minimum-support exact representation; equality with a sparsest feasible solution requires additional conditions on \(A\) and is not part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis pursuit finds an exact solution of Ax=b having minimum l1 norm; sparse recovery guarantees require additional assumptions on A.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Basis Pursuit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality-constrained basis-pursuit definition is correct and properly scoped, but no source reference with a section or page locator is attached.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform basis-pursuit recovery and projected cross-polytope faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates uniform recovery of all vectors having at most s nonzero entries by equality-constrained basis pursuit with preservation of specified face counts and faces of the cross-polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times N}\) and let \(s\in\mathbb{Z}\) with \(s\ge 1\). The following are equivalent: (a) every \(s\)-sparse vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^N\) is the unique minimizer of \(\|z\|_1\) subject to \(Az=Ax\); (b) \(f_k(AB_1^N)=f_k(B_1^N)\) for every integer \(k\) satisfying \(0\le k\le s-1\); (c) \(f_k(AB_1^N)=f_k(B_1^N)\) for \(k=0\) and \(k=s-1\); (d) \(AB_1^N\) has \(2N\) vertices, and every \((s-1)\)-face of \(B_1^N\) maps under \(A\) to an \((s-1)\)-face of \(AB_1^N\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ℓ1 reconstruction over the overcomplete dictionary formed by concatenating two orthonormal basis matrices; excludes the distinct approximate constrained-lasso formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi,\Psi\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\) satisfy \(\Phi^T\Phi=\Psi^T\Psi=I_p\), and define the overcomplete dictionary \(D=[\Phi\ \Psi]\). children.title: Basis-Pursuit Linear-Program Representations
children.top_down_role: Positive-part, epigraph, and standard-form linear optimization interfaces.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{Ax=b}\|x\|_1=\min_{Ax=b,-t\le x\le t}\mathbf1^Tt=\min_{A(u-v)=b,u,v\ge0}\mathbf1^T(u+v)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary exact linear-program reformulations of the l1 norm
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent epigraph and positive-part linear programs for real basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Equality-constrained basis pursuit has the epigraph linear-program representation
\[\min_{x,t}\ \mathbf1^Tt\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\ -t\le x\le t,\ t\ge0,\]
and the split-variable standard-form representation
\[\min_{u,v}\ \mathbf1^T(u+v)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(u-v)=b,\ u\ge0,\ v\ge0.\]
For any feasible \(x\), choosing \(t=|x|\), or choosing \(u=x_+\) and \(v=x_-\), attains objective \(\|x\|_1\). Conversely, every feasible epigraph or split point yields an \(x\) with \(\|x\|_1\) no larger than its linear objective. Hence all three formulations have the same optimal value and corresponding optimal coefficient vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute-value epigraph variables or nonnegative positive and negative parts turn basis pursuit exactly into a linear program.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Pursuit Linear-Program Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epigraph and split-variable linear-program representations are exact and the representation kind fits the container, but the record has no inspectable supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be feasible for basis pursuit and let \(S=\operatorname{supp}(\bar x)\). A strict dual certificate is a vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying \(A_S^{\mathsf T}y=\operatorname{sign}(\bar x_S)\) and \(\|A_{S^c}^{\mathsf T}y\|_\infty<1\). If such a certificate exists and \(A_S\) has full column rank, then \(\bar x\) is the unique solution of \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\|x\|_1\) subject to \(Ax=b\). Replacing the strict inequality by \(\leq 1\) certifies optimality but does not alone certify uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cone-conditioned stability bound for basis pursuit denoising
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds individual-vector reconstruction error under a positive lower gain of the measurement operator on the source-defined set \(T(\mathbf x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf A\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\), \(\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^N\), and \(\mathbf y=\mathbf A\mathbf x+\mathbf e\in\mathbb R^m\), with \(\|\mathbf e\|_2\leq\eta\). If, for some \(\tau>0\), \[\inf_{\mathbf v\in T(\mathbf x),\ \|\mathbf v\|_2=1}\|\mathbf A\mathbf v\|_2\geq\tau,\] and \(\mathbf x^\sharp\) is a minimizer of \(\|\mathbf z\|_1\) subject to \(\|\mathbf A\mathbf z-\mathbf y\|_2\leq\eta\), then \(\|\mathbf x-\mathbf x^\sharp\|_2\leq 2\eta/\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the measurement operator has gain at least tau on every unit vector in the relevant source-defined set, then a basis-pursuit-denoising minimizer has Euclidean reconstruction error at most twice eta divided by tau.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every optimizer has minimum \(\ell_1\)-norm over the Euclidean residual ball \(\{x:\|Ax-b\|_2\leq\varepsilon\}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained BPDN with a known Euclidean bound on additive residual noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Euclidean-residual basis pursuit denoising is the convex program \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \|x\|_1\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad \|Ax-b\|_2\leq\varepsilon.\] The parameter \(\varepsilon\geq0\) specifies the admissible Euclidean residual radius. At \(\varepsilon=0\), the formulation reduces to equality-constrained basis pursuit whenever \(Ax=b\) is feasible. knowledge_statements.title: Support-Overlap Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary for jointly sparse signal and corruption recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(0\le s\le n\) and \(0\le t\le m\) be integers, and define the admissible class \(\mathcal C_{s,t}=\{(x,e)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m:\|x\|_0\le s,\ \|e\|_0\le t\}\). The observation map \((x,e)\mapsto Ax+e\) fails to be injective on \(\mathcal C_{s,t}\) if and only if there is a nonzero pair \((h,g)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) such that \(Ah+g=0\), \(\|h\|_0\le2s\), and \(\|g\|_0\le2t\). In that case no estimator depending only on the observation can identify both components uniformly over \(\mathcal C_{s,t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform separation of s-sparse signals and t-sparse corruptions is impossible exactly when a nonzero signal change supported on at most 2s coordinates can be canceled by an error change supported on at most 2t coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le s\le n\) and \(0\le t\le m\) are integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \((x,e)\mapsto Ax+e\) is noninjective on \(\mathcal C_{s,t}\) if and only if \(\exists(h,g)\ne(0,0)\) with \(Ah+g=0\), \(\|h\|_0\le2s\), and \(\|g\|_0\le2t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-to-Noisy Recovery Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialization of residual-tolerant basis pursuit to exact basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), data \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), consider \(\min_x\{\|x\|_1:\|Ax-b\|_2\le\varepsilon\}\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), its feasible set is exactly \(\{x:Ax=b\}\), so the problem equals equality-constrained basis pursuit. If \(b=Ax_0+e\) and \(\varepsilon\ge\|e\|_2\), then \(x_0\) is feasible for the noisy problem. Moreover, increasing \(\varepsilon\) enlarges the feasible set and cannot increase the optimal \(\ell_1\) value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-tolerant basis pursuit becomes exact basis pursuit at zero tolerance; choosing tolerance at least the noise norm preserves feasibility of the true signal.

children.title: Pareto-Curve Methods
children.top_down_role: Value-function navigation between sparsity and data-fidelity budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Curve Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bisection navigation of the sparsity-budget versus residual Pareto curve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and define \(\phi(\tau)=\min_{\|x\|_1\le\tau}\|Ax-b\|_2\). Given \(0\le\tau_L<\tau_U\) with \(\phi(\tau_L)>\varepsilon\ge\phi(\tau_U)\), solve the subproblem at \(\tau_U\) and store a minimizer \(x_U\). Initialize \(L=\tau_L\) and \(U=\tau_U\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\tau_k=(L+U)/2\), solve the subproblem at \(\tau_k\), and let \(r_k=\|Ax_k-b\|_2\). If \(r_k>\varepsilon\), set \(L=\tau_k\). Otherwise set \(U=\tau_k\), store \(x_U=x_k\), and stop if \(|r_k-\varepsilon|\le\delta\). Also stop when \(U-L\le\eta\). Return the stored feasible incumbent \(x_U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bisect the sparsity budget while retaining the most recent upper-bracket solution whose residual meets the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every Pareto subproblem used by the algorithm attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned incumbent satisfies \(\|Ax_U-b\|_2\le\varepsilon\), and termination occurs when \(U-L\le\eta\) or a feasible iterate satisfies \(|r_k-\varepsilon|\le\delta\).

notation.meaning: Minimum residual under an l1 budget tau.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Parameter Noncorrespondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar example showing that penalized and constrained parameters need not correspond bijectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the scalar Lasso problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\tfrac12(x-1)^2+\lambda|x|\). Its unique solution is \(x_\lambda=\max\{1-\lambda,0\}\) for \(\lambda\ge0\). Hence every \(\lambda\ge1\) produces the same solution \(x_\lambda=0\), the same sparsity budget \(\tau=|x_\lambda|=0\), and the same residual \(1\). Thus the map from penalty parameters to equivalent constrained budgets is not injective, even though each penalized optimizer also solves the constrained problem with its attained budget. Flat Pareto segments and nonunique multipliers create the same obstruction in higher dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Many penalty values can yield one constrained budget and one optimizer, so equivalence of solutions does not imply a one-to-one parameter map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_1\neq\lambda_2\) with \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge1\) nevertheless gives \(x_{\lambda_1}=x_{\lambda_2}=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit scalar convex optimization calculation establishes noninjectivity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Null Space Property Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust null-space condition connecting exact and noisy sparse recovery guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has the robust \(\ell_1\) null-space property of order \(s\) relative to the Euclidean residual norm if there exist \(0\le\rho<1\) and \(\tau>0\) such that, for every \(h\in\mathbb R^n\) and every \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|S|\le s\), \[\|h_S\|_1\le\rho\|h_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Ah\|_2.\] Restriction to \(h\in\ker A\) removes the residual term and yields the stable null-space inequality; its strict form characterizes uniform exact basis-pursuit recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The null-space property requires every small coordinate restriction of an error vector to be controlled by its complement and, robustly, its measurement residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|h_S\|_1\le\rho\|h_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Ah\|_2\) for all admissible \(h,S\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Vector ℓp Bound from the ℓq-Robust Null Space Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General comparison inequality for 1 ≤ p ≤ q under an ℓq-robust null-space assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1\leq p\leq q\), and suppose \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\) satisfies the \(\ell_q\)-robust null space property of order \(s\) with constants \(0<\rho<1\) and \(\tau>0\). Then, for all \(x,z\in\mathbb C^N\),
\[\|z-x\|_p\leq\frac{C}{s^{1-1/p}}\left(\|z\|_1-\|x\|_1+2\sigma_s(x)_1\right)+D s^{1/p-1/q}\|A(z-x)\|,\]
where \(C=(1+\rho)^2/(1-\rho)\) and \(D=(3+\rho)\tau/(1-\rho)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust Null Space Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition relative to a fixed support and uniformly over supports of cardinality at most s.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\), let \(\|\cdot\|\) denote the specified measurement-space norm, and let \(0<\rho<1\), \(\tau>0\). The matrix \(A\) satisfies the robust null space property relative to \(S\subseteq[N]\) if
\[\|v_S\|_1\leq \rho\|v_{\bar S}\|_1+\tau\|Av\|\quad\text{for all }v\in\mathbb C^N.\]
It satisfies the robust null space property of order \(s\) if this holds for every \(S\subseteq[N]\) with \(|S|\leq s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix has the robust null space property relative to S when every vector's ℓ1 mass on S is bounded by rho times its ℓ1 mass outside S plus tau times its measurement norm. It has order s when this holds for every support of size at most s.
assumptions_latex: \|\cdot\|\text{ is the specified norm on the measurement space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall v\in\mathbb C^N,\ \|v_S\|_1\leq\rho\|v_{\bar S}\|_1+\tau\|Av\|;\quad\text{order }s\text{ requires this for every }S\subseteq[N]\text{ with }|S|\leq s.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust ℓp Recovery under the ℓ2-Robust Null Space Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous stable and noise-robust recovery bounds for 1 ≤ p ≤ 2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\) satisfies the \(\ell_2\)-robust null space property of order \(s\) with constants \(0<\rho<1\) and \(\tau>0\). For \(x\in\mathbb C^N\), let \(y=Ax+e\) with \(\|e\|_2\leq\eta\), and let \(x^\sharp\) be a solution of \((P_{1,\eta})\) using the measurement norm \(\|\cdot\|_2\). Then there are constants \(C,D>0\), depending only on \(\rho\) and \(\tau\), such that for every \(1\leq p\leq2\),
\[\|x-x^\sharp\|_p\leq\frac{C}{s^{1-1/p}}\sigma_s(x)_1+D s^{1/p-1/2}\eta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the ℓ2-robust null space property, noise-constrained basis pursuit has stable and noise-robust recovery bounds in every ℓp norm from ℓ1 through ℓ2.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ satisfies the }\ell_2\text{-robust NSP of order }s\text{ with }0<\rho<1\text{ and }\tau>0
x^\sharp\text{ is a solution of }(P_{1,\eta})\text{ with measurement norm }\|\cdot\|_2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists C,D>0\text{ depending only on }\rho,\tau\text{ such that }\forall p\in[1,2],\quad\|x-x^\sharp\|_p\leq C s^{-(1-1/p)}\sigma_s(x)_1+D s^{1/p-1/2}\eta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: ℓq-Robust Null Space Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform robust null-space inequality over supports of cardinality at most s.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\geq1\), \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\), \(s\geq1\), \(0<\rho<1\), and \(\tau>0\). The matrix \(A\) satisfies the \(\ell_q\)-robust null space property of order \(s\), with respect to the specified measurement norm \(\|\cdot\|\), if for every \(S\subseteq[N]\) with \(|S|\leq s\) and every \(v\in\mathbb C^N\),
\[\|v_S\|_q\leq\frac{\rho}{s^{1-1/q}}\|v_{\bar S}\|_1+\tau\|Av\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A has the ℓq-robust null space property of order s when, on every support of size at most s, a vector's ℓq norm is controlled by its scaled ℓ1 tail and its measurement norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall S\subseteq[N]\text{ with }|S|\leq s,\ \forall v\in\mathbb C^N,\quad\|v_S\|_q\leq\rho s^{-(1-1/q)}\|v_{\bar S}\|_1+\tau\|Av\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform s-sparse recovery characterized by the null space property of order s
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for uniform exact recovery of all vectors with sparsity at most s.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb K^{m\times N}\). Every \(s\)-sparse vector \(x\in\mathbb K^N\) is the unique solution of \[\min_{z\in\mathbb K^N}\|z\|_1\quad\text{subject to }Az=Ax\] if and only if \(A\) satisfies the null space property of order \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-constrained ℓ1 minimization uniquely recovers every s-sparse vector if and only if A has the null space property of order s.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall x\in\mathbb K^N,\ \|x\|_0\le s\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_{Az=Ax}\|z\|_1=\{x\}\bigr]\iff\operatorname{NSP}_A(s).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Vector Characterization of the Robust Null Space Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent characterization for a fixed support set and fixed constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\), \(S\subseteq[N]\), \(0<\rho<1\), and \(\tau>0\). The matrix \(A\) satisfies the robust null space property relative to \(S\) with constants \(\rho,\tau\) if and only if, for all \(x,z\in\mathbb C^N\),
\[\|z-x\|_1\leq\frac{1+\rho}{1-\rho}\left(\|z\|_1-\|x\|_1+2\|x_{\bar S}\|_1\right)+\frac{2\tau}{1-\rho}\|A(z-x)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robust null space property relative to S is equivalent to a uniform two-vector ℓ1 inequality involving the objective difference, the tail of x outside S, and the measurement discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ satisfies the robust NSP relative to }S\iff\forall x,z\in\mathbb C^N,\ \|z-x\|_1\leq\frac{1+\rho}{1-\rho}(\|z\|_1-\|x\|_1+2\|x_{\bar S}\|_1)+\frac{2\tau}{1-\rho}\|A(z-x)\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable Null Space Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines both the set-relative stable null-space property and its uniform order-s form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{C}^{m\times N}\), \(S\subseteq[N]\), and \(0<\rho<1\). The matrix \(A\) satisfies the stable null space property relative to \(S\) with constant \(\rho\) if \(\|v_S\|_1\leq\rho\|v_{\bar S}\|_1\) for every \(v\in\ker A\). It satisfies the stable null space property of order \(s\) with constant \(\rho\) if this condition holds for every \(S\subseteq[N]\) with \(|S|\leq s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix has the stable null space property relative to S if every null-space vector has l1 mass on S no greater than rho times its mass outside S. The order-s property requires this for every set of at most s indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall v\in\ker A,\ \|v_S\|_1\leq\rho\|v_{\bar S}\|_1;\qquad \operatorname{SNSP}(s,\rho)\iff\forall S\subseteq[N],\ |S|\leq s,\ \operatorname{SNSP}(S,\rho).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Isometry Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted isometry condition underlying uniform sparse-recovery guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(1\le s\le n\), the restricted isometry constant \(\delta_s(A)\) is the least \(\delta\ge0\) such that \[(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\le\|Ax\|_2^2\le(1+\delta)\|x\|_2^2\] for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\|x\|_0\le s\). The matrix has the restricted isometry property of order \(s\) when \(\delta_s(A)<1\). This condition makes every submatrix formed from at most \(s\) columns uniformly well-conditioned and, at stronger numerical thresholds, supports uniform stable and robust recovery results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted isometry requires the measurement map to approximately preserve Euclidean norms of all vectors supported on at most a fixed number of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) has RIP of order \(s\) exactly when \(\delta_s(A)<1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform robust recovery bounds for IHT and HTP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-iteration and conditional cluster-point instance-optimality bounds for hard-thresholding recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose A\in\mathbb{C}^{m\times N} satisfies \delta_{6s}<1/\sqrt3. For every x\in\mathbb{C}^N and e\in\mathbb{C}^m, let (x^n) be generated by (IHT), (\mathrm{HTP}_1), or (\mathrm{HTP}_2) with y=Ax+e, x^0=0, and sparsity parameter 2s. There exist C,D>0 and 0<\rho<1, depending only on \delta_{6s}, such that for every n\ge0, \|x-x^n\|_1\le C\sigma_s(x)_1+D\sqrt{s}\|e\|_2+2\rho^n\sqrt{s}\|x\|_2 and \|x-x^n\|_2\le C\sigma_s(x)_1/\sqrt{s}+D\|e\|_2+2\rho^n\|x\|_2. If the sequence clusters around x^\sharp\in\mathbb{C}^N, then \|x-x^\sharp\|_1\le C\sigma_s(x)_1+D\sqrt{s}\|e\|_2 and \|x-x^\sharp\|_2\le C\sigma_s(x)_1/\sqrt{s}+D\|e\|_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the order-6s RIP condition, IHT and the two HTP variants run with sparsity parameter 2s have uniform l1 and l2 recovery errors consisting of best s-term approximation error, measurement noise, and a geometrically decaying iteration term. A stated cluster vector satisfies the corresponding bounds without the geometric term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x-x^n\|_1\le C\sigma_s(x)_1+D\sqrt{s}\|e\|_2+2\rho^n\sqrt{s}\|x\|_2,\quad \|x-x^n\|_2\le\frac{C}{\sqrt{s}}\sigma_s(x)_1+D\|e\|_2+2\rho^n\|x\|_2;\quad (x^n\text{ clusters around }x^\sharp)\Rightarrow\begin{cases}\|x-x^\sharp\|_1\le C\sigma_s(x)_1+D\sqrt{s}\|e\|_2,\\\|x-x^\sharp\|_2\le\frac{C}{\sqrt{s}}\sigma_s(x)_1+D\|e\|_2.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Isometry Bound for Gaussian Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample high-probability control of the order-s restricted isometry constant of a normalized Gaussian measurement matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf A\) be an \(m\times N\) Gaussian matrix with \(m<N\). For \(\eta,\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), assume that \[m\ge 2\eta^{-2}\left(s\ln\!\left(\frac{eN}{s}\right)+\ln\!\left(2\varepsilon^{-1}\right)\right).\] Then, with probability at least \(1-\varepsilon\), the restricted isometry constant \(\delta_s\) of \(m^{-1/2}\mathbf A\) satisfies \[\delta_s\le 2\left(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\ln(eN/s)}}\right)\eta+\left(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\ln(eN/s)}}\right)^2\eta^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an underdetermined Gaussian matrix has at least the stated number of rows, then with probability at least 1 minus epsilon the order-s restricted isometry constant of its normalized form is at most the stated expression in eta.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf A\text{ is an }m\times N\text{ Gaussian matrix}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P\!\left\{\delta_s(m^{-1/2}\mathbf A)\le 2\left(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\ln(eN/s)}}\right)\eta+\left(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\ln(eN/s)}}\right)^2\eta^2\right\}\ge 1-\varepsilon

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameterized BOS Restricted-Isometry Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit sample-size and failure-probability conditions for restricted isometry of BOS sampling matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\) be the random sampling matrix associated with a bounded orthonormal system having constant \(K\ge1\), and let \(\varepsilon,\eta_1,\eta_2\in(0,1)\). If
\[
\frac{m}{\ln(9m)}\ge C_1\eta_1^{-2}K^2s\ln^2(4s)\ln(8N),
\qquad
m\ge C_2\eta_2^{-2}K^2s\ln(\varepsilon^{-1}),
\]
then
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\delta_s(m^{-1/2}A)\le\eta_1+\eta_1^2+\eta_2\right)\ge1-\varepsilon.
\]
The constants may be chosen as \(C_2=32/3\) and \(C_1=c_0C^2\), where \(c_0=174.24\) and \(C=4\sqrt2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two stated sample-size bounds ensure, with probability at least 1−ε, that the normalized BOS sampling matrix has restricted isometry constant at most η₁+η₁²+η₂; explicit universal constants are available.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\text{ is a BOS random sampling matrix with constant }K\ge1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P\!\left(\delta_s(m^{-1/2}A)\le\eta_1+\eta_1^2+\eta_2\right)\ge1-\varepsilon

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted bounds for the RIP Gram error

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{C}^{m\times N} have order-t restricted isometry constant \delta_t. knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-probability restricted-isometry guarantee for random sampling from a bounded orthonormal system.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable IHT and HTP approximation under RIP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-iteration contraction and stability estimate for hard-thresholding recovery with model mismatch and noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose A\in\mathbb{C}^{m\times N} satisfies \delta_{3s}<1/\sqrt{3}. Let x\in\mathbb{C}^N, e\in\mathbb{C}^m, S\subseteq[N] with |S|=s, and y=Ax+e. If (x^n) is generated by (IHT), (\mathrm{HTP}_1), or (\mathrm{HTP}_2), then for every n\ge0, \|x^n-x_S\|_2\le\rho^n\|x^0-x_S\|_2+\tau\|Ax_{\bar S}+e\|_2. For (IHT), \rho=\sqrt{3}\,\delta_{3s}<1 and \tau\le2.18/(1-\rho). For (\mathrm{HTP}_1) and (\mathrm{HTP}_2), \rho=\sqrt{2\delta_{3s}^2/(1-\delta_{2s}^2)}<1 and \tau\le5.15/(1-\rho).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under delta_3s below 1/sqrt(3), IHT and both stated HTP variants contract geometrically toward x restricted to any s-element set, up to an error determined by the unmodeled measurements and noise, with the stated method-specific constants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer from head approximation to global sparse-recovery error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts an approximation estimate on the largest coordinates into global l_p error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose A\in\mathbb{C}^{m\times N} has restricted isometry constant \delta_s<1. Let \kappa,\tau>0, \xi\ge0, e\in\mathbb{C}^m, and x,x'\in\mathbb{C}^N. Let T index 2s largest-magnitude entries of x. If \|x'\|_0\le\kappa s and \|x_T-x'\|_2\le\tau\|Ax_{\bar T}+e\|_2+\xi, then for every 1\le p\le2, \|x-x'\|_p\le(1+c_\kappa\tau)s^{-(1-1/p)}\sigma_s(x)_1+d_\kappa\tau s^{1/p-1/2}\|e\|_2+d_\kappa s^{1/p-1/2}\xi, where c_\kappa,d_\kappa>0 depend only on \kappa.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a kappa-s-sparse vector approximates the largest 2s coordinates of x with the stated measurement-tail, noise, and residual error, then its global l_p error for every p from 1 to 2 is bounded by the best s-term l1 error plus scaled noise and residual terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall p\in[1,2],\quad \|x-x'\|_p\le\frac{1+c_\kappa\tau}{s^{1-1/p}}\sigma_s(x)_1+d_\kappa\tau s^{1/p-1/2}\|e\|_2+d_\kappa s^{1/p-1/2}\xi

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-optimal recovery bounds under an explicit order-2s restricted-isometry condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\), \(s\in\mathbb N\), and \(\delta_{2s}(A)<4/\sqrt{41}\). children.title: Mutual-Coherence Criteria
children.top_down_role: Computable dictionary criteria based on pairwise atom similarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Mutual-Coherence Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform noiseless recovery criterion for normalized dictionaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have unit-norm columns and mutual coherence \(\mu(A)=\max_{i\ne j}|a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j|\), with \(0<\mu(A)\le1\). If \(x_0\) is \(s\)-sparse and \[s<\frac12\left(1+\frac1{\mu(A)}\right),\] then \(x_0\) is the unique sparsest solution of \(Ax=Ax_0\) and is also the unique minimizer of \(\min_x\{\|x\|_1:Ax=Ax_0\}\). Consequently, the criterion gives a uniform recovery guarantee for every signal having at most \(s\) nonzero coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized dictionary recovers every sufficiently sparse signal uniquely by basis pursuit when sparsity lies below the standard mutual-coherence threshold.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(A\) have unit Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0\) is the unique sparsest feasible vector and the unique basis-pursuit solution.

notation.meaning: Largest absolute inner product between distinct normalized columns.
Number of nonzero coordinates of x.

children.title: Spark Criteria
children.top_down_role: Dictionary identifiability regimes organized by minimal linear dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Spark Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact uniqueness criterion for uniformly sparse linear representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define \(\operatorname{spark}(A)=\inf\{\|h\|_0:h\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}\}\), with \(\operatorname{spark}(A)=+\infty\) when \(\ker A=\{0\}\). Let \(1\le s\le n\) be an integer. Every \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\|x_0\|_0\le s\) is the unique vector having at most \(s\) nonzero coordinates and satisfying \(Ax=Ax_0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s\). Equivalently, no nonzero \(h\in\ker A\) has \(\|h\|_0\le2s\). This criterion concerns uniqueness among sparse representations and does not by itself assert recovery by \(\ell_1\) minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All representations with at most s nonzeros are unique exactly when every nonzero null vector has more than 2s nonzeros, with infinite spark assigned to an injective matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform \(s\)-sparse uniqueness holds if and only if \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s\).

notation.meaning: Minimum support size of a nonzero null vector, or positive infinity when the null space is trivial.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform sparse uniqueness is characterized by the minimum support of a nonzero null vector

children.title: Coherence-Based Spark Bounds
children.top_down_role: Navigation between computable coherence quantities and spark-based guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Coherence-Based Spark Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound on spark obtained from normalized-column coherence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have unit-norm columns and mutual coherence \(0<\mu(A)\le1\). Then \[\operatorname{spark}(A)\ge 1+\frac1{\mu(A)}.\] Since spark is integer-valued, this inequality is interpreted with the corresponding integer ceiling when used numerically. Combining it with \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s\) yields the readily computable sufficient uniqueness condition \(s<\tfrac12(1+1/\mu(A))\). The bound may be strict because mutual coherence retains only the largest pairwise column correlation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reciprocal of mutual coherence gives a computable lower bound on spark and therefore a sufficient, though potentially conservative, sparse-uniqueness threshold.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(A\) have unit Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{spark}(A)\ge1+1/\mu(A)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum number of linearly dependent columns.

children.title: Criterion-Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where coherence surrogates differ materially from spark-level identifiability.

knowledge_statements.title: Criterion-Separation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-spark dictionary where spark certifies two-sparse uniqueness but coherence does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4,v]\in\mathbb R^{4\times5}\), where \(e_i\) are the standard basis vectors and \(v=(\sqrt{0.97},0.1,0.1,0.1)^{\mathsf T}\). All columns have unit norm, every four columns are independent, and hence \(\operatorname{spark}(A)=5>4\); the spark criterion therefore certifies uniqueness of every two-sparse representation. However, \(\mu(A)=\sqrt{0.97}\), so \(\tfrac12(1+1/\mu(A))<2\). The mutual-coherence criterion consequently fails to certify order-two uniqueness. Thus the coherence criterion is strictly more conservative than direct spark knowledge for this dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearly aligned but full-spark dictionary can satisfy the exact spark threshold for two-sparse uniqueness while failing the coherence-based sufficient threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(e_1,\ldots,e_4\) are the standard basis of \(\mathbb R^4\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2(2)\) while \(2\not<\tfrac12(1+1/\mu(A))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit matrix calculation separates the spark and coherence sufficient criteria

children.title: Instance Optimality Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Instance Optimality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation-relative recovery guarantee with additive measurement-noise sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(\Delta:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) be a decoder, and let \(1\le q\le p\le\infty\). The pair \((A,\Delta)\) is noise-robust instance optimal of order \(s\) in \((\ell_p,\ell_q)\) if constants \(C,D\ge0\) exist such that, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(e\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\|x-\Delta(Ax+e)\|_p\le C s^{1/p-1/q}\sigma_s(x)_q+D\|e\|_2,\] where \(\sigma_s(x)_q=\inf_{\|z\|_0\le s}\|x-z\|_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Instance optimality bounds reconstruction error by the signal's best sparse-approximation error plus a term proportional to measurement noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed approximation-plus-noise inequality holds uniformly for all \(x\) and \(e\).

notation.meaning: Best s-term approximation error in the lq norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer of Mixed Instance Optimality to a Smaller Recovery-Norm Exponent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse-recovery instance optimality when the recovery-error exponent is decreased while the approximation exponent and recovery order are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\ge q'\ge p\ge 1\). If \((\mathbf A,\Delta)\) is mixed \((\ell_q,\ell_p)\)-instance optimal of order \(s\) with constant \(C\), then there exists a reconstruction map \(\Delta'\) such that \((\mathbf A,\Delta')\) is mixed \((\ell_{q'},\ell_p)\)-instance optimal of order \(s\) with a constant \(C'\) depending only on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If q is at least q′, q′ is at least p, and p is at least 1, then mixed (ℓq, ℓp) instance optimality of order s yields a possibly different reconstruction map having mixed (ℓq′, ℓp) instance optimality of the same order, with a constant depending only on the original constant.
assumptions_latex: (\mathbf A,\Delta)\text{ is mixed }(\ell_q,\ell_p)\text{-instance optimal of order }s\text{ with constant }C
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\Delta'\ \exists\,C'\text{ depending only on }C\text{ such that }(\mathbf A,\Delta')\text{ is mixed }(\ell_{q'},\ell_p)\text{-instance optimal of order }s\text{ with constant }C'.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonuniform Gaussian ℓp-to-ℓq instance-optimal recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-signal recovery in \(\ell_q\), controlled by best \(s\)-term \(\ell_p\) approximation and uniform over additive noise vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist universal constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3,C,D>0\) such that, for \(1\le p\le q\le2\), every fixed \(\mathbf x\in\mathbb C^N\), and \(\widetilde{\mathbf A}=m^{-1/2}\mathbf A\), where \(\mathbf A\) is a random draw of an \(m\times N\) Gaussian matrix, if \(N\ge c_2m\) and \(s\le c_3s_*\), with \(s_*=m/\ln(eN/m)\), then with probability at least \(1-5e^{-c_1m}\), simultaneously for all \(\mathbf e\in\mathbb C^m\), \[\left\|\mathbf x-\Delta_1(\widetilde{\mathbf A}\mathbf x+\mathbf e)\right\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\sigma_s(\mathbf x)_p+D s_*^{1/q-1/2}\|\mathbf e\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For 1≤p≤q≤2 and every fixed signal, a normalized Gaussian measurement matrix satisfies, with probability at least 1−5 exp(−c₁m), an ℓq recovery bound simultaneously for every noise vector under the stated dimensional and sparsity conditions.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde{\mathbf A}=m^{-1/2}\mathbf A,\quad \mathbf A\text{ is a random }m\times N\text{ Gaussian matrix}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left(\forall\mathbf e\in\mathbb C^m:\ \|\mathbf x-\Delta_1(\widetilde{\mathbf A}\mathbf x+\mathbf e)\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\sigma_s(\mathbf x)_p+D s_*^{1/q-1/2}\|\mathbf e\|_2\right)\ge1-5e^{-c_1m}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonuniform Gaussian ℓ2 instance-optimal recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-signal, noise-uniform recovery under normalized Gaussian measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist universal constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3,C,D>0\) such that, for every fixed \(\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{C}^N\), if \(\widetilde{\mathbf A}=m^{-1/2}\mathbf A\), where \(\mathbf A\) is a random draw of an \(m\times N\) Gaussian matrix, \(N\ge c_2m\), and \(s\le c_3s_*\) with \(s_*=m/\ln(eN/m)\), then with probability at least \(1-5e^{-c_1m}\), simultaneously for all \(\mathbf e\in\mathbb C^m\), \[\left\|\mathbf x-\Delta_1(\widetilde{\mathbf A}\mathbf x+\mathbf e)\right\|_2\le C\sigma_s(\mathbf x)_2+D\|\mathbf e\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every fixed signal, a normalized Gaussian measurement matrix obeys, with probability at least 1−5 exp(−c₁m), an ℓ2 recovery bound simultaneously for all noise vectors, provided the stated dimensional and sparsity conditions hold.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde{\mathbf A}=m^{-1/2}\mathbf A,\quad \mathbf A\text{ is a random }m\times N\text{ Gaussian matrix}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left(\forall\mathbf e\in\mathbb C^m:\ \|\mathbf x-\Delta_1(\widetilde{\mathbf A}\mathbf x+\mathbf e)\|_2\le C\sigma_s(\mathbf x)_2+D\|\mathbf e\|_2\right)\ge1-5e^{-c_1m}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed (ℓq, ℓp)-Instance Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform recovery in an ℓq error norm relative to best s-term approximation in ℓp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\ge p\ge 1\), \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\), \(\Delta:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^N\), and \(C>0\), the pair \((A,\Delta)\) is mixed \((\ell_q,\ell_p)\)-instance optimal of order \(s\) with constant \(C\) if \[\|x-\Delta(Ax)\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\,\sigma_s(x)_p\qquad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb C^N.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed (ℓq, ℓp)-instance optimality bounds every signal's ℓq reconstruction error by C times its best s-term ℓp approximation error, scaled by s raised to minus (1/p−1/q).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathbb C^N,\quad \|x-\Delta(Ax)\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\sigma_s(x)_p

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-Space Characterization of Mixed Instance Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes existence of a mixed-norm instance-optimal reconstruction map, with a factor-two loss in the converse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\ge p\ge 1\), \(A\in\mathbb C^{m\times N}\), and \(C>0\). If there exists \(\Delta\) such that \((A,\Delta)\) is mixed \((\ell_q,\ell_p)\)-instance optimal of order \(s\) with constant \(C\), then \[\|v\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\sigma_{2s}(v)_p\qquad\text{for all }v\in\ker A.\] Conversely, if this inequality holds for every \(v\in\ker A\), then there exists a reconstruction map \(\Delta\) for which \((A,\Delta)\) is mixed \((\ell_q,\ell_p)\)-instance optimal of order \(s\) with constant \(2C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Existence of a mixed (ℓq, ℓp)-instance-optimal reconstruction with constant C implies the stated null-space approximation inequality at sparsity 2s. Conversely, that inequality yields such a reconstruction with constant 2C.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists\Delta:\ (A,\Delta)\text{ is mixed-instance optimal with constant }C\bigr]\Rightarrow\bigl[\forall v\in\ker A,\ \|v\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\sigma_{2s}(v)_p\bigr];\quad \text{the null-space inequality}\Rightarrow\bigl[\exists\Delta\text{ with constant }2C\bigr]

children.title: Canonical Convex Representations
children.top_down_role: Standard solver classes arising from loss and regularizer geometry.

children.title: Linear-Program Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral representations for absolute values, coordinate sparsity, and robust fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Program Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph linearization of coefficient and residual absolute values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^r\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^q\), and \(\lambda\ge0\). The convex problem \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \|x\|_1+\lambda\|Ax-b\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad Cx=d,\ Gx\le h\] is equivalent to the linear program \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,\,u\in\mathbb R^n,\,v\in\mathbb R^m}\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u+\lambda\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}v\quad\text{subject to}\quad -u\le x\le u,\ -v\le Ax-b\le v,\ Cx=d,\ Gx\le h.\] The two problems have the same optimal value and the same optimizing \(x\)-components; for each optimizing \(x\), auxiliary variables may be chosen as \(u=|x|\) and \(v=|Ax-b|\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing componentwise magnitude epigraph variables converts the l1-regularized, l1-fidelity model into a linear program with the same optimizing original variables.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^r\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original convex problem and the displayed linear program have identical optimal values and identical optimizing \(x\)-components.

notation.meaning: All-ones vector of the required dimension.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise absolute-value epigraphs give the canonical LP representation

children.title: Quadratic-Program Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Quadratic-loss and quadratic-regularization canonical forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Program Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical QP form for quadratic loss with quadratic regularization and affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\), \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\), and \(\lambda\ge0\). The problem \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}\lVert Lx\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Gx\le h,\;Ex=d\] is, after dropping the constant \(\frac12\lVert b\rVert_2^2\), the convex quadratic program \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Gx\le h,\;Ex=d,\] where \(Q=A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L\succeq0\) and \(q=-A^\top b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the same affine constraints, quadratic loss plus quadratic regularization is equivalent, up to an objective constant, to a convex QP whose Hessian is the sum of the loss and regularizer Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L\succeq0\), and the two constrained formulations have identical minimizers.

children.title: Second-Order Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Residual-norm and group-norm canonical forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph SOCP form for residual and nonoverlapping group norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(\mathcal G\) partition the coordinates of \(x\), with weights \(w_g\ge0\). The norm-regularized problem \[\min_x\;\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2+\lambda\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\lVert x_g\rVert_2\] has the equivalent second-order cone representation \[\min_{x,t,(s_g)}\;t+\lambda\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_gs_g\quad\text{subject to}\quad (t,Ax-b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1},\;(s_g,x_g)\in\mathcal Q^{|g|+1}\;\forall g,\] where \(\mathcal Q^{k+1}=\{(u,v):u\ge\lVert v\rVert_2\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual and group Euclidean norms are replaced by epigraph variables constrained to second-order cones, producing an equivalent SOCP.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a finite partition of the coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SOCP and norm-regularized problem have the same optimal \(x\) and optimal value.

children.title: Generic Conic Canonicalization
children.top_down_role: Modeling-system routes from regularized formulations to solver-ready cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Generic Conic Canonicalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph-and-graph reduction from convex models to a product-cone program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every nonlinear atom in a finite-dimensional convex model has an exact conic epigraph or graph representation using a closed convex cone. After introducing auxiliary variables, collect all canonical variables in \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\). For closed convex cones \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{a_i}\), let \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_p\subseteq\mathbb{R}^a\), where \(a=\sum_{i=1}^p a_i\). With \(c\in\mathbb{R}^d\), \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{a\times d}\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^a\), \(N\in\mathbb{R}^{e\times d}\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}^e\), the assembled canonical problem has the form \[\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}\;c^\top z\quad\text{subject to}\quad Mz+q\in K,\qquad Nz=r.\] If every atom representation is exact and the compositions obey the modeling system's convexity rules, eliminating the auxiliary variables recovers the original feasible set and objective epigraph. Thus the canonicalization preserves feasibility, optimal value, and the original-variable minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact finite-dimensional conic representations of all atoms can be assembled into one affine product-cone problem without changing the original optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: Every nonlinear atom has an exact finite-dimensional representation using a closed convex cone \(K_i\).
All compositions satisfy the modeling system's convexity rules, and all displayed matrices and vectors have the stated compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection of the canonical feasible set and objective epigraph onto the original variables reproduces the original epigraphical formulation.

notation.meaning: product of primitive closed convex cones
vector collecting original and auxiliary canonical variables

children.title: Proximal-Projection Operator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Operator structure exposed by penalties and constraint sets.

children.title: Coordinate-Thresholding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Separable proximal structure for coordinate-sparse penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Thresholding Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise proximal interface for the weighted one-norm penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), stepsize \(\gamma>0\), and weights \(w_i\ge0\), define \(R(x)=\lambda\sum_{i=1}^n w_i|x_i|\). The proximal point \[x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(v):=\arg\min_x\left\{R(x)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert x-v\rVert_2^2\right\}\] is computed independently by coordinates: \[x_i^+=\operatorname{sign}(v_i)\max\{|v_i|-\gamma\lambda w_i,0\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] A proximal-gradient interface supplies \(v=x^k-\gamma\nabla f(x^k)\) and returns \(x^{k+1}=x^+\); stopping may use a prescribed norm of \(x^{k+1}-x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted one-norm proximal operator is coordinatewise soft thresholding and directly supplies the update in proximal-gradient methods.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at the current iterate when the proximal-gradient interface is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(v)\) equals the displayed coordinatewise soft-thresholding vector.

notation.meaning: proximal operator of the scaled penalty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The soft-thresholding formula and algorithm role fit the coordinate-thresholding container, but no inspectable source supports the proximal formula or interface.

children.title: Block-Thresholding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Group-separable proximal structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Thresholding Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Groupwise proximal interface for a nonoverlapping weighted group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and define \(R(x)=\lambda\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\lVert x_g\rVert_2\), with \(w_g\ge0\). For \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\gamma>0\), compute each block independently by \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(v)\bigr)_g=\begin{cases}\left(1-\dfrac{\gamma\lambda w_g}{\lVert v_g\rVert_2}\right)_+v_g,&v_g\ne0,\\0,&v_g=0.\end{cases}\] Thus a proximal-gradient method initializes \(v=x^k-\gamma\nabla f(x^k)\), applies this block shrinkage, and outputs the assembled vector as \(x^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonoverlapping group-norm proximal operator separates by groups and shrinks each block radially toward zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a finite partition of the coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled block-shrinkage vector is the unique minimizer defining \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(v)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonoverlapping block-shrinkage formula is precise and fits the algorithmic interface, but it has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Nested Proximal Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Composed proximal structure for multi-penalty and hierarchical models.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Proximal Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus lifting for sums whose individual proximal maps are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,r_1,\ldots,r_p:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions. The multi-penalty problem \[\min_x\;f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p r_j(x)\] is equivalently lifted to \[\min_{x,z_1,\ldots,z_p}\;f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p r_j(z_j)\quad\text{subject to}\quad z_j=x\quad(j=1,\ldots,p).\] This representation exposes each \(r_j\) through its own proximal interface \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r_j}\). In general, \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\sum_j r_j}\) must not be replaced by the simple composition of the individual proximal maps without additional structural conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus lifting separates multiple penalties so algorithms can call their proximal maps individually; naive composition is generally invalid.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f,r_j\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The lifted problem is feasible and has finite infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(z_j\) from the lifted formulation exactly recovers the original problem.

notation.meaning: local copy associated with penalty j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a consensus-splitting representation for multiple penalties, not a nested or composed proximal interface for hierarchical models. It belongs in the splitting family and does not fit this immutable terminal container.

children.title: Constraint-Set Operator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Constraint-set operations supporting projected and conditional-gradient methods.

children.title: Euclidean-Projection Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Exact or structured projection access for constrained regularized formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean-Projection Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection oracle for a nonempty closed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Its Euclidean-projection interface maps any \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) to \[\Pi_C(v):=\arg\min_{x\in C}\frac12\lVert x-v\rVert_2^2.\] The minimizer exists and is unique. Equivalently, \(p=\Pi_C(v)\) exactly when \(p\in C\) and \[\langle v-p,x-p\rangle\le0\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.\] Thus a solver-facing projection oracle accepts \(v\) and returns the uniquely characterized point \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean projection returns the unique feasible point nearest the query vector and is characterized by a variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\Pi_C(v)\) exists uniquely and satisfies the displayed variational inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection definition, uniqueness claim, and variational characterization are correct and locally relevant, but the existence-and-characterization theorem lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Linear-Minimization Oracle Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Linear-oracle access over regularization constraint sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Minimization Oracle Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear optimization oracle over a compact convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. A linear-minimization oracle returns, for each query \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a point \[s(g)\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle g,s\rangle.\] Compactness guarantees that the argmin is nonempty. In a conditional-gradient interface at \(x^k\in C\) for a function \(f\) differentiable at \(x^k\), query \(g=\nabla f(x^k)\), obtain \(s^k=s(g)\), and form \[x^{k+1}=(1-\eta_k)x^k+\eta_k s^k,\qquad \eta_k\in[0,1].\] Convexity of \(C\) then guarantees \(x^{k+1}\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-minimization oracle returns a feasible minimizer of a queried linear objective; conditional gradient takes a feasible convex-combination step toward that point.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\in C\), and \(f\) is differentiable at \(x^k\), for the conditional-gradient use.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle output satisfies \(\langle g,s(g)\rangle\le\langle g,x\rangle\) for every \(x\in C\), and the displayed conditional-gradient update lies in \(C\).

children.title: Constraint-Set Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric features determining the availability of projection or oracle access.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-cone characterization linking projection and linear minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x\in C\), define \[N_C(x):=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle u,y-x\rangle\le0\ \text{for all }y\in C\}.\] Then \(x=\Pi_C(v)\) if and only if \(v-x\in N_C(x)\). If the linear minimum is attained, \(x\in\arg\min_{y\in C}\langle g,y\rangle\) if and only if \(-g\in N_C(x)\). Hence projection and linear-minimization interfaces interrogate the same normal geometry with different query relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection and linear minimization are both characterized by membership in the feasible set's normal cone.
assumptions_latex: The stated linear minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=\Pi_C(v)\iff v-x\in N_C(x)\), and \(x\in\arg\min_{y\in C}\langle g,y\rangle\iff-g\in N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both normal-cone equivalences are correct and match the geometry container, but neither is supported by an inspectable citation.

children.title: Operator-Choice Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem classes favoring projection access versus linear-oracle access.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Choice Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for projection-based and linear-oracle-based constrained updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing a differentiable convex function \(f\) over \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a projected-gradient interface is valid when \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex and the oracle computes \(\Pi_C\); it updates \[x^{k+1}=\Pi_C\bigl(x^k-\gamma_k\nabla f(x^k)\bigr),\qquad \gamma_k>0.\] A conditional-gradient interface is valid when \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex and a linear-minimization oracle is available; it updates \[s^k\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x^k),s\rangle,\qquad x^{k+1}=(1-\eta_k)x^k+\eta_k s^k,\quad\eta_k\in[0,1].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection-based updates require a projection oracle; conditional-gradient updates require compact convex geometry and a linear-minimization oracle.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on a neighborhood of \(C\).
The chosen oracle returns an exact solution of its defining subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each displayed update remains in \(C\) whenever \(x^k\in C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated assumptions suffice for feasibility of the two exact-oracle updates and the condition role fits the container, but no source locator supports the operator regimes.

children.title: Splitting-Dual Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Reformulations exposing separability, linear operators, or simpler dual geometry.

children.title: Loss–Regularizer Splitting
children.top_down_role: Variable separation between data fit and regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss–Regularizer Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus separation of data-fit and regularization terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,r:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions and let \(\lambda\ge0\). The regularized problem \[\min_x\;f(x)+\lambda r(x)\] has the equivalent split representation \[\min_{x,z}\;f(x)+\lambda r(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x-z=0.\] Its unscaled augmented Lagrangian with multiplier \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and parameter \(\rho>0\) is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,z,y)=f(x)+\lambda r(z)+\langle y,x-z\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-z\rVert_2^2.\] The split exposes separate loss and regularizer subproblems while preserving the original primal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating the variable and enforcing consensus separates the loss from the regularizer without changing the primal problem.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(r\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(z\) using \(x=z\) recovers the original objective and minimizers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The consensus split and augmented Lagrangian are correctly stated and fit the representation container, but an operator-splitting or augmented-Lagrangian source with a specific locator is missing.

children.title: Transform Splitting
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable interfaces for generalized Lasso and total variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Transform Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-variable form for penalties applied through a linear transform.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(r:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions, let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and let \(\lambda\ge0\). The transformed-penalty problem \[\min_x\;f(x)+\lambda r(Dx)\] is equivalent to \[\min_{x,z}\;f(x)+\lambda r(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Dx-z=0.\] The constraint isolates the transform from the penalty, permitting separate linear-system and proximal interfaces. Generalized Lasso uses \(r(z)=\lVert z\rVert_1\); discrete total variation uses a difference operator for \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing a variable for the transformed coefficients separates a composite penalty into a linear constraint and a direct penalty term.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(r\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection onto the \(x\)-coordinate of the split feasible set preserves the original objective values and minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-variable consensus form for a finite sum of closed convex local objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each worker hold a proper closed convex function \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(r:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex. The problem \[\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}\;r(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)\] has the equivalent consensus representation \[\min_{z,x_1,\ldots,x_m}\;r(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Feasible points correspond bijectively through \(x_i=z\), so both formulations have the same objective values and minimizers in \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replicate the common model at each worker and impose equality with a global variable; feasibility then recovers exactly the original finite-sum problem.
assumptions_latex: \(f_1,\ldots,f_m\) and \(r\) are proper closed convex functions.
The primal problem has at least one feasible point of finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_z[r(z)+\sum_i f_i(z)]\) equals the projection onto \(z\) of the consensus solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Partitioned Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-partitioned empirical-risk form with local losses and a shared parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition observations into disjoint index sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\). For convex losses \(\ell_j:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\), data vectors \(a_j\in\mathbb{R}^d\), responses \(b_j\), and a proper closed convex regularizer \(r\), define \(f_i(x)=\sum_{j\in I_i}\ell_j(a_j^\top x,b_j)\). Then \[\min_x\;r(x)+\sum_j\ell_j(a_j^\top x,b_j)\] is equivalently \[\min_{z,x_1,\ldots,x_m}\;r(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \text{for every }i.\] Each worker evaluates only its local rows, while consensus couples the replicated parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign disjoint observation rows to workers, form one local loss per worker, replicate the model, and enforce agreement among all copies.
assumptions_latex: \(\{I_i\}_{i=1}^m\) is a partition of the observation indices.
Each loss is convex in its prediction argument, and \(r\) is proper closed convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Partitioned Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-partitioned linear-prediction form coupled through per-sample prediction variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feature matrix be column-partitioned as \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), and suppose \(r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\). For a proper closed convex loss \(L:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\;L\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i\right)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\] is equivalently \[\min_{u,u_1,\ldots,u_m,x_1,\ldots,x_m}\;L(u)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad u=\sum_{i=1}^m u_i,\quad u_i=A_i x_i.\] Thus workers compute local prediction contributions, while only their sum enters the loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With columns distributed across workers, split the linear predictor into local contributions and couple workers by requiring their contributions to sum to the global prediction.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and every \(r_i\) are proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(u\) and \(u_i\) recovers the original feature-partitioned objective exactly.

children.title: Communication Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Scalability limits arising from synchronization, transfer volume, or network topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-round payload lower bound for exact dense consensus-message transmission.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a synchronous consensus method on a graph \(G=(V,E)\) in which every directed edge transmits an arbitrary dense vector in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) exactly once per round, using a fixed-width representation of \(b\) bits per coordinate. One round communicates \(2|E|d\) scalars, hence exactly \(2|E|db\) payload bits. After \(T\) rounds the payload is \(2T|E|db\) bits, excluding headers and synchronization. Consequently, when local computation is cheaper than transmitting \(d\)-vectors, reducing arithmetic alone cannot remove the communication bottleneck; compression, sparsification, fewer rounds, or a different splitting is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact exchange of one dense model vector in each direction on every edge costs 2|E|d scalars per round and scales linearly with rounds.
assumptions_latex: Each endpoint sends one dense \(d\)-vector across every incident edge per round.
Each coordinate uses exactly \(b\) payload bits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The payload after \(T\) rounds is \(2T|E|db\) bits.
review_flags: The counting claim is model-dependent, and no supplied locator documents this communication model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the Communication Bottlenecks leaf, and the payload count follows under the stated bidirectional fixed-width model. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions, and let \(A:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be linear. Fenchel conjugacy gives \[f(Ax)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{\langle Ax,y\rangle-f^*(y)\}.\] Therefore \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\{f(Ax)+g(x)\}=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\mathcal{L}(x,y),\qquad \mathcal{L}(x,y)=g(x)+\langle Ax,y\rangle-f^*(y).\] The function \(\mathcal{L}\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\). If there exists \(x_0\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\) with \(Ax_0\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), and the primal value is finite, then \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\mathcal{L}(x,y)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\mathcal{L}(x,y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugating the loss converts a regularized composite objective into a convex-concave saddle representation; an explicit relative-interior qualification gives equality of its primal and dual minimax values.

children.title: Primal–Dual Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient optimality relations linking primal and Fenchel-dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \[\inf_x\;f(Ax)+g(x),\qquad \sup_y\;-f^*(y)-g^*(-A^\top y),\] assume strong duality and attainment. A feasible pair \((x^*,y^*)\) is primal-dual optimal if and only if \[y^*\in\partial f(Ax^*),\qquad -A^\top y^*\in\partial g(x^*).\] Equivalently, both Fenchel-Young gaps vanish. These inclusions are locally verifiable from subgradient oracles and certify that the primal-dual gap \[f(Ax^*)+g(x^*)+f^*(y^*)+g^*(-A^\top y^*)\] equals zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong duality and attainment, two subgradient inclusions exactly characterize matching primal and dual optima and certify a zero primal-dual gap.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions, and \(A\) is linear.
The associated primal and Fenchel-dual problems attain equal finite optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^*,y^*)\) is primal-dual optimal exactly when \(y^*\in\partial f(Ax^*)\) and \(-A^\top y^*\in\partial g(x^*)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Driven Representation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation choice determined by which primal or dual geometry admits tractable operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P(x)=f(Ax)+g(x)\), equivalent primal, dual, and saddle representations expose different primitive operations. A primal proximal representation is directly implementable when \(\operatorname{prox}_{\tau g}\) and multiplication by \(A,A^\top\) are tractable; a dual proximal representation is directly implementable when \(\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma f^*}\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\tau g^*}\) are tractable; and the saddle representation permits separate use of \(\operatorname{prox}_{\tau g}\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma f^*}\). Thus an equivalent representation is solver-compatible precisely relative to the available proximal, projection, linear-map, or linear-minimization oracles; equivalence of optimal values alone does not imply equal computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose among primal, dual, and saddle forms according to which side provides tractable proximal or projection operations and favorable linear-map geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions, and \(A\) is linear.
The compared formulations satisfy the qualification needed for equal optimal values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential solution of a finite regularization grid using preceding solutions as initial states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given parameters \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_K>0\), objectives \(F_k(x)=L(x)+\lambda_k R(x)\), an initial state \(x^{(0)}\), a solver map \(S(F,x,\varepsilon)\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\), order the grid so consecutive parameters are adjacent along the desired path. knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Descent Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or proximal cyclic coordinate minimization for a composite convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^d r_j(x_j)\), where \(f\) is differentiable convex and each \(r_j\) is proper closed convex. Given \(x^0\), coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_j>0\), a coordinate rule \(j_k\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\), update only coordinate \(j_k\) by \[x_{j_k}^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{\nabla_{j_k}f(x^k)(u-x_{j_k}^k)+\frac{L_{j_k}}{2}(u-x_{j_k}^k)^2+r_{j_k}(u)\right\},\] leaving all other coordinates unchanged. Stop when a prescribed composite-gradient residual is at most \(\varepsilon\), and return the final iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, minimize a one-coordinate quadratic upper model plus that coordinate's regularizer, leaving every other coordinate fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex differentiable with coordinate-wise Lipschitz gradients.
Each \(r_j\) is proper closed convex and has a computable scalar proximal map.
The coordinate rule visits every coordinate repeatedly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update is a well-defined coordinate proximal-gradient step for \(F\), and the output satisfies the chosen residual tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Descent Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal block-coordinate minimization for a block-separable composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) and let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\), with differentiable convex \(f\). Given \(x^0\), positive definite block metrics \(H_i\), a block rule \(i_k\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\), compute \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u}\left\{\langle\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k),u-x_{i_k}^k\rangle+\frac12\|u-x_{i_k}^k\|_{H_{i_k}}^2+r_{i_k}(u)\right\},\] and set \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for \(j\ne i_k\). Stop when a specified block composite-gradient residual does not exceed \(\varepsilon\), and return the final iterate.

Each \(r_i\) is proper closed convex with a computable metric proximal map.
The block rule visits every block repeatedly.
