knowledge_statements.title: Separable-Structure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural predicate enabling independent coordinate or block regularizer operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a product space \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and a partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\). A proper closed convex regularizer \(R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is block separable with respect to this partition when there exist proper closed convex functions \(r_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) such that \[R(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\quad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Under the product Euclidean metric, this condition implies \[\operatorname{prox}_{\tau R}(x)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\tau r_1}(x_1),\ldots,\operatorname{prox}_{\tau r_m}(x_m)\bigr)\quad(\tau>0),\] so regularizer subproblems decouple across blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularizer is block separable when it is a sum of functions of disjoint blocks; its Euclidean proximal map then decomposes blockwise.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) is a finite-dimensional product Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Block separability of \(R\) yields a Cartesian product decomposition of \(\operatorname{prox}_{\tau R}\) for every \(\tau>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(q_B(d)=g_B^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12 d^{\mathsf T}H_Bd+\sum_{j\in B}r_j(d_j)\), with \(H_B\succeq0\) and proper closed convex \(r_j\). knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Path Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate dual-residual continuation interface for the squared-loss Lasso path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a decreasing interval or sequence of values of \(\lambda>0\). On each nondegenerate segment, maintain the primal support \(A\), its fixed sign vector \(s\), and \(u(\lambda)=y-X_A\beta_A(\lambda)\), where \(X_A\) has full column rank and \(\beta_A(\lambda)=(X_A^{\mathsf T}X_A)^{-1}(X_A^{\mathsf T}y-\lambda s)\). The residual must satisfy \(\lVert X^{\mathsf T}u(\lambda)\rVert_\infty\leq\lambda\) and \(X_A^{\mathsf T}u(\lambda)=\lambda s\). Continue to the largest lower value of \(\lambda\) at which an inactive dual constraint becomes tight or an active primal coefficient reaches zero, then update the active equations. Ties, rank loss, and other degeneracies must be passed to a declared degeneracy policy rather than treated as a unique one-coordinate event.

children.title: Primal–Dual Path Correspondence

assumptions_latex: The Lasso primal problem is \(\min_\beta \tfrac12\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\), with \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal and dual path points correspond through \(u^*=y-X\beta^*\) and \(\theta^*=u^*/\lambda\). Their active relations satisfy \(x_j^{\mathsf T}\theta^*=\operatorname{sign}(\beta_j^*)\) whenever \(\beta_j^*\neq0\), and \(\lvert x_j^{\mathsf T}\theta^*\rvert\leq1\) otherwise.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel primal-dual correspondence for the squared-loss Lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual problem is \(\max_{\theta:\,\lVert X^{\mathsf T}\theta\rVert_\infty\leq1}\lambda y^{\mathsf T}\theta-\tfrac12\lambda^2\lVert\theta\rVert_2^2\). A primal-dual pair \((\beta^*,\theta^*)\) is optimal if and only if \(y-X\beta^*=\lambda\theta^*\) and \(X^{\mathsf T}\theta^*\in\partial\lVert\beta^*\rVert_1\). Equivalently, with \(u^*=\lambda\theta^*\), dual feasibility is \(\lVert X^{\mathsf T}u^*\rVert_\infty\leq\lambda\); every nonzero primal coefficient makes the corresponding dual constraint tight with its sign, while a strictly slack dual constraint forces that coefficient to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lasso residual scales to the dual solution, and the subgradient equations match nonzero primal coefficients with tight signed dual constraints.

Degeneracy occurs if two or more inactive correlations become tight at the same \(\lambda_k\), two or more active coefficients reach zero simultaneously, an entry and exit coincide, or \(X_A^{\mathsf T}X_A\) is singular. assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\).

children.title: Certificate-Disagreement Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where gap-based and residual-based accuracy assessments diverge.

assumptions_latex: Only convexity is assumed; no uniform strong convexity, error bound, or metric subregularity constant is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No universal function forcing objective accuracy from a small stationarity residual exists over this class.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit convex family separates residual size from objective error
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and gap certificates need not agree without quantitative conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a>0\), let \(F_a(x)=a|x|\), whose minimum value is \(0\) at \(x^\star=0\), and take \(x_a=1/a\). Then \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_a(x_a))=a\to0\) as \(a\downarrow0\), while \(F_a(x_a)-F_a(x^\star)=1\). Thus arbitrarily small stationarity residuals can coexist with fixed objective error across convex problems. A residual stopping rule and a duality-gap stopping rule are quantitatively comparable only after adding a uniform error-bound or conditioning assumption.

children.title: Identifiability-Degeneracy Boundary
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity caused by nullspaces, redundant representations, and indistinguishable supports.

children.title: Measurement Nonidentifiability
children.top_down_role: Failure of the observation operator to separate admissible structured parameters.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is the admissible structured parameter class.
Observations are generated by the linear map \(A:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((\mathcal M-\mathcal M)\cap\ker A\neq\{0\}\), exact identification from noiseless measurements is impossible on \(\mathcal M\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: injectivity on the model class is equivalent to a trivial kernel intersection with its difference set
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless injectivity boundary for a linear observation operator on a structured model class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Measurement nonidentifiability occurs when there exist distinct \(u,v\in\mathcal M\) with \(Au=Av\). Equivalently, \((\mathcal M-\mathcal M)\cap\ker A\neq\{0\}\). For such a pair, every reconstruction rule receiving the common noiseless measurement \(Au=Av\) must return the same output under both admissible parameters and therefore cannot recover both exactly. Hence no choice of convex regularizer or optimization accuracy can provide uniform exact recovery on \(\mathcal M\) unless \(A\) is injective on \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact recovery is impossible when two distinct admissible structured parameters produce the same measurement.
knowledge_statements.title: Measurement Nonidentifiability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind exactly matches the topic role. The injectivity characterization and impossibility statement are precise, but no source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Support Aliasing
children.top_down_role: Distinct sparse supports producing identical or nearly identical observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Support Aliasing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and approximate aliasing of sparse supports under a linear measurement map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\), let \(s\in\mathbb{N}\), and let \(\eta\ge 0\). Distinct supports \(S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) with \(|S|,|T|\le s\) are \(\eta\)-aliased if there exist vectors \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^p\) satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}(u)=S\), \(\operatorname{supp}(v)=T\), and \(\|A(u-v)\|_2\le\eta\). Exact support aliasing is the case \(\eta=0\). In that case observations \(y=Au=Av\) cannot determine whether the generating support was \(S\) or \(T\); for \(\eta>0\), the two supports are indistinguishable at any observation tolerance at least \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct sparse supports are aliased when their coefficient vectors produce identical, or tolerance-indistinguishable, linear observations; the observations then cannot identify the generating support.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\) is a fixed linear measurement matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|A(u-v)\|_2\le\eta\) makes \(S\) and \(T\) observationally indistinguishable at tolerance \(\eta\).

notation.meaning: indices of the nonzero coordinates of u

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct finite-dimensional definition of sparse-support aliasing under a linear map
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and exact-aliasing definition fit the terminal container, but no inspectable citation supports the terminology or the approximate indistinguishability claim. The latter also depends on the observation tolerance or noise model being used.

children.title: Representation Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Multiple coefficient or latent decompositions representing the same fitted object.

assumptions_latex: \(D:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathcal{H}\) is linear, where \(\mathcal{H}\) is a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(D\alpha=D\beta\) with \(\alpha\ne\beta\), observations and losses depending only on the fitted object cannot identify which coefficient vector generated that object; if also \(R(\alpha)=R(\beta)\), the regularized objective assigns them equal values.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary characterization of representation nonuniqueness through a nontrivial kernel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noninjective coefficient-to-object maps in regularized learning formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathcal{H}\) be linear, where \(\mathcal{H}\) is a real Hilbert space. Representation nonuniqueness occurs at \(x\in\mathcal{H}\) when there exist distinct \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p\) such that \(D\alpha=D\beta=x\). For any fixed \(\alpha\) satisfying \(D\alpha=x\), another vector \(\beta\) represents the same object if and only if \(\beta-\alpha\in\ker D\). Consequently, observations and losses depending only on \(D\gamma\) cannot distinguish such coefficient vectors. If \(L:\mathcal{H}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(R:\mathbb{R}^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and \(R(\alpha)=R(\beta)\), then \(L(D\gamma)+\lambda R(\gamma)\) has the same value at \(\gamma=\alpha\) and \(\gamma=\beta\) for every \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fitted object has a nonunique representation when two distinct coefficient vectors map to it. Object-level observations and losses cannot distinguish those vectors, and equal regularizer values preserve the tie in the regularized objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Nonuniqueness

children.title: Scale-Calibration Failure Family
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by incompatible units, weights, budgets, or noise calibration.

children.title: Feature-Scale Distortion
children.top_down_role: Unintended selection preferences caused by inconsistent feature scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Scale Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate rescaling changes an unweighted coefficient penalty despite preserving fitted predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p} L(X\beta)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p w_j|\beta_j|\), with \(w_j>0\). For positive scale factors \(c_j\), set \(X'_j=c_jX_j\) and \(\beta'_j=\beta_j/c_j\), so \(X'\beta'=X\beta\). The transformed penalty is \(\sum_j w_j|\beta_j|/c_j\). Hence unequal \(c_j\) alter the effective feature penalties and can change the selected support although every fitted prediction remains available. Scale invariance holds under this reparameterization precisely when transformed weights satisfy \(w'_j=c_jw_j\), because then \(w'_j|\beta'_j|=w_j|\beta_j|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling feature columns preserves predictions but changes unweighted coefficient penalties, creating artificial selection preferences unless penalty weights are rescaled correspondingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feature rescaling preserves the optimization problem exactly only when \(w'_j=c_jw_j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic reparameterization of weighted lasso penalties
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic reparameterization is precise, and failure_boundary is the correct role for this leaf. However, the record has no authoritative citation or inspectable locator supporting the feature-scaling interpretation and weighting prescription.

children.title: Group-Size Distortion
children.top_down_role: Systematic preference for or against groups of different sizes.

knowledge_statements.title: Group-Size Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Group penalties induce size-dependent thresholds unless their weights calibrate group dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let disjoint groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_K\) partition the coordinates and consider orthonormal grouped least squares, \(\min_\beta \frac12\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\sum_{g=1}^K w_g\|\beta_{G_g}\|_2\), with \(X^\top X=I\). Group \(g\) is selected exactly when \(\|X_{G_g}^\top y\|_2>\lambda w_g\). Under pure isotropic Gaussian noise with variance \(\sigma^2\), \(\|X_{G_g}^\top y\|_2/\sigma\) has a chi distribution with \(|G_g|\) degrees of freedom. Thus equal weights impose unequal null selection probabilities across group sizes; dimension-calibrated weights or quantiles are required for comparable thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal group-lasso weights create size-dependent false-selection rates because larger groups have larger noise-score norms, even under orthonormal designs.
assumptions_latex: The groups are disjoint and \(X^\top X=I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With constant \(w_g\), the null probability \(\Pr(\|X_{G_g}^\top y\|_2>\lambda w_g)\) depends on \(|G_g|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orthonormal group-lasso threshold and Gaussian chi-score calculation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthonormal group-lasso threshold and chi-distribution calculation fit the group-size distortion leaf, but neither claim has an inspectable supporting citation. A source should specifically cover the block soft-thresholding rule and group-size calibration under Gaussian noise.

children.title: Noise-Budget Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility or excessive fitting caused by an incorrect residual budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Budget Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-constrained estimation fails when its budget is below or far above attainable noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For data \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), design \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\), regularizer \(R\), and budget \(\varepsilon\ge0\), consider \(\min_\beta R(\beta)\) subject to \(\|y-X\beta\|_2\le\varepsilon\). Let \(r_*=\inf_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\|y-X\beta\|_2\). If \(\varepsilon<r_*\), the problem is infeasible. If \(y=X\beta^\star+e\) and \(\varepsilon\ge\|e\|_2\), then \(\beta^\star\) is feasible; however, an excessively large budget enlarges the feasible set and may admit lower-regularizer solutions with substantially larger residuals, so the constraint no longer enforces the intended fit accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual budget below the best attainable residual causes infeasibility; an overly large budget admits weakly fitting, overly regularized solutions.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon<r_*\) implies infeasibility, whereas increasing \(\varepsilon\) monotonically enlarges the feasible set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility follows directly from the minimum attainable residual
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The infeasibility boundary and feasible-set monotonicity are mathematically consistent and fit the terminal container. The broader excessive-budget interpretation remains uncited, and no source reference with a section, theorem, or page locator is present.

children.title: Parameter-Search Truncation
children.top_down_role: Omission of relevant model regimes from an inadequate regularization path or grid.

assumptions_latex: For every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), \(S(\lambda)\) is the solution set of the stated penalized problem.
\(M:\mathcal{B}\to\mathfrak{M}\) maps an individual solution to a model in a model space \(\mathfrak{M}\).
Only parameters in the finite grid \(G\subset\Lambda\) are evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a target model \(\mu\in\mathfrak{M}\) occurs for some \(\lambda_*\in\Lambda\) but \(\mu\notin\mathcal{M}_G\), the grid search cannot return \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: regularized solution set at parameter lambda
map extracting a model from an individual solution

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: set-theoretic characterization of regimes omitted by a finite parameter grid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite regularization search omits solution regimes outside its parameter range or between grid points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{B}\) be a parameter space, let \(L,R:\mathcal{B}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and define \(S(\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathcal{B}}\{L(\beta)+\lambda R(\beta)\}\) for \(\lambda\in\Lambda\subseteq[0,\infty)\). Let \(M:\mathcal{B}\to\mathfrak{M}\) extract a fitted model or support, and define \(\mathcal{M}(\lambda)=\{M(\beta):\beta\in S(\lambda)\}\). If a procedure inspects only a finite grid \(G\subset\Lambda\), its attainable model set is \(\mathcal{M}_G=\bigcup_{\lambda\in G}\mathcal{M}(\lambda)\). Parameter-search truncation occurs when a target model \(\mu\in\mathfrak{M}\) belongs to \(\mathcal{M}(\lambda_*)\) for some \(\lambda_*\in\Lambda\) but \(\mu\notin\mathcal{M}_G\). In particular, a grid contained in \([\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\) omits any model occurring only at parameter values outside that interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated or coarse regularization grid fails for a target model when that model occurs somewhere on the full solution path but at no inspected parameter value.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Search Truncation

children.title: Regularizer–Signal Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between the chosen regularizer and the structure of the target parameter or signal.

children.title: Dense-Signal Regime
children.top_down_role: Sparse regularization applied to broadly distributed effects.

assumptions_latex: Signal approximation quality is assessed through the best \(s\)-term error in the \(\ell_1\) norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma_s(\beta^\star)_1/\sqrt{s}\) is large, a recovery bound containing this approximation term cannot by itself guarantee a small recovery error.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero coordinates of z
best s-term approximation error in the l1 norm

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard best-s-term approximation boundary for compressive sparse recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate sparsity penalties poorly approximate signals whose energy is broadly distributed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\beta^\star\in\mathbb{R}^p\) and an integer \(s\) satisfying \(1\le s<p\), define the best \(s\)-term approximation error by \(\sigma_s(\beta^\star)_1=\inf_{\|z\|_0\le s}\|\beta^\star-z\|_1\). A dense-signal regime relative to \(s\) occurs when \(\sigma_s(\beta^\star)_1\) is not small compared with \(\|\beta^\star\|_1\). A recovery bound containing an approximation term proportional to \(\sigma_s(\beta^\star)_1/\sqrt{s}\) cannot guarantee a small error from that term when it is large. This boundary distinguishes compressible dense signals, for which the best sparse approximation error is small, from signals lacking an accurate sparse approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse regularization loses its approximation advantage when no support of the prescribed size captures most of the coefficient mass; a dense signal remains compatible with sparse approximation only when it is compressible.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Signal Regime

children.title: Incorrect Group, Graph, or Order Structure
children.top_down_role: Structural priors that couple, select, or exclude inappropriate parameters.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{A}\subseteq2^{\{1,\ldots,p\}}\) is the family of support patterns permitted by a hard structural model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{supp}(\beta^\star)\notin\mathcal{A}\), an estimator constrained to supports in \(\mathcal{A}\) cannot recover \(\beta^\star\) exactly and incurs coefficient error at least \(d_{\mathcal{A}}(\beta^\star)\).

notation.meaning: support patterns permitted by the structural model
Euclidean distance from the target to vectors with permitted supports

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distance-to-model formulation of hard structural-prior misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A hard group, graph, or order model excludes the signal's actual structural pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{A}\subseteq2^{\{1,\ldots,p\}}\) be the support family permitted by a group, graph, or order model, and let \(\beta^\star\in\mathbb{R}^p\). Structural misspecification occurs when \(\operatorname{supp}(\beta^\star)\notin\mathcal{A}\). For an estimator constrained by \(\operatorname{supp}(\beta)\in\mathcal{A}\), exact recovery of \(\beta^\star\) is then impossible, even with noiseless identifiable observations. Define \(d_{\mathcal{A}}(\beta^\star)=\inf\{\|\beta^\star-z\|_2:\operatorname{supp}(z)\in\mathcal{A}\}\). Every estimator satisfying the hard structural constraint has coefficient error at least \(d_{\mathcal{A}}(\beta^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wrong hard group, graph, or order model fails when the true support is outside its permitted family, ruling out exact recovery and creating a distance-to-model error floor.
knowledge_statements.title: Incorrect Group, Graph, or Order Structure

children.title: Representation Mismatch Family
children.top_down_role: Failure of the assumed synthesis or analysis representation.

children.title: Basis Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failure caused by an unsuitable fixed coordinate representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A signal sparse in one basis need not be sparse in the basis used for regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U,V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be orthogonal bases and let \(x=U\alpha\). A formulation using the basis \(V\) penalizes \(\beta=V^\top x=V^\top U\alpha\). Relative to sparsity level \(s\), basis mismatch occurs when \(\|\alpha\|_0\le s\) but \(\beta\) is not sparse or compressible, as measured by a large best \(s\)-term error \(\sigma_s(\beta)_1\). Consequently, an \(\ell_1\) penalty in the \(V\)-coordinates does not exploit the actual sparse representation in \(U\), and recovery guarantees expressed through \(\sigma_s(\beta)_1\) can become noninformative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis mismatch occurs when a signal sparse in its correct basis becomes dense in the basis whose coefficients are penalized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large \(\sigma_s(V^\top U\alpha)_1\) removes the sparse-approximation advantage of regularization in basis \(V\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coordinate-change characterization of sparsity basis mismatch
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement cleanly distinguishes the true and assumed orthogonal bases and fits the Basis Mismatch failure-boundary leaf. No inspectable source supports the best-term approximation interpretation or the claim about recovery guarantees.

children.title: Dictionary Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failure caused by inaccurate, incomplete, or poorly adapted dictionary atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Dictionary Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse synthesis with an assumed dictionary cannot exactly represent signals generated by a different dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_0,D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), let \(x=D_0\alpha^\star\), and suppose \(\|\alpha^\star\|_0\le s\). The assumed dictionary \(D\) is mismatched for \(x\) at sparsity \(s\) when \(x\notin\{D\alpha:\|\alpha\|_0\le s\}\). Define \(\delta_s(x;D)=\inf_{\|\alpha\|_0\le s}\|x-D\alpha\|_2\). If \(\delta_s(x;D)>0\), every synthesis estimator restricted to \(s\)-sparse coefficients in \(D\) has representation error at least \(\delta_s(x;D)\), even with noiseless direct observation of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assumed dictionary is mismatched when it has no sufficiently sparse representation of the true signal, producing irreducible synthesis error even without noise.
assumptions_latex: The assumed synthesis model uses \(D\) and at most \(s\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_s(x;D)>0\) is an irreducible error floor for every \(s\)-sparse synthesis representation using \(D\).

notation.meaning: best s-sparse synthesis error under D

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: best sparse dictionary-approximation error gives the exact mismatch boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distance-to-model formulation is internally consistent and fits Dictionary Mismatch. It still requires an authoritative dictionary-approximation source with a specific locator; none is supplied.

children.title: Analysis-Representation Failure
children.top_down_role: Mismatch affecting transform-domain or cosparse structural assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Analysis-Representation Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An analysis-cosparse model fails when the target has many nonzero analyzed coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\) be an analysis operator and let \(x^\star\in\mathbb{R}^n\). An analysis model of cosparsity at least \(\ell\) assumes \(|\{i:(\Omega x^\star)_i=0\}|\ge\ell\), equivalently \(\|\Omega x^\star\|_0\le q-\ell\). Analysis-representation failure at level \(\ell\) occurs when this inequality is false. Then \(x^\star\) lies outside the union of analysis subspaces defined by at least \(\ell\) zero rows. Any estimator imposing that union as a hard constraint cannot recover \(x^\star\) exactly, even from noiseless direct observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analysis-cosparse formulation fails when the target has fewer analyzed zeros than assumed, placing it outside the permitted union of subspaces.
assumptions_latex: The model requires analysis cosparsity at least \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\|\Omega x^\star\|_0>q-\ell\), exact recovery under the hard cosparsity constraint is impossible.

notation.meaning: required number of zero analysis coefficients
number of rows of the analysis operator

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining support condition for the finite-dimensional analysis-cosparse model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Synthesis-Representation Failure
children.top_down_role: Mismatch affecting sparse coefficient generation through dictionary atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Synthesis-Representation Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sparse synthesis model fails when the target lacks an adequately sparse dictionary expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), let \(x^\star\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and fix \(s\in\mathbb{N}\). The \(s\)-sparse synthesis model is \(\mathcal{S}_s(D)=\{D\alpha:\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ \|\alpha\|_0\le s\}\). Synthesis-representation failure occurs when \(x^\star\notin\mathcal{S}_s(D)\), equivalently when \(\delta_s(x^\star;D)=\inf_{\|\alpha\|_0\le s}\|x^\star-D\alpha\|_2>0\). Every estimator constrained to \(\mathcal{S}_s(D)\) then incurs Euclidean representation error at least \(\delta_s(x^\star;D)\), regardless of measurement quality or optimization accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse synthesis model fails when the target is outside the union generated by at most s dictionary atoms, creating an irreducible representation-error floor.
assumptions_latex: The synthesis model permits at most \(s\) nonzero coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\notin\mathcal{S}_s(D)\) implies a positive irreducible error \(\delta_s(x^\star;D)\).

notation.meaning: signals synthesized from at most s columns of D
distance from the target to the s-sparse synthesis model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distance-to-model characterization of sparse synthesis failure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sparse synthesis model and distance-to-model failure boundary are precise and appropriate for this leaf. An inspectable source is nevertheless required for the model definition and irreducible-error interpretation.

children.title: Nonuniform Structured Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Signals whose complexity varies systematically across levels, blocks, or scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform Structured Sparsity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch between uniform group regularization and level-dependent noise or signal scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the coordinates be partitioned into groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\), and consider \(\widehat\beta\in\arg\min_b \tfrac12\lVert y-Xb\rVert_2^2+\lambda\sum_g w_g\lVert b_{G_g}\rVert_2\). The KKT condition for excluding group \(G_g\) is \(\lVert X_{G_g}^{\mathsf T}(y-X\widehat\beta)\rVert_2\leq\lambda w_g\). If the null-group dual-noise scales \(s_g\) vary substantially while \(w_g\equiv1\), then controlling false inclusion requires \(\lambda\geq\max_g s_g\), whereas retaining an active group requires its effective signal to exceed that same threshold. Consequently, active groups at quieter levels with effective signal between their local scale and \(\max_g s_g\) are systematically excluded; weights satisfying \(w_g\propto s_g\) remove this particular scale mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform group penalties impose one threshold despite varying groupwise noise. Controlling the noisiest group can therefore erase detectable signals in quieter groups; scale-adapted weights address this mismatch.
assumptions_latex: The groupwise dual-noise magnitudes admit relevant scales \(s_g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_g\equiv1\) can force false exclusions when groupwise complexity scales are nonuniform, while \(w_g\propto s_g\) aligns the KKT thresholds with those scales.

notation.meaning: Relevant dual-noise scale for group g.
Penalty weight assigned to group g.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but no source supports the asserted groupwise scales, the global-threshold necessity, or the claim that proportional weights remove the mismatch. These statements require precise probabilistic and design assumptions.

children.title: Shrinkage-Selection Error Family
children.top_down_role: Distortion and selection error shared by convex sparse penalties.

children.title: Large-Signal Shrinkage
children.top_down_role: Persistent attenuation of strong coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Signal Shrinkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact persistent bias of the lasso under an orthonormal design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\widehat\beta\in\arg\min_b \tfrac12\lVert y-Xb\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert b\rVert_1\) with \(X^{\mathsf T}X=I\) and \(z=X^{\mathsf T}y\). Coordinatewise, \(\widehat\beta_j=\operatorname{sign}(z_j)(|z_j|-\lambda)_+\). Hence every selected coordinate satisfying \(|z_j|>\lambda\) is attenuated by exactly \(\lambda\): \(|z_j-\widehat\beta_j|=\lambda\). In the noiseless case \(y=X\beta^\star\), any coefficient with \(|\beta_j^\star|>\lambda\) remains selected but obeys \(\widehat\beta_j-\beta_j^\star=-\lambda\operatorname{sign}(\beta_j^\star)\). Thus increasing signal magnitude does not eliminate the absolute lasso shrinkage bias at fixed \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With orthonormal predictors, lasso soft-thresholds every selected coefficient by exactly the penalty level. Even arbitrarily strong noiseless coefficients retain absolute bias equal to that level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|z_j|>\lambda\Longrightarrow |z_j-\widehat\beta_j|=\lambda\), including for arbitrarily large \(|z_j|\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthonormal-design soft-thresholding statement is precise and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but the record supplies no authoritative source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Support Selection Error Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Selection errors driven by noise, correlation, and parameter calibration.

children.title: False Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Omission of relevant variables, coefficients, or groups from selected structure.

knowledge_statements.title: False Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-level false negative for a sparse estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \( eta^\star\in\mathbb R^p\) be a target coefficient vector and let \(\widehat eta\in\mathbb R^p\) be an estimator. Define the true and estimated supports by \(S^\star=\{j: eta_j^\star
eq0\}\) and \(\widehat S=\{j:\widehat eta_j
eq0\}\). A false exclusion is an index \(j\in S^\star\setminus\widehat S\); equivalently, \( eta_j^\star
eq0\) but \(\widehat eta_j=0\). The false-exclusion set is \(E_-=S^\star\setminus\widehat S\), and its count is \(|E_-|\). With a numerical activity threshold \(	au\geq0\), replace \(\widehat S\) by \(\widehat S_	au=\{j:|\widehat eta_j|>	au\}\), making the definition explicitly tolerance-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A false exclusion occurs when a truly active coefficient is absent from the estimated support. Under numerical thresholding, activity and therefore exclusion depend on the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_-=S^\star\setminus\widehat S=\{j:\beta_j^\star\neq0,\ \widehat\beta_j=0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and tolerance-dependent variant match the leaf, but no support-recovery source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: False Inclusion
children.top_down_role: Retention of irrelevant variables, coefficients, or groups in selected structure.

knowledge_statements.title: False Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-level false positive for a sparse estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \( eta^\star\in\mathbb R^p\) be a target coefficient vector and let \(\widehat eta\in\mathbb R^p\) be an estimator, with supports \(S^\star=\{j: eta_j^\star
eq0\}\) and \(\widehat S=\{j:\widehat eta_j
eq0\}\). A false inclusion is an index \(j\in\widehat S\setminus S^\star\); equivalently, \( eta_j^\star=0\) but \(\widehat eta_j
eq0\). The false-inclusion set is \(E_+=\widehat S\setminus S^\star\), and its count is \(|E_+|\). If reported activity uses a tolerance \(	au\geq0\), the operative support is \(\widehat S_	au=\{j:|\widehat eta_j|>	au\}\), so inclusions below that threshold are not counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A false inclusion occurs when an estimated support contains a truly inactive coefficient. If activity is thresholded numerically, the declared threshold determines which estimates count as included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_+=\widehat S\setminus S^\star=\{j:\beta_j^\star=0,\ \widehat\beta_j\neq0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and appropriate for the leaf, but it lacks a cited source and specific locator.

children.title: Correlation-Driven Selection Errors
children.top_down_role: Exclusion or inclusion failures associated with correlated predictors or atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlation-Driven Selection Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonidentifiable support caused by perfectly correlated predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(\lVert x\rVert_2=1\), set \(X=[x\ x]\), and observe noiseless data \(y=ax\) with \(a>\lambda>0\). For the lasso objective \(\tfrac12\lVert y-Xb\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert b\rVert_1\), every vector \(b=(t,a-\lambda-t)\) with \(0\leq t\leq a-\lambda\) is optimal. These optima have the same prediction and objective value, but include supports \(\{1\}\), \(\{2\}\), and \(\{1,2\}\). If the data-generating coefficient is \((a,0)\), some optimal solutions falsely exclude coordinate \(1\), falsely include coordinate \(2\), or do both. Perfect predictor correlation therefore prevents unique support recovery without an additional identifying convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate predictors make lasso support nonidentifiable: equally optimal solutions can select either duplicate or both, producing false exclusions and inclusions despite identical fitted values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(t,a-\lambda-t):0\leq t\leq a-\lambda\}\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_b\{\tfrac12\lVert y-Xb\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert b\rVert_1\}\), and the optimal supports differ.

notation.meaning: Design with two identical normalized columns.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duplicate-predictor construction is an appropriate counterexample and its support conclusions are consistent, but no authoritative correlated-lasso source or locator is provided.

children.title: Calibration-Driven Selection Errors
children.top_down_role: Exclusion or inclusion failures associated with regularization or noise calibration.

knowledge_statements.title: Calibration-Driven Selection Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact threshold-calibration errors for orthonormal-design lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\widehat\beta\in\arg\min_b \tfrac12\lVert y-Xb\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert b\rVert_1\) with \(X^{\mathsf T}X=I\), write \(z=X^{\mathsf T}y\). Then \(\widehat S=\{j:|z_j|>\lambda\}\). Relative to a target support \(S^\star\), calibration at level \(\lambda\) produces a false exclusion exactly when some \(j\in S^\star\) satisfies \(|z_j|\leq\lambda\), and a false inclusion exactly when some \(j\notin S^\star\) satisfies \(|z_j|>\lambda\). Thus increasing \(\lambda\) monotonically removes selected coordinates and can increase exclusions, whereas decreasing \(\lambda\) monotonically adds coordinates and can increase inclusions; calibration chooses the boundary between these opposing errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under orthonormal lasso, selection is exact thresholding at the penalty level. Raising the level favors exclusions; lowering it favors inclusions, making support error directly calibration-dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_-=\{j\in S^\star:|z_j|\leq\lambda\}\) and \(E_+=\{j\notin S^\star:|z_j|>\lambda\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthonormal-lasso threshold characterization fits the calibration-error leaf, but it has no authoritative citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Unstable Supports under Correlation
children.top_down_role: Support variability when predictors or dictionary elements are difficult to distinguish.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Supports under Correlation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support instability under duplicate or nearly duplicate predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[x\ x]\), where \(\lVert x\rVert_2=1\), and let \(y=ax\) with \(a>\lambda>0\). The lasso solution set contains every \((t,a-\lambda-t)\) for \(0\leq t\leq a-\lambda\). Hence arbitrarily small linear perturbations of the objective, such as adding \(\delta(b_1-b_2)\), select opposite endpoint solutions as the sign of \(\delta\) changes, switching the support between \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2\}\). The fitted vector remains \((a-\lambda)x\) in the zero-perturbation limit. Thus prediction can be stable while coefficient support is discontinuous when correlated columns are indistinguishable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With duplicate predictors, tiny objective perturbations can switch the selected variable while leaving the limiting prediction unchanged. Stable fitted values therefore do not imply stable supports.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta\downarrow0\) and \(\delta\uparrow0\) can select supports \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2\}\), respectively, while predictions converge to \((a-\lambda)x\).

notation.meaning: An arbitrarily small objective perturbation parameter.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample captures support instability under duplicate predictors, but the perturbation-based selection claim lacks an authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Numerical-Certificate Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Implementation boundaries that can invalidate apparent sparsity or solver conclusions.

children.title: Conditioning-Progress Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Design and transform geometry that impedes numerical optimization.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Design Geometry
children.top_down_role: Poor numerical geometry arising from correlated or unevenly scaled design variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Design Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of coefficient identifiability along nearly null design directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). If a nonzero direction \(h\) satisfies \(\lVert Xh\rVert_2\leq\epsilon\lVert h\rVert_2\), then the coefficient vectors \(\beta\) and \(\beta+h\) differ by \(\lVert h\rVert_2\) while their predictions differ by at most \(\epsilon\lVert h\rVert_2\). Consequently, a prediction perturbation of size comparable to \(\epsilon\lVert h\rVert_2\) cannot reliably distinguish these coefficients. On any admissible error cone \(C\), the restricted gain \(\gamma_C=\inf_{h\in C\setminus\{0\}}\lVert Xh\rVert_2/\lVert h\rVert_2\) controls amplification: a prediction-error certificate \(\lVert Xh\rVert_2\leq r\) yields only \(\lVert h\rVert_2\leq r/\gamma_C\), which becomes vacuous as \(\gamma_C\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly null design directions make widely separated coefficients produce nearly identical predictions. Prediction-error certificates then amplify by the reciprocal restricted gain and become ineffective as that gain vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is the relevant admissible error cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Xh\rVert_2\leq r\) and \(h\in C\) imply \(\lVert h\rVert_2\leq r/\gamma_C\); this control degenerates when \(\gamma_C\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Restricted minimum gain of the design.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary is mathematically plausible, but the restricted-cone formulation and certificate interpretation require a source specifying the relevant cone and positive-gain conditions.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Transform Geometry
children.top_down_role: Poor numerical geometry arising from linear transforms or redundant representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Transform Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning degradation induced by an invertible analysis or coordinate transform.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_\beta \tfrac12\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert D\beta\rVert_1\) with invertible \(D\), and introduce \(u=D\beta\). The smooth term in the transformed problem has Hessian \(H_u=D^{-\mathsf T}X^{\mathsf T}XD^{-1}\). Even when \(X^{\mathsf T}X\) is well-conditioned, small singular values of \(D\) can make \(\lambda_{\max}(H_u)\) large, while anisotropic singular directions can make \(\kappa(H_u)\) large. In particular, for \(X=I\), one has \(H_u=D^{-\mathsf T}D^{-1}\) and \(\kappa(H_u)=\kappa(D)^2\). Thus a poorly conditioned transform can create slow or numerically sensitive geometry solely through reparameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing variables through an ill-conditioned transform can square its condition number in the smooth Hessian, creating numerical difficulty even when the original design is perfectly conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=I\Longrightarrow \kappa(D^{-\mathsf T}D^{-1})=\kappa(D)^2\), so transform ill-conditioning directly degrades transformed geometry.

notation.meaning: Hessian of the transformed smooth loss.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transform-Hessian calculation and condition-number identity fit the leaf, but no authoritative transform-conditioning source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Slow-Progress Regimes
children.top_down_role: Optimization regimes characterized by weak practical progress under adverse geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Slow-Progress Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear convergence degradation for gradient descent on ill-conditioned quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx-b^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(H\) is symmetric positive definite with eigenvalues in \([\mu,L]\) and \(0<\mu<L\). Apply gradient descent with fixed step \(\alpha=2/(L+\mu)\). Writing \(x^\star=H^{-1}b\), \(\kappa=L/\mu>1\), and \(q=(\kappa-1)/(\kappa+1)\), every nonnegative integer \(k\) satisfies \(\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert_2\leq q^k\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert_2\). Therefore, for \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), the relative iterate-error bound \(\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert_2\) is guaranteed whenever \(k\geq\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log((\kappa+1)/(\kappa-1))\). The sufficient iteration count is of order \(\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon)\) as \(\kappa\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic with condition number strictly greater than one, optimal fixed-step gradient descent contracts the iterate error by a condition-number-dependent factor. The sufficient iteration count grows proportionally to the condition number for large condition numbers.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) with spectrum contained in \([\mu,L]\) and \(0<\mu<L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\geq\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log((\kappa+1)/(\kappa-1))\) guarantees \(\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\lVert x_0-x^\star\rVert_2\) when \(\kappa>1\).

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number of the quadratic Hessian.

children.title: Preconditioning Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of numerical behavior on scaling or geometry-adjustment choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioning Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral sensitivity of quadratic geometry to a change of variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\) be a quadratic Hessian and let the invertible change of variables be \(x=Pz\). The transformed Hessian is \(H_P=P^{\mathsf T}HP\), and its spectral condition number satisfies \(\kappa(H)/\kappa(P)^2\leq\kappa(H_P)\leq\kappa(H)\kappa(P)^2\). Thus an aligned preconditioner can reduce anisotropy, whereas an ill-scaled or misaligned transformation can worsen it by a factor as large as \(\kappa(P)^2\). Since fixed-step first-order convergence depends on the extremal eigenvalues of \(H_P\), convergence certificates and admissible step sizes are sensitive to the chosen preconditioner even though the underlying minimizer is unchanged after mapping back to \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable transformation changes the Hessian by congruence. Its condition number can improve or worsen substantially, so step sizes and convergence rates depend sensitively on preconditioner scaling and alignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(H)/\kappa(P)^2\leq\kappa(P^{\mathsf T}HP)\leq\kappa(H)\kappa(P)^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The congruence and condition-number bounds are appropriate as a preconditioning-sensitivity property, but no authoritative source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Stopping-Activity Consistency Boundary
children.top_down_role: Approximate solutions whose apparent active structure lacks certificate support.

children.title: Premature Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination before the solution reaches the accuracy needed for structural interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small iterate changes need not certify proximity to optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) and gradient descent \(x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x_k\) with \(0<\alpha<1\). A stopping rule declaring convergence when \(|x_{k+1}-x_k|\leq\tau\) accepts whenever \(\alpha|x_k|\leq\tau\). For any prescribed suboptimality level \(M>0\) and tolerance \(\tau>0\), choose \(|x_k|=\sqrt{2M}\) and \(0<\alpha\leq\tau/\sqrt{2M}\). The rule then accepts, although \(f(x_k)-f(0)=M\). Hence a small-step stopping test without a lower bound on step size or an independent residual, gap, or stationarity certificate can terminate arbitrarily far from the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small algorithmic step can satisfy an iterate-change tolerance while the objective gap remains arbitrarily large. Step-size tests alone therefore do not certify convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|x_{k+1}-x_k|\leq\tau\) does not imply any finite universal upper bound on \(f(x_k)-f^\star\) when \(\alpha\) may be arbitrarily small.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction is an appropriate premature-stopping counterexample and supports the stated absence of a step-size-independent gap bound, but it lacks an authoritative stopping-criteria source and locator.

children.title: False Activity
children.top_down_role: Apparent active variables or groups unsupported by sufficient optimization accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: False Activity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Group-regularized convex learning with activity determined by a numerical coefficient threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a finite partition of the coordinates of \(x\). A reported group \(g\in\mathcal G\) is falsely active at tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{act}}>0\) if \(\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2>\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\) while \(x_g^*=0\) for every \(x^*\in X^*\). If some \(x^*\in X^*\) satisfies \(\lVert\widehat x-x^*\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon_x\), then every group absent from all exact solutions satisfies \(\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon_x\). Consequently, the error estimate rules out false activity whenever \(\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\geq\varepsilon_x\). When \(\tau_{\mathrm{act}}<\varepsilon_x\), the estimate alone permits a truly inactive group to be reported active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A group is falsely active when its computed norm strictly exceeds the reporting threshold although every exact solution sets that group to zero. A solution-error bound rules this out when the activity threshold is at least the error bound, but not when it is smaller.
assumptions_latex: \(F_\lambda(x)=f(x)+\lambda\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\lVert x_g\rVert_2\), where \(\mathcal G\) is a finite coordinate partition, \(f\) is convex and differentiable, \(\lambda>0\), and \(w_g>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution-error estimate excludes false activity when \(\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\geq\varepsilon_x\), whereas it does not exclude false activity when \(\tau_{\mathrm{act}}<\varepsilon_x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the groupwise norm error is bounded by the full Euclidean error, and reported activity uses a strict inequality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Certificate–Support Consistency
children.top_down_role: Alignment between reported active structure and available accuracy certificates.

assumptions_latex: \(F_\lambda(x)=f(x)+\lambda\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\lVert x_g\rVert_2\), with convex differentiable \(f\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(w_g>0\).
A computed pair \((\widehat x,\widehat z)\) has stationarity residual \(r=\nabla f(\widehat x)+\lambda\widehat z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual, dual-feasibility, alignment, and strict-inactivity inequalities constitute a verifiable certificate-support consistency condition at the chosen tolerances.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: group-norm subgradient conditions link primal support to dual saturation and alignment
needs a source for this particular approximate consistency formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate KKT consistency for weighted group-norm regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{align}},\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\geq0\) and margin \(\delta>0\), the pair \((\widehat x,\widehat z)\) is certificate-support consistent when \(\lVert r\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\), \(\lVert\widehat z_g\rVert_2\leq w_g\) for every \(g\), and each reported active group satisfies
\[
\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2>\tau_{\mathrm{act}},\qquad \left\lVert\widehat z_g-w_g\frac{\widehat x_g}{\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2}\right\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{align}}.
\]
Every group certified inactive must instead satisfy \(\lVert\widehat z_g\rVert_2\leq w_g-\delta\) and \(\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2\leq\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\). Declaring a group inactive or active contrary to these respective inequalities is certificate-support inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical support is consistent only when stationarity is small, active groups align with saturated group certificates, and certified inactive groups have both small coefficients and strict dual slack.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate–Support Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the container, but this particular approximate certificate is uncited. In particular, strict dual slack is a sufficient inactive-group certification rule rather than a necessary KKT condition, while the plain statement says consistency holds only under that rule. A source or an explicit derivation of the intended sufficient-versus-necessary status is required.

children.title: Tolerance-Sensitive Activity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where selected structure changes materially with stopping tolerance.

assumptions_latex: An exact solution \(x^*\) is unique and the computed point obeys \(\lVert\widehat x-x^*\rVert_{2,\infty}\leq\varepsilon_x\).
The smallest active group magnitude is \(\beta_{\min}=\min_{g:x_g^*\neq0}\lVert x_g^*\rVert_2>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Thresholded activity is invariant throughout the stable interval; outside it, the available error information cannot distinguish every active group from every inactive group.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the stable threshold interval follows directly from coordinatewise error separation
needs a source connecting numerical stopping error to support-threshold regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable and ambiguous coefficient-threshold regimes under a groupwise solution-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the reported support by \(\widehat S(\tau)=\{g:\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2>\tau\}\) and the exact support by \(S^*=\{g:x_g^*\neq0\}\). For an inactive group, \(\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon_x\); for an active group, \(\lVert\widehat x_g\rVert_2\geq\beta_{\min}-\varepsilon_x\). Hence, if \(2\varepsilon_x<\beta_{\min}\), every threshold satisfying
\[
\varepsilon_x\leq\tau<\beta_{\min}-\varepsilon_x
\]
yields \(\widehat S(\tau)=S^*\). Thresholds below \(\varepsilon_x\) admit false activity, while thresholds at least \(\beta_{\min}-\varepsilon_x\) admit missed activity. If \(2\varepsilon_x\geq\beta_{\min}\), no universally support-correct threshold is certified by this error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activity is stable only when coefficient error is less than half the smallest signal and the threshold lies strictly between inactive-error and active-signal bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Sensitive Activity Regimes

children.title: Unsafe Screening
children.top_down_role: Incorrect feature or group elimination without valid verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A duplicate-feature lasso counterexample to screening rules intended to preserve the complete optimizer set or all potentially active coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The complete minimizer set is \[X^*=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2:x_1\geq0,\ x_2\geq0,\ x_1+x_2=1-\lambda\}.\] Both \((0,1-\lambda)\) and \((1-\lambda,0)\) belong to \(X^*\). Thus observing \(x_1=0\) in the first optimizer does not certify that \(x_1=0\) in every optimizer. A rule that permanently screens feature \(1\) on that basis fails to preserve the complete minimizer set and excludes an optimizer in which feature \(1\) is active. It nevertheless preserves the optimal value in this example because an optimizer with \(x_1=0\) remains feasible; therefore the safety judgment depends on whether screening must preserve one optimizer or all optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With duplicate lasso features, one optimum can set a feature to zero while another activates it. Screening from the first solution alone is unsafe if the goal is to preserve every optimizer or every potentially active coordinate, although it can still preserve the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero coordinate in one selected optimizer does not certify that the coordinate vanishes in every optimizer; screening safety must use the intended quantification over solutions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reducing the duplicated-feature objective to the coefficient sum yields the displayed non-singleton minimizer set
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Path-Knot Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Numerical instability near simultaneous events and nonunique path segments.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Knot Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lasso path degeneracy caused by identical predictors and simultaneous entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\geq1\), the unique minimizer is \(x=(0,0)\). At the knot \(\lambda=1\), both predictor correlations attain the entry threshold simultaneously, although the coefficient solution is still the singleton \(\{(0,0)\}\). For every \(0<\lambda<1\), the complete solution set is \[\{x\in\mathbb R^2:x_1\geq0,\ x_2\geq0,\ x_1+x_2=1-\lambda\}.\] Thus the fitted value \(Xx=1-\lambda\) is unique, but below the knot the coefficient path contains an entire line segment at each \(\lambda\). Different tie-breaking rules, or small perturbations that distinguish the duplicated columns, may select different coefficient allocations and active sets. The simultaneous-entry knot therefore marks the onset of coefficient-path degeneracy despite stable fitted values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical predictors meet the lasso entry threshold simultaneously. The coefficient vector is unique at the knot but becomes nonunique immediately below it, so tie-breaking or small perturbations may select different supports while fitted values remain stable.
assumptions_latex: For \(\lambda\geq0\), let \(X=[1\;1]\), \(y=1\), and minimize \(F_\lambda(x)=\frac12\lVert Xx-y\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert x\rVert_1\) over \(x\in\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The knot at \(\lambda=1\) is a simultaneous-entry event, and for \(0<\lambda<1\) the coefficient path is set-valued; a single-valued continuation therefore requires a tie-breaking rule.
